colour/colour-core-library.title: Colour-core library
colour/colour-core-library.content:
In one sentence: the Prisma/lib/ colour core is the shared, framework-free toolbox of colour-space conversions, two non-interchangeable ΔE definitions, the spline transmission model (build / predict / compose / pair-correct), adjacent-layer collapsing, the filament-registry accessor, and the Camera Transform loader (forward fit, Newton inverse, trilinear LUT) that both the generator and calibration apps build on.

This page documents the modules under Prisma/lib/ that the generator solve path depends on. These are pure helpers — no FastAPI, no disk writes beyond reading JSON/.npz artifacts. If you are wiring a new solve stage, this is the layer you import from. For how these pieces compose into a render, see The Transmission Model and generator.model; for the colour-domain contracts, see Colour domain doctrine.
Related architecture nodes: lib.transmission, lib.color, lib.stack_geometry, lib.filaments, lib.camera_transform.

Two ΔE definitions — not interchangeable
The repo has two distinct colour-difference functions that live in different modules, use different colour spaces, and serve different consumers. Mixing them up is a real trap. (One wiring caveat: the generator’s deltaE_ok path is live, but the lib/color.py compute_dE_from_linear shown here is a dormant copy — the calibration app consumes an identical duplicate; details below.)























FunctionSpaceFormulaSourcedeltaE_ok(lab1, lab2)OKLabEuclidean distance in OKLablib/transmission.py:59compute_dE_from_linear(measured, predicted)CIE Lab (CIE76)Euclidean distance of CIE-Lab tripletslib/color.py:95

deltaE_ok operates on OKLab coordinates produced by linear_to_oklab (lib/transmission.py:40). It is the generator’s perceptual metric — the solver imports linear_to_oklab directly (generator/model.py:22, used at generator/model.py:160) and compares candidates in OKLab. The module docstring’s claim that OKLab is “faster than CIEDE2000” is a design note, not a guarantee — what matters is it is a different space from CIE76.
compute_dE_from_linear converts each linear-RGB triplet to CIE Lab via linear_to_lab (lib/color.py:77, an approximate D65 transform) and returns the plain CIE76 distance (lib/color.py:99). This is the calibration metric in spirit, but watch the wiring: the calibration app imports a byte-for-byte duplicate from calibration/fitting/color_math.py (defined at calibration/fitting/color_math.py:93), not the lib/color.py copy. Its consumers are calibration/server.py:104 (imports from fitting.color_math) and calibration/fitting/composition.py:176 (same). Grep finds no importer of lib/color.py anywhere in the codebase — see the liveness note below.

Practical rule: a “ΔE 3.3” reported by the generator’s OKLab metric and a “ΔE 3.3” from the calibration CIE76 metric are not the same number. Never compare them across the two systems. See Delta E definitions.

OKLab round-trip (lib/transmission.py)

























FunctionWhat it doesSourcelinear_to_oklab(rgb_linear)linear-sRGB (...,3) in [0,1] → OKLab; vectorised over arbitrary leading dims via the _M1/_M2 matriceslib/transmission.py:40oklab_to_linear(lab)OKLab → linear-sRGB; inverts _M2, cubes LMS, inverts _M1, then clips to [0,1]lib/transmission.py:51deltaE_ok(lab1, lab2)scalar Euclidean OKLab distancelib/transmission.py:59
Note the round-trip is not loss-free at the gamut edge: oklab_to_linear clips its output to [0,1] (lib/transmission.py:56), so OKLab values that map outside the unit cube are clamped. The matrices are the standard Björn Ottosson OKLab coefficients hard-coded at lib/transmission.py:27 and :33.
linear_to_oklab is the generator’s entry point into perceptual space — generator/model.py:160 wraps it as to_oklab(...) and casts to float32.

sRGB / linear / Lab helpers (lib/color.py)
These are the scalar, stdlib-only conversions (the module imports only math). They are the calibration-flavoured cousins of the vectorised numpy helpers above.

Liveness: lib/color.py is currently unwired. Grep finds zero importers of this module across Prisma/, the tests, or any caller — production or otherwise. It was created during the 2026-04-03 reorganization as an extraction from unified_calibration/pipeline/color_math.py, but the calibration app never switched to it: it imports a duplicate of these same functions from calibration/fitting/color_math.py instead. So everything below describes a module that is dormant — accurate as a reference, but not on any live path. The behaviours (CIE76 ΔE, log-linear interp_single) are live via that calibration-side duplicate.
















































FunctionDirectionNotesSourcelinear_to_srgb(c)linear [0,1] → sRGB [0,255] intexact sRGB piecewise transfer (0.0031308 / 2.4 gamma)lib/color.py:54linear_to_hex(r,g,b)linear [0,1] → #RRGGBBwraps linear_to_srgblib/color.py:64srgb_to_linear(c)sRGB [0,255] int → linear [0,1]inverse sRGB transferlib/color.py:69linear_to_lab(rgb_linear)linear RGB → CIE Labapproximate D65, sRGB→XYZ matrix + f(t)lib/color.py:77interp_single(knots, values, d)scalar interpolationlinear interp; log-linear extrapolation past the last knot (lib/color.py:20)lib/color.py:12interpolate_pchip(knots, values, d_dense)vector PCHIPfalls back to interp_single when <2 knots or scipy missing (lib/color.py:36, :50)lib/color.py:31
interp_single / interpolate_pchip are the single-value interpolators of the calibration colour pipeline (live via the calibration/fitting/color_math.py duplicate, not this module — see the liveness note above); they are distinct from the three-channel build_spline/predict pair in transmission.py. Note linear_to_srgb here is the exact sRGB transfer with the 2.4 exponent, whereas transmission.to_srgb uses a plain gamma=2.2 power (see below) — two different gamma conventions in the core, used in different places.

Spline transmission model (lib/transmission.py)
This is the heart of The Transmission Model: measured (thickness, T_rgb) knots interpolated with monotone cubic (Pchip), not Beer-Lambert. Composition is multiplicative and order-independent (the corrections term excepted).
Build / predict






























FunctionContractSourcebuild_spline(knots_mm, T_r, T_g, T_b)returns {'r','g','b'} of PchipInterpolator with extrapolate=False; asserts knots_mm[0] == 0.0 (lib/transmission.py:81) and clips T to [0,1]lib/transmission.py:67predict(profile, d)linear-RGB (3,) transmission at thickness d. d<=0 → ones(3); d>d_max → _extrapolate; otherwise clipped spline evallib/transmission.py:89_get_splines(profile)lazily builds and caches splines under profile['_splines']lib/transmission.py:138_extrapolate(profile, spl, d, d_max)Beer-Lambert slope extrapolation from the last two knots when d exceeds the measured rangelib/transmission.py:120

De-facto public despite the underscore. _get_splines and _extrapolate are imported by name across the generator and are part of the real contract, not private internals:

generator/palette/suggest.py:52 (vectorised T sampling)
generator/lut.py:1256 (white-cap profile splines)
generator/pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:60 (the staged backend solve path — see generator.pipeline.staged_runner)

They are duplicated, not shared, in calibration/fitting/fitting.py:153,171 — calibration carries its own copy. Treat the transmission.py pair as the canonical generator-side definitions.

Compose / pair-corrections



































FunctionContractSourcecompose(layers, corrections=None)multiply predict over an ordered [(profile, d), ...] stack; optionally apply a per-pair correction factor C(d_overlay); final clip [0,1]lib/transmission.py:146_interpolate_correction(corr, d)linear interp of C_r/C_g/C_b over the correction’s knots_mm; anchored C=1 at d=0, holds constant past the last knotlib/transmission.py:183to_srgb(T_linear, gamma=2.2)gamma-encode linear transmission (plain pow(1/gamma))lib/transmission.py:196profile_from_dict(d)pre-build splines and return the (mutated) dictlib/transmission.py:203profile_to_save_dict(profile)drop the non-serialisable _splines key for JSON savinglib/transmission.py:209
Pair-correction key format (verify before constructing one): when len(layers) >= 2, compose builds the lookup key from the first layer as overlay and the rest as base (lib/transmission.py:168-179):
pair_key = f"{overlay_fid}|{base1_fid}@{d1:.2f}+{base2_fid}@{d2:.2f}..."

i.e. "overlay|base@0.20" with thicknesses formatted to two decimals. Each profile must carry a filament_id for this to match; absent it, the key uses an empty string and the correction silently no-ops.
compute_pair_corrections lives elsewhere. The compose/build_spline docstrings reference compute_pair_corrections(), but that producer is not in this module — it is defined in calibration/fitting/fitter_core.py (grep-confirmed) and writes data/filaments/pair_corrections.json. The generator only consumes the resulting dict: it loads the JSON (generator/server.py:152,880) and threads it through compose(..., corrections=...) via the solve config (generator/pipeline/runner.py:811, generator/facade.py:689). See Pair corrections.

Adjacent-layer collapsing (lib/stack_geometry.py)
For prediction, a light path through A 0.40 + A 0.20 + W 0.20 sees A 0.60 + W 0.20 — adjacent same-filament runs are one contiguous region, but non-adjacent repeats stay separate because interface order matters.

























FunctionContractSourcecollapse_adjacent_layers(layers, *, precision=5, drop_zero=True)merge adjacent same-filament runs, preserving order; rounds thickness to precision, drops sub-epsilon and (optionally) zero layerslib/stack_geometry.py:31canonicalize_filament_stack(filaments, thicknesses_mm, *, ...)zip parallel lists then collapselib/stack_geometry.py:62unzip_layers(layers)inverse: a layer sequence → parallel (filaments, thicknesses) tupleslib/stack_geometry.py:82
Live in the generator: generator/appearance_model.py:29 imports collapse_adjacent_layers and calls it at appearance_model.py:294 before predicting a stack. Also used calibration-side: calibration/fitting/photo_stack_model/evidence.py:157 (imports at :22/:25) and lib/photo_stack_model/predictor.py:1428 (imports at :23/:25). The example transforms in the docstring (stack_geometry.py:40-41) match the code behaviour.

Note: appearance_model’s appearance-named methods are pass-through after the projection-slot retirement — they return model-domain values, not display values. Collapsing happens regardless; the naming is the stale part, not the geometry. See generator.appearance_model.


Filament registry accessor (lib/filaments.py)
Thin JSON reader over data/filaments/registry.json. No caching — every call re-reads the file.

























FunctionReturnsSourceload_registry(registry_path)the full dict keyed by filament_idlib/filaments.py:9list_filament_ids(registry_path)sorted list of IDslib/filaments.py:15get_filament(registry_path, filament_id){"filament_id": id, **info} or None if absentlib/filaments.py:20
get_filament injects filament_id into the returned dict (lib/filaments.py:26) — convenient, because compose’s pair-correction key needs exactly that field. All three take an explicit registry_path: Path; the module hard-codes no location. See Filament registry.

Camera Transform artifact (lib/camera_transform.py)
The Camera Transform (CT) is the colour bridge between the model domain (predicted transmission RGB) and display sRGB. It has two directions:

Forward F — model RGB → camera-rendered display sRGB. A Finlayson degree-2 root-polynomial matrix (rp_features) followed by monotone PCHIP curves.
Inverse G — display sRGB → model RGB, used for image ingress. Baked once into a 33³ trilinear LUT.

The on-disk schema is camera_transform_v1 carrying a v2 fit model (camera_transform.py:20, :183-187). See Camera Transform and Colour domain doctrine.
Artifact layout, generation-pinning, sha256



































ConstantValueSourceCAMERA_TRANSFORM_JSONcamera_transform.json (fit params)camera_transform.py:21CAMERA_TRANSFORM_LUTinverse_lut_33.npz (baked G)camera_transform.py:22CAMERA_TRANSFORM_MANIFESTmanifest.json (hashes)camera_transform.py:23CAMERA_TRANSFORM_CURRENTCURRENT (generation pointer)camera_transform.py:24N_KNOTS=10, N_W=18, N_PARAMS=48, LUT_SHAPE=(33,33,33,3)model dimscamera_transform.py:26-32
Generation pinning. A CT directory holds dated gen-* subdirs plus a CURRENT file naming one of them. _read_current_generation (camera_transform.py:69) reads CURRENT, and rejects anything that is absolute or not a single local path component (camera_transform.py:80) — a guard against pointer traversal. _resolve_artifact_file (camera_transform.py:88) transparently follows CURRENT when the path is a directory, so callers pass the CT root and get the pinned generation’s file.
SHA-256 integrity. When a generation dir is resolved, _verify_generation_hashes (camera_transform.py:160) loads manifest.json, requires an artifact_hashes map containing both filenames, and recomputes each file’s SHA-256 (_sha256_file, camera_transform.py:139) — raising CameraTransformError on mismatch (:175). Both load_camera_transform and load_inverse_lut run this verification before reading (camera_transform.py:205, :337). Separately, load_camera_transform records the raw JSON bytes’ SHA-256 on the returned CameraTransform.sha256 (camera_transform.py:223) for downstream provenance.
Caching. Both loaders cache by (resolved_path, mtime_ns) and clear the cache on every miss (camera_transform.py:225, :351) — a deliberate single-entry cache, not an unbounded one.
Data-root indirection. _configured_data_root (camera_transform.py:105) reads Prisma/calibration/.data-root; _resolve_data_root_default (:118) re-roots a Prisma/data/... path under that pointer if present. This is how the CT loader finds artifacts when data lives outside the repo.
Validators




















ValidatorChecksSourcevalidate_camera_transform_payload(payload, *, path)dict; schema == "camera_transform_v1"; model_version == "v2"; used_lattice falsy (lattice unsupported, :188); params shape (48,) and finite; n_params/n_knots matchcamera_transform.py:178validate_inverse_lut(lut, *, path)shape (33,33,33,3); all finitecamera_transform.py:325
Both raise CameraTransformError whose message appends the actionable "Rebuild via Calibration -> Camera Transform." (camera_transform.py:34, :136).
Forward F, Newton inverse, trilinear LUT


















































FunctionRoleSourcerp_features(linear_rgb)degree-2 root-polynomial features [r,g,b,√(rg),√(gb),√(rb)]camera_transform.py:244unpack_params(params)split the 48-vector into the (3,6) matrix w and the 3×10 curve knotscamera_transform.py:254_decode_knots(raw)monotone-positive PCHIP knot decode (softplus deltas, capped at OUT_MAX)camera_transform.py:230apply_forward(linear_rgb, params)F: root-poly matrix → clip → per-channel PCHIP curvecamera_transform.py:259invert_curve_channel(y_col, raw)invert one PCHIP curve (swap knot axes)camera_transform.py:273invert_forward(display_srgb, params, *, n_newton=4)G analytic: curve-invert, then Newton iteration on the root-poly residual with a hand-built Jacobiancamera_transform.py:279load_inverse_lut(path)load + validate the baked 33³ LUTcamera_transform.py:333apply_inverse_lut(img_srgb, lut)trilinear interpolation of the LUT over an sRGB image (auto-normalises uint8 → [0,1])camera_transform.py:356
Where each runs — the load-bearing distinction. The generator’s image ingress does not call invert_forward. It loads the pre-baked LUT and trilinearly interpolates it:

generator/model.py:21 imports apply_inverse_lut, load_inverse_lut; calls them at model.py:120 / :125.
generator/model_domain_display.py:28 imports apply_forward, load_camera_transform; applies F at model_domain_display.py:44 (model RGB → display, for previews).

invert_forward (the Newton inverse) is called only at calibration bake time — calibration/fitting/camera_transform/lut.py:17 runs it over the 33³ grid to produce inverse_lut_33.npz. Grep finds no generator caller of invert_forward. So: the generator consumes the trilinear LUT; the Newton solve lives in the calibration bake. Do not expect invert_forward on a hot solve path.

Quick map: who imports what (generator side)








































SymbolGenerator callerAnchorpredict, compose, linear_to_oklab, profile_from_dictgenerator/model.pygenerator/model.py:22_get_splines, _extrapolatepalette/suggest.py, lut.py, pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.pygenerator/palette/suggest.py:52collapse_adjacent_layersgenerator/appearance_model.pygenerator/appearance_model.py:29apply_inverse_lut, load_inverse_lutgenerator/model.py (ingress G)generator/model.py:21apply_forward, load_camera_transformgenerator/model_domain_display.py (forward F preview)generator/model_domain_display.py:28pair_corrections.json (via compose)generator/server.py → pipeline/runner.pygenerator/server.py:152, generator/pipeline/runner.py:811
See also: The Transmission Model, generator.model, generator.pipeline.staged_runner, Colour domain doctrine, Camera Transform, Pair corrections, Filament registry, Delta E definitions.

colour/the-photo-stack-v2-model.title: The photo-stack v2 model
colour/the-photo-stack-v2-model.content:
The photo-stack v2 model

In one sentence: the photo-stack v2 model is the context-aware colour predictor the generator can use instead of the spline model — a calibration fitter writes a self-contained runtime bundle, the generator resolves the latest live bundle, and a multi-stage predictor (plus an optional residual correction layer) turns a physical layer stack into a backlit colour.

This is the model behind the photo_stack_bundle appearance backend. Where the spline model treats a stack’s colour as the product of independent per-filament curves (see The Transmission Model), photo-stack v2 is context-aware: the same blue layer predicts a different colour depending on what is above it, below it, how much white caps it, and which other colours sit alongside it. That context-sensitivity is exactly why it cannot be reduced to per-filament profile JSONs and must enter through the Appearance provider boundary.
If you just want to drive it, read “How to drive it” then skip to “Live vs reference”. If you are the developer who forgot how the backend works, read the whole thing.
How to drive it (for users)
You never call this model directly. You select it through the Appearance provider:

Set appearance_model_provider = "photo_stack_bundle".
Point photo_stack_bundle_path at a live calibration candidate directory (or its runtime_bundle.json). This is mandatory; there is no implicit default for a real solve.
Optionally set use_corrections (the direct-vs-corrected toggle — covered below under “The residual correction layer”).

The model comes from running a calibration fit, not from editing any file by hand. The fitter (Prisma/calibration/fitting/photo_stack_model/) photographs swatch stacks, fits the model, and publishes a candidate; the generator then resolves the newest published candidate automatically when you don’t pin an explicit path.
Producer → artifact → consumer
The model is a hand-off across two apps that share no runtime code:

























RoleWhereWhat it doesProducer (fitter)Prisma/calibration/fitting/photo_stack_model/ (live_fit.py, fit_job.py, write_artifact.py)Fits the model from photographed swatch stacks and publishes a candidate run directory.Artifact (bundle + siblings)Prisma/data/filaments/photo_stack_models/<run_id>/A self-contained, research-independent JSON payload the runtime can load without importing any fitter code.Consumer (generator)generator/appearance_model.py → lib/photo_stack_model/predictor.pyResolves the latest live bundle and scores stacks during a solve.
The package header states the contract plainly: “the bridge between the research fitter and Prisma runtime code: research code may create it, but webapp/runtime code must be able to load it without importing any research package” (lib/photo_stack_model/bundle.py:3).
The candidate directory
A published run is a directory of fixed-named files (ARTIFACT_FILES, lib/photo_stack_model/artifacts.py:18):





























FilePurposeruntime_bundle.jsonThe validated bundle the predictor consumes.model.jsonThe fitted model + manifest-level live-fit flags.correction_layer.jsonThe residual kNN correction artifact (sibling, applied only when corrections are on).metrics.json, fit_log.json, review_summary.json, evidence_summary.json, sample_predictions.jsonDiagnostics / review data.manifest.jsonRun identity: model_family, model_version, run_id, timestamps, fingerprints.
Publishing is atomic: everything is written to a .tmp-<run_id> directory, every required file is validated, and only then is the directory renamed into place and latest.json advanced (write_candidate_artifact, artifacts.py:226–artifacts.py:332). A candidate without a validated runtime bundle is refused outright (artifacts.py:300). After a successful publish, superseded run directories are garbage-collected down to the survivor (_gc_superseded_runs, artifacts.py:178; keep=1, so only the live model survives — without it every ~63 MB run leaked forever, artifacts.py:182).
How the generator resolves “the live candidate”
latest.json is a pointer file holding the survivor run_id (artifacts.py:36, artifacts.py:306). The generator resolves it through latest_live_candidate_dir → latest_live_runtime_bundle_path (artifacts.py:124, artifacts.py:139). The server wraps this in _resolve_photo_stack_candidate_path_for_solve (server.py:959): an explicit photo_stack_bundle_path is validated; otherwise it falls back to latest_live_candidate_dir(_DATA_DIR) (server.py:979). This resolution runs live on every photo-stack solve — confirmed by grep, not assumed: the resolved path flows into the SolveConfig at server.py:1012 and then into the main create_appearance_provider(...) call at runner.py:670; the white-rescale pass also reconstructs the provider via a second create_appearance_provider(...) call (server.py:3803).
Live vs reference
There are two bundles, and the distinction is enforced in code, not just convention.

Live — a freshly fitted candidate carrying live_fit_source_of_truth: true and artifact_role: "live_calibration_fit" (set by the fitter at Prisma/calibration/fitting/photo_stack_model/live_fit.py:408, from LIVE_ARTIFACT_ROLE at live_fit.py:50). This is the only kind a real generator solve will accept.
Reference / replay — the checked-in default at lib/photo_stack_model/bundles/runtime_bundle.json, loaded by load_default_photo_stack_bundle (default_bundle.py:18). It is a point-in-time snapshot for replay/comparison and bootstrapping.

The guard validate_live_runtime_bundle_path (artifacts.py:80) rejects a bundle that is marked replay (live_fit_source_of_truth is False or artifact_role == "point_in_time_reference_replay", artifacts.py:73) or that is not positively marked live (artifacts.py:94); it also checks the candidate’s model.json carries live_fit_bundle_generated: true (artifacts.py:100). validate_live_candidate_dir (artifacts.py:107) additionally requires a valid correction_layer.json schema beside it.
Liveness check on the reference bundle: grep finds load_default_photo_stack_bundle used only in tests and the package README within the product tree — never in the live generator solve path or calibration runtime. So the checked-in default really is reference-only; the live solve always goes through a calibration candidate.
The runtime bundle contract
Before any runtime code trusts a bundle, validate_photo_stack_bundle_payload (bundle.py:125) checks its shape. The version knobs at the top of the bundle:






























FieldValueMeaningschema"prisma_photo_stack_v2_runtime_bundle" (bundle.py:16)Bundle format identity.schema_version1 (bundle.py:17)Bundle format version.runtime_constants_version"photo_stack_v2_2026_06_09" (bundle.py:18)The frozen-constants epoch; a mismatch is rejected (bundle.py:132).fingerprintnon-empty string (bundle.py:137)Identity used in caching / fingerprints.
The bundle’s model object must contain a fixed key set (REQUIRED_MODEL_KEYS, bundle.py:22): the per-channel optical-density curves, the fallback curve, and one parameter block per prediction stage. Each stage block has a required-field contract (REQUIRED_PARAM_FIELDS, bundle.py:40) — e.g. white_context needs white_gamma/white_tau; endpoint_corridor needs ab_weight/l_weight/endpoint_tau/path_mode/… The color pair-correction sub-artifact is optional but, when present, must carry schema "prisma_photo_stack_v2_color_pair_corrections_v1" (bundle.py:192). The bundle also carries a source.prediction_reference_rows block and a verification block (prediction_reference_columns, prediction_reference) used for replay checking (bundle.py:200–bundle.py:212).
There is a separate, code-side version too: PHOTO_STACK_PREDICTOR_LOGIC_VERSION = 4 (predictor.py:34). This is the logic epoch of the predictor itself, distinct from the bundle’s data version. It is folded into the predictor cache key (predictor.py:1374) and the provider fingerprint, so a code-only change to the math invalidates cached solves even when the bundle bytes are unchanged.
How a colour is predicted
The predictor (PhotoStackPredictor, predictor.py:713) is compiled once from a bundle (from_bundle, predictor.py:736) and cached per (path, fingerprint, logic_version) (predictor_for_bundle, predictor.py:1377). Prediction works on rows — one physical stack per row — through predict_rows_rgb (predictor.py:1304). The unit of geometry is a canonical layer group: adjacent same-filament same-role layers are merged, and each group is tagged color, base_white (white below any colour), or cap_white (white above colour) (canonical_layer_groups, predictor.py:137).
Everything starts in per-channel optical density (OD = -log T, od_from_t / t_from_od, predictor.py:292), sampled from the bundle’s per-filament curves with a frozen high-thickness taper (channel_curve_od, predictor.py:309). The stages, in execution order:







































































#StageMethodWhat it adds / does0Latent OD splitlayer_optical_arrays (predictor.py:504)Splits the stack into summed colour OD, white OD, cap OD, base OD, and the first/last ordered colour layers.0White contextwhite_context_od (predictor.py:815)Re-adds attenuated white OD gated by colour strength (white_gamma, white_tau) — white behind colour darkens differently than white alone.0Cap attenuationcap_attenuation_od (predictor.py:824)Extra OD from white on top of colour (the “surface white”), gated by colour strength and selectivity.0Multi-colour interactionmulticolor_interaction_od (predictor.py:993)For ≥2 distinct colours, a directional OD term driven by colour-direction diversity, copresence, and layer order.1(assemble)predict_row_od_parts (predictor.py:1138)Sums latent + white + white-context + cap + interaction OD → base RGB → base OKLab.2Ordered tint retentionordered_tint_retention_lab (predictor.py:1075)Pulls the result back toward lower colour layers’ intrinsic tint that plain summed OD washes out.3Single-colour cap transfersingle_color_cap_transfer_lab (predictor.py:845)For single-colour sandwiches, transfers hue/chroma/lightness from the bare colour through the white cap.4Single-colour profile evidencesingle_color_profile_lab (predictor.py:964)If a measured single-colour sandwich profile matches the context, it is blended in and allowed to dominate.5Endpoint corridorendpoint_corridor_lab (predictor.py:1246)For two-colour stacks, pulls the prediction toward the line between two physically-supported one-colour endpoints.—Colour pair correctioncolor_pair_corrected_rgb (predictor.py:1199)For ordered two-colour / no-white stacks, replaces the result with OD-only × a calibrated per-channel curve.
The stage commentary in predict_rows_rgb (predictor.py:1309–predictor.py:1352) labels these Stages 1–5 inline. A few important wiring details:

Pair correction short-circuits the OKLab stages. If color_pair_corrected_rgb matches (an ordered two-colour, no-white stack with a calibrated pair), the predictor uses OD-only × correction and skips Stages 2–5 entirely (predictor.py:1311–predictor.py:1318), zeroing the suppressed context info (color_pair_suppressed_context_info, predictor.py:1230). The rationale: these pair rows are colour-only evidence excluded from white-stack context calibration (predictor.py:1201 comment).
The OKLab→RGB round-trip only happens if a later stage actually moved the colour — the predictor checks each stage’s reported weight before re-deriving RGB from final_lab (predictor.py:1338–predictor.py:1345), otherwise it keeps the cheap base RGB.
Every stage also emits a bag of *_info scalars (gates, weights, support) that ride along in the output frame for diagnostics.

Evidence classes
Each runtime stack is tagged with an evidence class (_runtime_evidence_class, predictor.py:1396) describing what kind of calibration evidence governs it. This drives both which stages have authority and which rows the correction layer trains on:
white_only, naked_single_filament, color_over_white, multicolor_over_white, single_color_sandwich, cross_color_multilayer_sandwich, and the catch-all unsupported_or_diagnostic (predictor.py:1414–predictor.py:1422).
Transmission-distance and material profiles
Two per-filament side-tables refine the stages:

Transmission-distance (TD) profiles (transmission_distance_profiles) provide per-filament channel weights, an over-layer attenuation scale, and a “tint authority” (how strongly a layer’s intrinsic tint survives under other layers). They are blended by an evidence-confidence factor so an unmeasured filament defaults to neutral behaviour (td_* methods, predictor.py:772–predictor.py:813).
Material profiles (material_profiles) carry each colour’s naked-chroma anchor, hue anchor, and various gates (bright-vivid relief, chroma gate). They are aggregated across a stack’s colours in material_gates_for_ids (predictor.py:475) and feed the cap/white/transfer stages.

The residual correction layer
The bundle prediction is the base model. An optional residual kNN correction sits on top (correction_layer.py), selected by the use_corrections toggle on the Appearance provider.

The fitter builds an all-evidence correction artifact (build_photo_stack_correction_artifact, correction_layer.py:217) carrying training rows: for each calibration sample, the base model’s OKLab residual (photo_oklab − photo_stack_v2, correction_layer.py:171). Only rows whose evidence class is in TRAIN_EVIDENCE are kept (correction_layer.py:25; note unsupported_or_diagnostic is excluded).
At runtime, correction_residuals_for_rows (correction_layer.py:254) looks up training rows in the same context — keyed on (unordered_color_key, white_key, evidence_class) (correction_layer.py:269) — and does a Gaussian-weighted nearest-neighbour average of residuals in a scaled feature space (FEATURE_COLUMNS/FEATURE_SCALES, correction_layer.py:41/correction_layer.py:55). The residual is norm-capped (max_norm) and scaled by a saturating authority that grows with local support (correction_layer.py:293).
apply_photo_stack_correction (correction_layer.py:298) adds the residual to the base OKLab and re-derives RGB, emitting the corrected prediction under the photo_stack_v2_corrected name plus per-row support, authority, and correction_norm columns.

The correction is schema-gated: requesting it when no valid correction_layer.json (schema "prisma_photo_stack_v2_correction") is present raises rather than silently using direct (predict.py:86, mirrored at appearance_model.py:261).
Two prediction shapes: row predictor vs LUT
The same equations are evaluated two ways, and they are kept in sync deliberately:

Row predictor — predictor.py scores one stack per DataFrame row. It is the source of truth for isolated predictions and calibration review, and the fallback for off-grid thicknesses.
Vectorized LUT — generator/photo_stack_lut.py mirrors the frozen equations with NumPy arrays to score the hundreds of thousands of grid-aligned candidate stacks a Joint LUT needs at interactive speed. The provider routes grid-aligned rows to the LUT and everything else to the row predictor (appearance_model.py:533), so callers never lose exactness — only speed. The LUT module imports the predictor’s frozen constants directly (photo_stack_lut.py:26) precisely so the two cannot drift.

The library exposes convenience entry points for one-off stacks too: predict_stack_from_layers (predictor.py:1476), predict_stack_rows_from_layers (predictor.py:1456), and the artifact-level predict_stack (predict.py:65, which applies corrections when present).
How it plugs into a solve
The webapp solve runs the staged backend (run_staged_backend_path, pipeline/staged_runner.py:10310, called from runner.py:846) — not solve.py’s legacy CLI engine. The staged runner branches on state.appearance_provider.model_kind, and when the provider is photo_stack_bundle it is the PhotoStackBundleAppearanceProvider (appearance_model.py:210) wrapping the predictor described here. Everything above is what produces a single backlit colour for one candidate stack inside that loop; see Appearance provider for the boundary contract and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve for how those colours become a LUT and a solved image.

Related: Appearance provider · The Transmission Model · Joint LUT · The Joint LUT and Staged Solve · Model-domain ingress · OKLab · Colour domains
