output/colour-region-geometry-(dormant).title: Colour-region geometry (dormant)
output/colour-region-geometry-(dormant).content:
In one sentence: Prisma/generator/geometry/ turns a solved plan into first-class vector colour-region polygons (ColourRegion/RegionGeometry), and mesh/canonical_mesh.py hashes meshes for order-insensitive equivalence — both are real, tested code with no production caller, so they do not feed STL/3MF output today.

This page exists to stop a reader from assuming these two well-built subsystems are on the live print path. They are not. The export path is documented in Exporting Print Files; what is actually wired end-to-end is catalogued in What Actually Runs. This page is the explicit “wired-but-unused” record for the geometry package and the canonical_mesh oracle.
The geometry package — what it does
Prisma/generator/geometry/ derives connected, same-stack colour regions from a SolvedMaterialPlan and expresses each as an explicit boundary polygon in solved image-domain millimetres.






























SymbolModuleRoleColourRegiongenerator.geometry.regionOne connected same-stack component: exterior ring + hole rings (mm), segment_ids, area_mm2, bbox_mm. frozen dataclass (geometry/region.py:22).RegionGeometrygenerator.geometry.regionContainer of all regions + image-domain dimensions + solve pitch (geometry/region.py:65). Accessors n_regions (geometry/region.py:88) and regions_for_stack (geometry/region.py:91).extract_regions(plan)generator.geometry.extractThe entry point: plan → RegionGeometry (geometry/extract.py:210).simplify_region / simplify_regionsgenerator.geometry.simplifyRamer-Douglas-Peucker contour reduction in mm space (geometry/simplify.py:73, geometry/simplify.py:117).
How extract_regions works (developer view)
extract_regions (geometry/extract.py:210) reads three things off the plan and produces region polygons:

It expands the per-segment stack assignment into a full per-pixel stack-label image by indexing segment_stack_id with segment_id_map (geometry/extract.py:229). Those two arrays are the plan’s identity/assignment split — segment identity is immutable, the stack assignment is the mutable material choice (pipeline/solved_material_plan.py:99, pipeline/solved_material_plan.py:100).
For each distinct stack label it runs scipy.ndimage.label (imported geometry/extract.py:18, called geometry/extract.py:239) so that disconnected patches of the same stack become separate ColourRegions — one connected component per region, never fused.
For each component it traces a rectilinear, pixel-corner-aligned boundary by walking mask edges (_mask_to_grid_polygon, geometry/extract.py:38) and unions them with shapely (geometry/extract.py:143), deliberately avoiding marching-squares half-pixel offsets (rationale stated geometry/extract.py:8). The largest ring becomes the exterior and the rest become holes (_extract_rings, geometry/extract.py:153; exterior-vs-hole selection geometry/extract.py:194).
Coordinates are converted to mm using solver_fine_pitch_mm (geometry/extract.py:227) and emitted Y-down in array convention (geometry/region.py:11 documents the convention; the Y flip back to Y-down is applied in _to_y_down, geometry/extract.py:179).

Provenance survives: each region carries the source segment_ids it covers (geometry/extract.py:247, stored at geometry/extract.py:268).
How simplification works
simplify_regions(geometry, tolerance_mm) is the public sweep (geometry/simplify.py:117); it delegates to simplify_region per region (geometry/simplify.py:73), which RDP-simplifies the exterior and each hole ring via the internal _rdp (geometry/simplify.py:25). Contracts worth knowing:

tolerance_mm <= 0 is an exact identity — the original objects are returned untouched (geometry/simplify.py:128 for the sweep, geometry/simplify.py:84 per region).
Closure is preserved, and a ring that would collapse below 4 vertices is left un-simplified to stay a valid polygon (geometry/simplify.py:67).
It is explicitly not printability cleanup — it only re-represents an already-accepted boundary, it never decides whether a region should exist (stated geometry/simplify.py:11). Printability lives elsewhere; see Exporting Print Files.
bbox_mm and area_mm2 are recomputed from the simplified rings (geometry/simplify.py:93, geometry/simplify.py:103), reusing _signed_area imported back from the extract module (geometry/simplify.py:101).

Liveness: wired-but-unused
The package is internally complete — geometry/__init__.py re-exports ColourRegion, RegionGeometry, extract_regions, and simplify_regions (geometry/__init__.py:13-geometry/__init__.py:15). But a grep for any importer outside the package itself finds none in Prisma/generator/. The only consumer anywhere in the tree is the test suite:

tests/generator/test_phase4_region_extraction.py:16 imports extract_regions, ColourRegion, RegionGeometry and exercises them across ~12 cases (test_phase4_region_extraction.py:62 onward), including an end-to-end run_pipeline → extract_regions case (test_phase4_region_extraction.py:285).

No staged_runner, server, facade, or mesh/export module imports geometry. So despite the package docstring calling these objects the “downstream geometry of record for colour-layer export” (geometry/__init__.py:4), nothing exports through them — that header is aspirational, not a description of the current wiring. Trust the line anchors above, not the prose at the top of the file. This matches the audit note in Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract and the dormancy entry in What Actually Runs.


                  
                  Do not confuse with the live export geometry 
                  
                

The STL/3MF that OrcaSlicer opens is built by the mesh/export path described in Exporting Print Files, driven from the staged backend (The staged backend (Stage 0-5)). The shapely.geometry imports in mesh/rectilinear_interval.py and mesh/printability.py are unrelated to this geometry package — same word, different code. The historical plans that wanted region geometry to become the export authority (e.g. the 2026-04-11 “geometry-native printability” sketches) were never wired in.


Status — geometry package: WIRED-BUT-UNUSED (test-covered, no production caller). Confirmed by grep over Prisma/generator excluding the package and the test that imports it.
canonical_mesh — a test/verification equivalence oracle
mesh/canonical_mesh.py answers one question: “are these two meshes the same shape, ignoring face order, vertex order within a face, and vertex renumbering?” It is a verification helper, not part of building geometry.

























FunctionAnchorBehaviourcanonical_triangle_arraymesh/canonical_mesh.py:43Quantise each triangle (XY at mesh pitch, Z at layer height — _quantize_triangles, mesh/canonical_mesh.py:30), sort the 3 vertices within each triangle (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:67), then sort triangles lexicographically (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:72).canonical_mesh_hashmesh/canonical_mesh.py:76SHA-256 over that array, domain-separated by the quanta and face count (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:101-mesh/canonical_mesh.py:108). Accepts (vertices, faces) arrays or a trimesh.Trimesh (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:87).canonical_mesh_equalmesh/canonical_mesh.py:112True iff two (vertices, faces) meshes hash equal.
The criterion is spelled out at mesh/canonical_mesh.py:10-mesh/canonical_mesh.py:19: intentionally insensitive to face/vertex ordering and index renaming, while still catching any real geometric difference. It exists so an emitter rewrite that reorders faces can be proven output-preserving even when byte-identical STL is no longer available (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:6).
Liveness: suspected inert on the live path
Grep across the whole tree finds these symbols referenced only in: this file, the Architecture node generator.mesh.canonical_mesh, two docs/mesh_printability/ plan/validation write-ups, the doc agent’s knowledge files, and exactly one runnable caller — scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py:23 imports canonical_mesh_hash and calls it at scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py:123 to fingerprint exported objects in a benchmark. No Prisma/generator/ source path calls it on a live export, and (unlike the geometry package) no test in tests/ imports it — a grep for canonical_mesh under tests/ returns nothing.
Status — canonical_mesh: SUSPECTED INERT on the live path. Its sole non-doc caller is the standalone benchmark script scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py; it was the equivalence oracle for the white-cap vectorised-emitter work (docs/mesh_printability/validation/white_cap_step3_vectorised_emitter_2026-04-20.md) and survives as a reusable check, not as a runtime gate.
If you want to revive either

To put region geometry on the export path you would add a caller that takes state.solved_plan (The pipeline orchestrator and shared state), runs extract_regions, optionally simplify_regions, and feeds the polygons to an emitter — none of that wiring exists today.
To use canonical_mesh as a CI gate, import canonical_mesh_hash/canonical_mesh_equal in a test and assert two emitter variants agree; the benchmark script (scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py) shows the call shape.

See also

What Actually Runs — the master live/dormant ledger
Exporting Print Files — the geometry that actually produces STL/3MF
Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract — the plan these regions are derived from
generator.geometry.extract · generator.geometry.region · generator.geometry.simplify · generator.mesh.canonical_mesh — Architecture nodes
generator.pipeline.solved_material_plan — the upstream plan contract

output/fixed-budget-layer-scheduling-(ex.title: Fixed-budget layer scheduling (experimental)
output/fixed-budget-layer-scheduling-(ex.content:
In one sentence: the scheduling/ package is a deterministic research harness that quantizes an already-solved material plan into per-layer filament/white assignments and scores competing ordering policies, but it is wired only into one offline eval script and its tests — nothing in the live solve or export path calls it.

This page is the status note for the fixed-budget layer scheduler. It exists to answer two questions a future reader will have: does the print I export actually use this? (no), and what does it compute if I run it by hand? (per-layer schedules plus setup/tiny-presence metrics). The aliasing target [[Layer scheduling]] resolves here.
Liveness: NOT in the live solve/export path
The package lives at Prisma/generator/scheduling/ with three implementation modules plus a re-export shim:

























FileRolescheduling/model.pydataclasses + quantization, derives cases from a SolvedMaterialPlanscheduling/policies.pysix deterministic ordering policies + a registryscheduling/metrics.pybudget/reserve checks + setup-change / tiny-presence costsscheduling/__init__.pyre-exports everything, adds build_schedule_case / evaluate_policy convenience entry points
Grepping the whole tree for importers of the package, the only non-package, non-test caller is one offline script: scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py. That script’s own header states it does not export STL / 3MF geometry and does not mutate repo-tracked configuration or pipeline state (scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py:7-8).
Confirmed by grep — these live entry points contain zero references to scheduling, LayerSchedule, setup_beam_search, etc.:








































SubjectStatusEvidenceLive webapp serverdoes not call schedulingno matches in Prisma/generator/server.pyStaged backend (the real solve engine)does not call schedulingno matches in pipeline/staged_runner.pySolve facade / CLI enginedoes not call schedulingno matches in facade.py, runner.py, solve.pySolveStatementions scheduling only in a commentpipeline/state.py:256 (“consumed by export, triage, and scheduling”) — no import, no callOffline eval scriptonly runtime callerscripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py:106-111, :1556Test suiteimports the packagetests/generator/test_layer_scheduling.py:8 (12 test functions)
The state.py:256 comment is aspirational wording, not a wiring. The schedule outputs are never meshed: the live mesh/export path is documented in From solve to mesh the export pipeline and the staged backend in The staged backend (Stage 0-5); neither touches this package.

Disambiguation: the experimental setup_beam_search_policy / layer_sparse_greedy_policy here are unrelated to the live grouping code ([[generator.grouping.beam_search]] / [[generator.grouping.greedy_optimize]]) that The Solve Facade actually wires. There are two unrelated beam-search and two unrelated greedy implementations in the tree.

What “fixed-budget” means
The scheduler never decides how much of each filament a region gets — the solve already committed that. It only decides layer order within a fixed material budget. A budget is committed material thickness; quantization turns thickness into an integer layer count via round(thickness_mm / layer_height_mm), rejecting any non-zero thickness whose reconstruction error exceeds a 1e-6 mm tolerance (scheduling/model.py:65-73, tolerance QUANTIZATION_TOLERANCE_MM at :34). White is tokenized as WHITE_LAYER_TOKEN = "__white__" (scheduling/model.py:35); in an absolute schedule, white is represented as None (scheduling/model.py:195-196).
Deriving a case from a solved plan
derive_fixed_budget_schedule_case(plan, ordering, layer_height_mm, d_wc_min_mm, ...) (scheduling/model.py:375) reads an immutable SolvedMaterialPlan (generator.pipeline.solved_material_plan) and produces a FixedBudgetScheduleCase. Steps:

Quantize each stack’s colour budgets into ordering-stable positive (filament_id, count) tuples (scheduling/model.py:407-422 calling _ordered_positive_colour_layers at :77). Any stack filament with positive thickness that is missing from ordering raises (scheduling/model.py:411-415).
Quantize the per-pixel cap-height map into integer white-cap layer counts (scheduling/model.py:424-433).
Label each pixel by stack via committed_stack_label_map(plan) (scheduling/model.py:435, defined in generator.pipeline.derived_views at derived_views.py:33), and build a total_layers_map = stack_total_layers[labels] + cap_levels (scheduling/model.py:440).
Derive an anisotropic white surface reserve from cliff geometry (see below) and take the elementwise max against the flat d_wc_min-derived reserve (scheduling/model.py:441-448).
Group identical (stack_index, cap_layers, effective_reserve, sidewall_reserve, sidewall_band) pixels into unique signatures with their pixel counts and area_mm2 (scheduling/model.py:450-490).

If top_white_reserved_layers is not given, it defaults to ceil(d_wc_min_mm / layer_height) (scheduling/model.py:393-394) — i.e. the minimum white cap implied by the solve’s d_wc_min. min_printable_line_width_mm defaults to the plan’s solver_fine_pitch_mm (scheduling/model.py:397-401), and the sidewall band width in pixels is ceil(line_width / fine_pitch) clamped to ≥1 (scheduling/model.py:402-405).
derive_unique_layer_budget_signatures(...) (scheduling/model.py:505) is the thin wrapper returning just the signatures tuple.
The anisotropic sidewall reserve
derive_anisotropic_white_surface_reserve(total_layers, band_width_px=...) (scheduling/model.py:355) returns (reserve_layers, sidewall_band_mask). It finds, per pixel, the local positive height drop to its lower 4-neighbours (_internal_cliff_drop_layers, :317), then propagates that reserve inward only across the high side of a cliff for band_width_px - 1 steps (_propagate_sidewall_reserve, :329). The intent: a tall region adjacent to a short one exposes a vertical wall that needs a white shell, and that reserve should not spill onto the lower face. This is the only geometry-aware part of the model; everything else is pure integer bookkeeping.
The signature dataclass (the unit of work)
LayerBudgetSignature (scheduling/model.py:94) is a frozen dataclass holding one committed (stack, cap) combination:









































FieldMeaningstack_indexwhich committed colour stack (:107)orderingthe global filament order tuple (:108)colour_layers((fid, count), ...), all counts > 0 (:109)white_layersquantized white-cap layer count (:110)top_white_reserved_layerscontiguous white run the schedule must keep on top (:111)base_top_white_reserved_layersthe flat d_wc_min-derived component (:112)sidewall_white_reserved_layersthe cliff-derived component (:113)sidewall_bandwhether this signature sits in a sidewall band (:114)
__post_init__ enforces non-negativity, ordering membership, no duplicate filaments, positive counts, and that the effective top-white reserve covers both the base and sidewall reserves (scheduling/model.py:116-158). Convenience: total_colour_layers (:165), total_layers (:169), full_layer_budget_map() which adds the __white__ token (:185).
A LayerSchedule (scheduling/model.py:191) pairs a signature with absolute_layers — a bottom→top tuple of filament-id-or-None, plus the policy_name that produced it (:199-201).
The six policies
All policies take a FixedBudgetScheduleCase and return one LayerSchedule per entry. They are deterministic and bounded. The registry is POLICY_REGISTRY (scheduling/policies.py:640); get_policy_registry() returns a copy (:650).








































Policy nameFunctionBehaviourbaseline_top_white_only:470Control: fixed global ordering, all white on top (_fallback_schedule, :43).white_envelope:484Same colour order, but bury surplus white below the colour block, keep only the reserved run on top (_white_envelope_schedule, :79).absorber_strength_global_order:491Re-order colours strongest-absorber-first, then fixed top-white (absorber_strength_order, :108).layer_sparse_greedy:514Greedy case-level scheduler: pick one area-weighted-preferred filament per absolute layer; signatures take it when they can, else white, with a repair pass that re-fills white slots to preserve totals exactly (:603-625).setup_beam_search:344Bounded beam search (width _DEFAULT_BEAM_WIDTH = 12, :28) over per-layer family templates, ranked by (setup_cost, active_count, tiny_penalty, prefix_len) (_BeamState.rank_key, :70). Falls back to baseline if the beam empties (:422-423).setup_beam_guarded:445Runs beam search and baseline, evaluates both, and keeps the beam result only if it strictly beats baseline on (setup_change_cost, total active, tiny_penalty, transition_cost) (_report_rank_key, :436; comparison :465-467).
absorber_strength_order (scheduling/policies.py:108) ranks filaments by 1 - mean(predict_transmission(profile, layer_height)) — i.e. how much a single layer of that filament darkens — loading profiles via the shared model.load_profile / predict_transmission (generator.model, imported policies.py:20), with an lru_cache on per-filament strength (:93-105).
Every policy enforces the white-on-top reserve by appending exactly min(white_layers, top_white_reserved_layers) None layers at the top (_top_white_layers_used, scheduling/policies.py:31).
The metrics
metrics.py scores a (case, schedules) pair. The headline costs:



































MetricFunctionWhat it countsBudget preservationbudget_preserved (metrics.py:81) / budget_preservation_deltas (:49)Whether observed layer counts exactly match the signature’s full_layer_budget_map(); deltas list any mismatch. A correct schedule has zero deltas.Top-white reserve OKtop_white_reserve_ok (metrics.py:89)Whether the schedule’s own top reserve layers are all white (:100).Setup-change costsetup_change_cost (metrics.py:218)Minimum family-change cost with carry-over loaded state across adjacent layers — a tiny DP over which family is “loaded” after each layer (:231-248). Start family defaults to white.Adjacent-layer transition costadjacent_layer_filament_set_transition_cost (metrics.py:206)Symmetric-difference size of the active non-white filament set between neighbouring layers (:213-214).Tiny-presence penaltytiny_presence_penalty (metrics.py:251)For each family/layer whose total area is below min_area_mm2 (default 1.0, :255), adds threshold - area (:262-266).
Area is aggregated per absolute layer either including white (family_area_by_absolute_layer_mm2, :103) or excluding it (filament_area_by_absolute_layer_mm2, :134 — note: white is deliberately dropped here because the metric tracks chromatic activity, :140-142). Setup/tiny costs use the white-inclusive aggregation; “active filament” counts use the white-exclusive one.
evaluate_case_schedules(case, schedules, ...) (metrics.py:270) bundles all of the above into a frozen ScheduleEvaluation (scheduling/model.py:285), aligning schedules to entries by signature first (_align_schedules, metrics.py:22). The tiny-presence threshold here defaults to 1.0 mm² (metrics.py:275).
Driving it by hand
There is no UI and no CLI flag. Two ways to exercise it:
1. Package convenience API (scheduling/__init__.py):

build_schedule_case(payload) (:68) — dispatches to a synthetic fixture (build_swap_pressure_case / build_synthetic_equal_budget_case) or, given a solve_result carrying a solved_plan, calls derive_fixed_budget_schedule_case (:91-103).
evaluate_policy(case, policy_name) (:117) — runs one named policy and returns a flat dict of costs (setup_change_cost, active_count, tiny_presence_penalty, top_white_penalty, budget_ok, the schedules, etc., :124-145). Policy-name aliases map short names to canonical ones (POLICY_NAME_ALIASES, :54).

2. The offline eval script (scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py):
python scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py --out-dir <dir> \
    --cases synthetic_swap steve cafe \
    --policies baseline white_envelope absorber_strength_order \
               layer_sparse_greedy setup_beam_search setup_beam_guarded

It performs a real bounded solve per case (solve_full, :441) under a fixed recommended_v2 posture (dual_resolution_v2 + greedy grouping, :68-73), builds a scheduling case through a defensive adapter (SchedulerAdapter, :181; module discovery _load_scheduler_adapter, :482), evaluates every policy, and writes report.md + summary.json plus per-case stack_strips.png / layer_activity.png visuals (:1612-1616, _write_case_visuals :1492). It picks a “winner” with a weighted chooser whose weights (setup_change_cost 40, active_count 25, tiny_presence_penalty 20, top_white_penalty 10, printability_proxy 5) live in CHOOSER_COMPONENTS (:98-104) — note these chooser weights are the script’s, not the package’s. The adapter tries module names ("scheduling", "layer_scheduling", "schedule_evaluation", "evaluation.scheduling") (:106-111); only scheduling exists, so the others are dead fallbacks.
The synthetic fixtures build_swap_pressure_case (scheduling/model.py:589) and build_synthetic_equal_budget_case (:526) are also the basis of much of the test suite (tests/generator/test_layer_scheduling.py, 12 tests).
Stale-header warnings

The module docstrings are accurate here, but the package-status framing in scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py:12-15 (“expected to land separately from this runner”) and the adapter’s import-failure message (scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py:578-579, “once the new scheduling package lands”) are stale — the package has landed; the adapter’s multi-name probing is now vestigial.
The pipeline/state.py:256 comment listing scheduling as a plan consumer overstates reality: no live code path consumes scheduling output.

See also

Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract — the plan this scheduler reads

The staged backend (Stage 0-5) — the real solve engine
The Solve Facade — disambiguates the live grouping beam-search/greedy from these experimental ones
generator.scheduling.model · generator.scheduling.policies · generator.scheduling.metrics
generator.pipeline.derived_views · generator.pipeline.solved_material_plan · generator.model

output/from-solve-to-mesh-the-export-pip.filePath: Output/From solve to mesh the export pipeline.md
output/from-solve-to-mesh-the-export-pip.title: From solve to mesh the export pipeline
output/from-solve-to-mesh-the-export-pip.content:
From solve to mesh the export pipeline

In one sentence: export_solve_bundle reads a materialized solve bundle off disk, decides whether to print the exact solved raster or a smoother field-derived white cap, builds one watertight mesh object per material into a single ExportMeshBundle, and serializes it as per-object STL files or one packed 3MF — writing an export_manifest.json that records every object’s geometry, material, and mesh quality.

This page is the backend mechanics of export. For the user-facing webapp flow (HTTP routes, polling, AMS swap plan) read Exporting Print Files; this page follows what happens inside the one entry point that page calls. The whole contract lives in generator.mesh.post_solve_export and is deliberately free of any FastAPI/UI dependency — geometry is built before serialization, and format writers only serialize already-built meshes (mesh/export_mesh_bundle.py:1).
The boundary: MeshObject and ExportMeshBundle
Everything funnels through two frozen dataclasses in generator.mesh.export_mesh_bundle. They are the export boundary: mesh generation happens before them, format writers only consume them.
A MeshObject (export_mesh_bundle.py:16) is one positioned mesh in the shared coordinate frame. It carries raw vertices/faces arrays plus four identity strings — object_key, material_key, role, mesh_style — an optional 4×4 transform, and free-form metadata. It is built from a trimesh via MeshObject.from_trimesh (export_mesh_bundle.py:29), which copies vertices as float64 and faces as int64. to_trimesh (export_mesh_bundle.py:55) reconstructs a trimesh.Trimesh with process=False and applies the stored transform lazily, so the transform is only baked at serialization time.





























MeshObject fieldMeaningobject_keyUnique handle; also the STL filename stem and a thickness-map lookup keymaterial_keyWhich filament the object prints in (drives 3MF extruder slot)roleSemantic tag (white_base, color, combined_white_cap, white_cap_slab, …) used for display namesmesh_styleHow it was built (flat_plate, rectilinear_interval, primitive_frame, hybrid styles)transformOptional 4×4; None until a border shift or hybrid placement applies one
An ExportMeshBundle (export_mesh_bundle.py:73) holds the tuple of MeshObjects plus the export-wide metadata: image_domain_width_mm/height_mm, layer_height_mm, xy_quantum_mm, the object_coordinate_frame string, a mesh_build_report, a per-object quality map, color_export_details, and source_blueprint_fingerprint. The frame string is the constant OBJECT_COORDINATE_FRAME = "x-left-to-right_y-bottom-to-top_z-build-plate-mm" (post_solve_export.py:51). object_by_key (export_mesh_bundle.py:90) is a linear lookup over the tuple.
Note the bundle is immutable: every transformation (_with_mesh_build_report at post_solve_export.py:1131, _with_export_border at post_solve_export.py:1178) constructs a new ExportMeshBundle rather than mutating one.
The nine-stage pipeline
export_solve_bundle (post_solve_export.py:2120) is the integration entry point. The webapp calls it from _perform_export_files (server.py:5432, at the call site server.py:5503); the heavy-benchmark harness and the export tests call the same function. It walks a fixed nine-stage progress sequence, DEFAULT_EXPORT_STAGES (post_solve_export.py:187), emitting an ExportProgressEvent per stage and timing each scope with an ExportTimingCollector (post_solve_export.py:155).























































#Stage idWhat happens in export_solve_bundle1load_bundleResolve the bundle dir, load arrays.npz and the JSON sidecars (post_solve_export.py:2157)2detect_solve_modeDetect standard vs luminance; pull pitch / layer height / base thickness / border from metadata (post_solve_export.py:2165)3prepare_material_mapsCopy color maps, build the RectilinearExportConfig (post_solve_export.py:2228)4build_geometry_sourceBranch on exact-raster vs field-derived (post_solve_export.py:2244)5build_color_base_meshesWhite base flat plate + one z-slab object per color filament6build_white_cap_meshesExact white cap (with topology fallbacks) or hybrid field cap7serialize_outputsWrite per-object STLs (3MF packing is done by the caller afterward)8validate_meshesOptional reload-and-recheck of written STLs9write_manifestBuild and write export_manifest.json
Stage 1 — Load the bundle
_resolve_solve_bundle_dir (post_solve_export.py:1912) accepts either an arrays.npz file, the directory containing it, or a parent that holds exactly one such directory; it raises FileNotFoundError if it cannot find a unique one. _load_bundle_arrays (post_solve_export.py:1928) loads arrays.npz with allow_pickle=False. Three JSON sidecars are read with _load_json_file (post_solve_export.py:1902): stageA_field_bundle_summary.json (the summary), prediction_replay_metadata.json (the replay, which names the color filament ids), and run metadata via _bundle_run_metadata (post_solve_export.py:1936, preferring run_template.json then run.json). The webapp writes all of these in _materialize_post_solve_export_bundle_from_cached_solve before calling export — the replay block records color_thickness_filament_ids (server.py:4569).
Stage 2 — Detect the solve mode
detect_solve_mode_from_metadata (post_solve_export.py:253) returns a SolveMode enum — STANDARD or LUMINANCE (post_solve_export.py:62). Solve mode is not a user export toggle; it is detected. The preferred signal is a luminance_mode key found anywhere in run/bundle config or resolved_settings/solve_start_diagnostics (post_solve_export.py:283). The fallback for old bundles is array-key presence: if white_cap_visible_surface_mask or luminance_detail_field is present it is luminance, else standard (post_solve_export.py:289). This stage also reads pitch, layer height, white-base thickness, and border settings via _first_config_float (post_solve_export.py:1952) / _first_config_bool (post_solve_export.py:1978), which search a priority chain of metadata containers. If border is disabled, both border dimensions are forced to zero (post_solve_export.py:2224).
Stage 3 — Prepare material maps (now a near no-op)
_bundle_color_maps (post_solve_export.py:2020) unpacks the (F, H, W) color_thickness_maps array into a {filament_id: 2D map} dict keyed by the replay’s color_thickness_filament_ids, raising if the count mismatches (post_solve_export.py:2034). A RectilinearExportConfig (post_solve_export.py:200) is assembled from the resolved dimensions; its export_policy() (post_solve_export.py:219) produces a GeometryExportPolicy (generator.mesh.geometry_policy, geometry_policy.py:96) carrying the canonical printability pitch.
The separate module prepare_export_material_maps (generator.mesh.material_maps, material_maps.py:9) is the historical “prepare material maps” step but is now intentionally a near no-op: it returns shallow copies of the maps and ordering unchanged (material_maps.py:19). Its docstring confirms it previously promoted a solve-only translucent-underfill placeholder into a real filament map, but that feature was removed (material_maps.py:14). Liveness: this function is still wired — the webapp calls it through _prepare_export_materialization (server.py:835 → server.py:841), which runs before the bundle is materialized, not inside export_solve_bundle. So in the webapp path the maps are prepared (copied) once on the server side and the in-bundle “prepare_material_maps” stage just rebuilds the config. The two are distinct steps that happen to share a stage name.
Stage 4 — Choose the geometry source
GeometrySource (post_solve_export.py:55) is the one genuinely user-visible export choice: FIELD_DERIVED or EXACT_RASTER, normalized by normalize_geometry_source (post_solve_export.py:233). The branch is at post_solve_export.py:2245.

Exact raster loads the combined white-cap thickness map from the bundle via _bundle_white_cap_map (post_solve_export.py:2044) and calls build_exact_raster_mesh_bundle (post_solve_export.py:1407).
Field derived obtains a reconstructed white-cap height field — supplied as an array, loaded from a path, or reconstructed on the fly by reconstruct_field_white_cap_from_arrays (generator.mesh.field_white_reconstruction) (post_solve_export.py:2272). It validates the field is an integer uniform upscale of the solve grid (post_solve_export.py:2292), derives field_scale, builds a finer-pitch RectilinearExportConfig and a HybridWhiteCapConfig, and calls build_field_derived_mesh_bundle_mixed_resolution (post_solve_export.py:2315).

Stages 5–6 — Build the geometry
Both geometry sources share _base_and_color_objects (post_solve_export.py:1291) for the base and color stacks:

The white base is a single flat plate via generate_flat_plate (post_solve_export.py:1304), object key __white_base__ (post_solve_export.py:43), role white_base, style flat_plate.
Each color filament is meshed as a rectilinear interval body that floats on the accumulating floor (the running sum of layers below it) via _mesh_rectilinear_interval (post_solve_export.py:465, delegating to generator.mesh.rectilinear_interval mesh_interval_map). Color order follows the ordering, skipping any __-prefixed keys (post_solve_export.py:1318).
If a color body fails the strict reload-quality check, it is rebuilt defensively — first as a same-material topology quarantine (_build_color_quarantine_parts, post_solve_export.py:1102), and if that still fails as constant-Z slab bodies (_build_color_z_slab_parts, post_solve_export.py:985). This exists because a clean single-body mesh can become non-manifold after STL vertex welding; splitting at snapped plateaus keeps geometry exact while avoiding reload pinches (post_solve_export.py:996).

The white cap differs by source:

Exact raster (build_exact_raster_mesh_bundle, post_solve_export.py:1407) meshes the combined cap as one rectilinear interval (post_solve_export.py:1434). If it passes strict quality it ships as a single combined_white_cap object (post_solve_export.py:1461). If not, it falls through a cascade: forced slabs (_build_exact_white_cap_slabs, post_solve_export.py:499), then a topology quarantine (_build_white_cap_quarantine_parts, post_solve_export.py:774), then a recursive adaptive Z-partition that splits only failing Z ranges (_build_exact_white_cap_adaptive_parts, post_solve_export.py:595). Each branch records its selected_strategy.
Field derived (build_field_derived_mesh_bundle_mixed_resolution, post_solve_export.py:1634) keeps color stacks and base on the exact solve grid, nearest-upsamples only the combined color-top witness map to the field resolution (post_solve_export.py:1721), then builds a hybrid guard/freeform white cap via build_hybrid_white_cap_meshes (generator.mesh.hybrid_white_cap) (post_solve_export.py:1722). It asserts the color/field/hybrid configs agree on solve pitch, layer height, and base thickness (post_solve_export.py:1681).

Both builders finish through _bundle_from_objects (post_solve_export.py:1771), which stamps the mesh_build_report with geometry source, detected solve mode, geometry policy, and per-object vertex/face totals, then optionally wraps the bundle with a printable border frame via _with_export_border (post_solve_export.py:1178). When a border is enabled, the content objects are translated inward by the border width and a __border__ frame object (post_solve_export.py:50) is appended, printed in the white-cap material (post_solve_export.py:1247).
Stage 7 — Serialize per-object STL (3MF is the caller’s job)
If write_stls is true, export_solve_bundle imports and calls write_export_mesh_bundle_as_stls (generator.mesh.export_serializers, export_serializers.py:87) into an stls/ subdirectory (post_solve_export.py:2344). That writer skips empty objects, maps each object_key to a filename via _object_filename (export_serializers.py:17), and bakes the transform by exporting obj.to_trimesh(copy_arrays=False) (export_serializers.py:102). It returns {object_key: Path}.
The 3MF path is not inside export_solve_bundle. When the user picks 3MF the webapp passes output_format == "3mf", so export_solve_bundle is called with write_stls=False (server.py:5508) and the caller packs the in-memory result.bundle with write_export_mesh_bundle_as_3mf (export_serializers.py:189) afterward (server.py:5546). That writer builds one OPC-packaged zip: a [Content_Types].xml, a _rels/.rels, and 3D/3dmodel.model (export_serializers.py:222). Each object becomes a <object> with a slic3rpe:extruder slot (export_serializers.py:131) and an identity-transform <build> item; transforms are baked into vertices before writing (export_serializers.py:126). The extruder slot per object comes from filament_assignments — the webapp builds these by assigning one slot per distinct filament id via _filament_assignments_for_export (server.py:4611), and human-readable names via _material_display_names_for_export (server.py:4594), passed at server.py:5551–5552. Liveness: both STL and 3MF writers are live — STL via export_solve_bundle, 3MF via the webapp 3MF branch and the dedicated test tests/generator/test_export_3mf_filename.py.
Stage 8 — Validate quality
Mesh quality is computed at build time per object with check_mesh_quality (generator.mesh.quality, quality.py:20), which reports watertightness, open edges, pinch edges (counts != 2), and winding consistency. The export uses two stricter local gates: _quality_passes (post_solve_export.py:328, requires watertight + zero open + zero pinch) and _strict_processed_quality (post_solve_export.py:336), which re-welds the mesh with process=True and counts non-2-valence edges — emulating what a slicer-reload would see. Stage 8 itself is optional reload validation: only if validate_written_meshes is true does it re-load every written STL from disk through _reload_quality_for_path (post_solve_export.py:2096) and record reload_quality (post_solve_export.py:2352); otherwise it is disabled by default (post_solve_export.py:2361). In the webapp this is driven by payload.validate_written_meshes (server.py:5509).
Stage 9 — Write the manifest
build_export_manifest (post_solve_export.py:1820) assembles the JSON-serializable manifest (schema post-solve-export-manifest-v1, post_solve_export.py:1841). Its status is "ready" unless any object’s quality shows open edges, pinch edges, or non-watertightness, in which case "mesh_quality_failed" (post_solve_export.py:1844). It records the content/export footprint, border, grid, geometry policy, a per-object list (with STL paths if written), the full quality map, and the mesh_build_report. _jsonable (post_solve_export.py:294) coerces enums, numpy scalars/arrays, and Paths. write_export_manifest (post_solve_export.py:1895) writes it pretty-printed and sorted to export_manifest.json. The performance timings dict (ExportTimingCollector.as_dict, post_solve_export.py:179) is attached before writing (post_solve_export.py:2393).
What you get back
export_solve_bundle returns a PostSolveBundleExportResult (post_solve_export.py:73): the in-memory bundle, the manifest dict and its written manifest_path, the output_paths map ({object_key: Path} for written STLs), the tuple of progress_events, and reload_quality. The webapp reuses result.bundle directly to pack the 3MF, so the meshes are never re-read from disk for that format.
Progress and timing plumbing
ExportProgressReporter (post_solve_export.py:114) emits an ExportProgressEvent (post_solve_export.py:89) per stage; the webapp adapts these to its polling shape in _progress_dict_from_export_event (server.py:5410), turning stage index + fraction into an overall percentage. ExportTimingCollector.scope (post_solve_export.py:163) is a context manager that records wall-clock per labeled stage for performance audits, surfaced under manifest["performance"].
Related

Exporting Print Files — the user-facing webapp driver (routes, polling, AMS swaps)

generator.mesh.export_mesh_bundle — the MeshObject / ExportMeshBundle boundary
generator.mesh.export_serializers — STL and 3MF writers
generator.mesh.material_maps — the now near-no-op map prep
generator.mesh.rectilinear_interval — the robust interval-map mesher
generator.mesh.hybrid_white_cap — field-derived guard/freeform cap
generator.mesh.quality — mesh quality summary used by the manifest

output/robust-rectilinear-meshing.title: Robust rectilinear meshing
output/robust-rectilinear-meshing.content:
Robust rectilinear meshing

In one sentence: the generator turns each filament’s grid-aligned thickness map into a closed, slicer-safe triangle shell by walking every column’s vertical material intervals, assigning corner vertices to local occupied 2x2x2 sectors so the solid can touch itself at a point or edge without welding into a non-manifold blob, then merging flat faces, splitting bad fans, stitching open edges, separating coincident vertices, and filling residual holes — with a per-material fallback ladder (single body → topology-quarantine → Z-slab / adaptive-Z) that escalates only when a body fails the strict watertight check.

This page covers the geometry engine in generator/mesh/. It serves two readers: the user who just wants STLs that slice cleanly, and the developer who needs to know exactly how the shell is built and why a body sometimes splits into extra parts.
Where this runs (liveness)
The webapp’s export endpoint (server.py:5503, export_solve_bundle(...)) is the live entry point. server.py imports it at server.py:91. export_solve_bundle (mesh/post_solve_export.py:2120) loads the solve bundle, detects the solve mode, and dispatches on geometry source (mesh/post_solve_export.py:2245):




















Geometry sourceBuilderWhite capEXACT_RASTERbuild_exact_raster_mesh_bundle (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1407)rectilinear interval map of the combined cap, with the fallback ladderFIELD_DERIVEDbuild_field_derived_mesh_bundle_from_maps (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1528)hybrid: rigid rectilinear guard + freeform surface
Both builders call the same color-stack mesher (_base_and_color_objects, mesh/post_solve_export.py:1291), which is reused by the field path at mesh/post_solve_export.py:1577. The field path additionally reconstructs the cap thickness map from solve fields (reconstruct_field_white_cap_from_arrays, mesh/post_solve_export.py:2272) and meshes it with build_hybrid_white_cap_meshes (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1592).
All seven source modules named below are reachable from this one entry point — confirmed by import-and-call grep, not by module headers (which are stale: several still frame the code as “future webapp wiring” or a “sandbox” trial even though the webapp path is live).
The core mesher: mesh_interval_map
mesh_interval_map (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:778) is the workhorse. It takes a floor map and a thickness map (both H×W, in mm) plus the XY pitch_mm, and returns one closed single-material trimesh.Trimesh plus a RectilinearMeshStats audit record (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:34). Every color layer, the exact-raster cap, and the hybrid rigid guard go through it.
1. Z levels and per-slab occupancy
A column is “active” when its thickness exceeds eps (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:813). The set of distinct floor-and-top heights across all active columns becomes the global Z level array (_global_z_levels, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:122) — so every height where any column starts or stops material is a shared cutting plane. Each gap between consecutive Z levels is a “slab”; _occupancy_by_slab (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:131) marks, per column, which slabs are filled, using searchsorted on the column’s floor and top. The result present is an H×W×K boolean occupancy grid.
Optional z_snap_decimals rounds floor/top to a fixed decimal grid before level extraction (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:802), with top clamped >= floor so rounding can’t invert an interval (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:807). The export config defaults to z_snap_decimals = 6 (mesh/post_solve_export.py:212); the hybrid config defaults to 6 as well (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:47). Snapping makes adjacent layers share exact plane heights so their walls coincide instead of leaving a sub-micron crack.
2. Exposed faces
_neighbor_masks (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:163) shifts present in all six directions. A face is emitted wherever a filled cell has an empty neighbor: present & ~neighbors[dir] for east/west/north/south/top/bottom (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:844). _append_quads (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:186) turns each exposed cell-face into a quad, recording four corner grid indices (row, col, z) plus a 3-bit local code identifying which of the eight surrounding cells owns that corner. Corner winding order deliberately mirrors the legacy per-pixel emitter (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:209).
3. The 2x2x2 sector trick (the heart of it)
This is the mechanism that keeps a self-touching solid closed instead of pinched. Around every grid corner there are eight surrounding cells, forming a 2x2x2 neighborhood. _corner_patterns (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:149) packs the 8 occupancy bits of that neighborhood into one 8-bit code per corner (stored in a uint16 array, but only the low byte is ever set, so the lookup tables are sized 256). SECTOR_LOOKUP (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:114, built by _sector_lookup, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:80) is a 256×8 table that, for each of the 256 patterns, runs a connected-component flood over the occupied corners (6-connected adjacency, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:91) and labels which sector each occupied cell belongs to.
When two material regions of the same filament meet only at a corner point or along a single edge, the 2x2x2 pattern has two disconnected occupied components, so that corner gets two distinct sector labels. Each face vertex is keyed by (row, col, z, sector) (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:916), so the two regions get separate vertices at the same coordinate instead of one shared vertex. That prevents a single point/edge from being incident to too many faces — the classic non-manifold pinch that slicers reject. SECTOR_COMPONENT_COUNT (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:115) precomputes how many sectors each pattern splits into; _split_count (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:455) sums the “extra” sectors across the whole grid for the diagonal_or_corner_splits stat.
4. Vertex assembly
Quad corners are encoded into a single integer key (((row·(W+1)+col)·K + z)·8 + sector) (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:916), uniquified, and split into two triangles per quad (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:925). The key is decoded back into (x, y, z) world coordinates by reversing the packing (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:935), with y flipped to image-up orientation (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:943). The mesh is built process=False (no auto-weld) and only duplicate/degenerate faces are dropped (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:949).
5. Horizontal-face merge (optional, default on)
With merge_horizontal_faces=True (config default mesh/post_solve_export.py:211), top and bottom faces are not emitted as per-cell quads; only the four side directions are (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:863). Instead, _append_horizontal_merged_faces (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:409) treats each slab’s top/bottom mask as a region to be triangulated as a whole, drastically reducing triangle count on flat plateaus.
Per connected component (ndi.label with 4-connectivity, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:329), _component_ring_groups (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:250) traces the exact pixel-corner boundary rings with trace_mask_grid_rings (mesh/grid_rings.py:9) rather than Shapely booleans — deliberately, so long collinear boundary runs are kept and the merged face shares exact edge vertices with the unmerged side-wall quads (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:255). Rings are grouped into [outer, holes...] by signed area (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:263) and point-in-polygon containment (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:273). The polygon is triangulated by shapely.constrained_delaunay_triangles (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:357), falling back to mapbox_earcut if that raises (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:362). Every triangle vertex is re-mapped back to its occupied 2x2x2 sector via _component_vertex_key (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:279) so merged faces use the same sector-keyed vertices as the walls. flip controls bottom-vs-top winding (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:398).
trace_mask_grid_rings itself (mesh/grid_rings.py:9) walks boundary half-edges with a left-turn rule (mesh/grid_rings.py:38) to produce oriented loops; _trace_mask_grid_rings is an alias (mesh/grid_rings.py:86).
The cleanup pipeline (post-construction, in order)
After the raw shell exists, mesh_interval_map runs a fixed sequence (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:957–991):















































StepFunctionWhat it doesAnchorOverfull fan split_split_overfull_edge_fansonly on the merged path: splits the face fan at any edge used by >2 faces, cloning the shared vertex per connected fan group (union-find over incident faces)mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:559, called :958Open-edge stitch_stitch_duplicate_open_edgeswelds geometrically-coincident open (count-1) edge pairs left by sector splitting, via union-find on vertex coords rounded to 9 decimalsmesh/rectilinear_interval.py:652, called :961Re-split (merged)_split_overfull_edge_fanssecond fan split after stitching, merged path onlymesh/rectilinear_interval.py:963Separate duplicates_separate_duplicate_verticesnudges topologically-distinct coincident vertices apart by a sub-micron XY offsetmesh/rectilinear_interval.py:722, called :965Hole fill (≤2 passes)trimesh.repair.fill_holesfills any remaining count-1 edges, then re-runs fan-split + separation on added facesmesh/rectilinear_interval.py:972–989Fix normalstrimesh.repair.fix_normalsconsistent outward winding (fix_normals defaults True)mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:990
The unmerged quad path skips the first fan split entirely (fan_splits = 0, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:960) because sector-keyed quads can leave duplicate open edges but cannot create an over-full edge — see the inline rationale at mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:951. Merged horizontal triangulation can produce unpredictable fans, so the splitter is kept for it.
Why separate, don’t weld
_separate_duplicate_vertices (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:722) exists because STL does not preserve vertex identity — a slicer re-welds any two vertices at the same coordinate on import, which would undo the sector split and recreate the pinch. So at already-split contacts it shifts each duplicated vertex by offset_mm along the in-plane direction toward its incident-face centroid (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:767), introducing a tiny XY-only geometric gap (Z is never touched) without changing topology. Default offset is 0.001 mm (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:787, config mesh/post_solve_export.py:213). The hybrid module carries its own identical copy of this routine (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:519).
The hole-fill loop only triggers when count-1 (open) edges remain (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:974) and stops early if a pass adds no faces (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:979); newly-added fill faces get the same fan-split + separation treatment (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:984).
Mesh quality gates
check_mesh_quality (mesh/quality.py:20) is the product quality summary: it counts per-edge face references (edge_face_counts, mesh/quality.py:8), reports n_open_edges (count == 1) and n_pinch_edges (non-2 minus open) plus is_watertight. A mesh passes when watertight with zero open and zero pinch edges (_quality_passes, mesh/post_solve_export.py:328).
Because the exported (separated) mesh must survive a slicer’s reload-weld, there is a stricter second gate. _strict_processed_quality (mesh/post_solve_export.py:336) rebuilds the mesh with trimesh process=True — which does weld coincident vertices, simulating the slicer — and re-checks edges. _strict_processed_quality_passes (mesh/post_solve_export.py:362) requires watertight with zero strict-non-2 and zero open edges. A body is only accepted as-is when it passes both gates (color: mesh/post_solve_export.py:1343 via _color_mesh_quality_passes at :1098; white cap: mesh/post_solve_export.py:1454). Passing the loose gate but failing the strict one is the signal that “this will pinch after import” — and that triggers the fallback ladder.
The white-cap fallback ladder
When a single-body interval mesh fails the strict gate, the orchestrator escalates by splitting the body into multiple same-material parts that each survive welding. The escalation differs between the white cap and color layers.
White cap (exact-raster path), build_exact_raster_mesh_bundle
The decision is at mesh/post_solve_export.py:1454:

Single interval — if force_exact_white_cap_slabs is off and both gates pass, ship the one body (selected_strategy = "single_interval", mesh/post_solve_export.py:1459).
Forced slabs — if force_exact_white_cap_slabs is on (config default False, mesh/post_solve_export.py:214), skip straight to constant-Z slabs via _build_exact_white_cap_slabs (mesh/post_solve_export.py:499, dispatched :1471). Each gap between snapped Z levels becomes one flat-bottomed slab body.
Topology quarantine — otherwise, _build_white_cap_quarantine_parts (mesh/post_solve_export.py:774). This cleaves only the risky columns into a second same-material body, leaving the rest intact. If that yields a ready result, ship it (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1494).
Adaptive-Z partition — if quarantine still fails, _build_exact_white_cap_adaptive_parts (mesh/post_solve_export.py:595, dispatched :1500).

Topology quarantine, _build_interval_topology_quarantine_parts
The shared quarantine engine (mesh/post_solve_export.py:807) first asks topology_risk_column_mask (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:485) which solve-grid columns sit adjacent to a multi-sector corner (a SECTOR_COMPONENT_COUNT > 1 vertex touching an occupied slab, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:530–541). With no risk columns it reports no_risk_columns and bails (mesh/post_solve_export.py:834). Otherwise it tries six partitions of those risk columns — row_even/odd, col_even/odd, checker_even/odd (mesh/post_solve_export.py:847) — meshing the “main” body (risk cells removed) and the “quarantine” body (only risk cells) separately (mesh/post_solve_export.py:866). It accepts the first partition where both bodies pass both gates (mesh/post_solve_export.py:963); status is "ready" only if no part failed (mesh/post_solve_export.py:967). The idea: separating the touching cells into a different body means their welded-together vertices belong to different shells, so the pinch never forms.
Adaptive-Z partition, _build_exact_white_cap_adaptive_parts
This recursively bisects the Z range (build_range, mesh/post_solve_export.py:651). It clips the cap to [z0, z1] with _clipped_interval_map (mesh/post_solve_export.py:571), meshes it, and if it passes both gates accepts it as one part (mesh/post_solve_export.py:689). If it fails and spans more than one Z level, it splits at the midpoint and recurses (mesh/post_solve_export.py:751). A single-level range that still fails is shipped anyway tagged white_cap_slab_failed (mesh/post_solve_export.py:743) — the strategy emits everything and records leaf failures rather than aborting the export.
Color layers, _base_and_color_objects
Color materials use a slightly different ladder (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1346):

Single body if both gates pass (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1343).
Else topology quarantine via _build_color_quarantine_parts (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1102); shipped if status == "ready" (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1356).
Else Z-slab fallback via _build_color_z_slab_parts (mesh/post_solve_export.py:985) — one same-material body per snapped material plateau (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1021).

The white base plate is never an interval mesh; it is a single make_box plate (generate_flat_plate, mesh/primitives.py:50; called mesh/post_solve_export.py:1304).
The hybrid white cap (field-derived path)
build_hybrid_white_cap_meshes (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:621) builds the cap as two same-filament bodies so the layer-exact region near the color stacks stays rigid while the rest follows the smooth field surface:

Rigid guard — a rectilinear interval body (mesh_interval_map again, mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:651) that exactly caps the color columns and laterally shields them out to guard_width_mm. Its intervals come from derive_hybrid_white_cap_intervals (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:150): guard floor sits on the color top (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:194), and the lateral guard domain is the air ring within guard_width_mm of color (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:176) raised to the neighboring color top (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:187).
Freeform surface — mesh_freeform_cap_surface (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:402) builds a continuous top+bottom skin over the optically-free region. Per active cell it emits two top triangles and two bottom triangles (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:473) plus boundary walls (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:480). It has its own 2x2x2-style diagonal handling: at a checkerboard contact (NW+SE occupied, NE+SW empty, or the mirror) it assigns the shared corner a sector bit so the two diagonal cells get distinct vertices (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:432, :439), counted as diagonal_corner_splits. Corner heights are averaged from incident cells (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:450), then the surface is separated + hole-filled like the rigid path (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:503).

validate_hybrid_white_cap_intervals (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:298) sweeps layers and checks the guard+free union never removes reference-white coverage and never leaves color exposed; guard_coverage_status is "pass" only when zero exposed-color and zero removed pixels (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:391). The result’s status property (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:116) returns mesh_quality_failed if any cap body has open/pinch edges, else coverage_review if coverage didn’t pass, else ready.
Field reconstruction (upstream of the hybrid mesh)
reconstruct_field_white_cap_from_arrays (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:254) converts solve-bundle scalar fields into the cap thickness map the hybrid mesher consumes. It picks a target upper surface per solve mode (_target_upper_surface, mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:229: luminance uses white_cap_total_thickness_map; standard uses a boundary field plus optional detail, mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:163), upsamples to a finer grid by field_scale (default 4, mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:32), then collapses layer-by-layer into integer layer counts (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:299). Each layer’s white mask is cleaned by _cleanup_white_mask (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:92): tiny internal air voids are filled and tiny positive features removed, with thresholds from GeometryPrintabilityPolicy (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:268). It stops before mesh construction by design (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:5).
Printability policy
Thresholds are resolved once into GeometryPrintabilityPolicy (mesh/geometry_policy.py:21). The solve-grid pitch is the hard minimum positive width — a 0.2 mm grid means 0.2 mm minimum feature (mesh/geometry_policy.py:23). Derived defaults: lateral guard width defaults to that min width (mesh/geometry_policy.py:47), max internal empty-hole area defaults to 0.5·width² (mesh/geometry_policy.py:54), min positive feature area to width² (mesh/geometry_policy.py:64). GeometryExportPolicy (mesh/geometry_policy.py:95) bundles pitch/layer-height/white-base and enforces that any supplied printability policy agrees on the solve pitch (mesh/geometry_policy.py:120). These policy objects do not read UI state — callers resolve settings first and pass resolved numbers in (mesh/geometry_policy.py:1).
The audit record
Every interval mesh emits RectilinearMeshStats (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:34), serialized via as_dict (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:56) into the export manifest’s per-object stats. Useful fields when debugging a non-manifold report: diagonal_or_corner_splits (sector splits), nonmanifold_edge_fan_splits, duplicate_open_edge_stitches, separated_duplicate_vertices, filled_hole_faces, and the three topology_risk_* preflight counts (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:466). The fallback reports also carry single_interval_quality / single_interval_strict_processed_quality so you can see why the single body was rejected before the ladder kicked in.

printability/blueprint-triage-the-unwire.title: Blueprint triage the unwired engine
printability/blueprint-triage-the-unwire.content:
In one sentence: pipeline/blueprint_triage/ is a complete, tested printability-analysis engine — seven defect detectors, a CLEAN/WARNINGS/DISQUALIFYING verdict, and a fix planner with counterfactual-dE costing — that the live solve never calls (the state slot it would fill is hard-wired to None), so today it runs only under its own test corpus.

Blueprint triage: the unwired engine
This page documents the blueprint_triage package at design-intent altitude. It is not an exhaustive API reference for every helper, because the whole subsystem is computed-but-unwired: no live solve or export path constructs an AnalysisContext or calls analyze_triage. Read it to understand what was built and how it was meant to work, and as a map for anyone considering wiring it in.
Liveness up front — this is dormant, test-only
The state slot that would hold a triage report is PipelineState.blueprint_triage, declared Optional["PrintabilityReport"] = None at pipeline/state.py:275. Its full lifecycle in the live path:






























SiteWhat happensAnchorDeclaredblueprint_triage: Optional["PrintabilityReport"] = Nonepipeline/state.py:275Written (live)Stage-5 bridge of the staged backend sets state.blueprint_triage = None — never a real reportpipeline/runner.py:555Read (live)Facade passes it straight through: blueprint_triage=getattr(state, "blueprint_triage", None)facade.py:890Asserted dormantA real run_pipeline test asserts state.blueprint_triage is None after solvingtests/generator/blueprint_triage/test_runner_invocation.py:31
The engine’s three public entry points — analyze_triage, plan_fixes, apply_fixes — have zero callers outside the package and its tests. A repo-wide grep for those symbols excluding blueprint_triage/** returns only one legacy-audit markdown doc (Prisma/generator/docs/legacy_audit/07_COMPATIBILITY_MAPS_AND_EXPERIMENTAL_BRIDGE.md), never production code. The only generator-code reference to the package at all (outside state.py/runner.py/facade.py above) is server.py:94, which imports only PrintabilityError — see the disambiguation trap below; that import is unrelated to the triage engine’s verdict path.
The detectors, planner, and costing are nonetheless substantially tested: ~30 test modules under tests/generator/blueprint_triage/ plus four sibling suites (blueprint_triage_cliff, blueprint_triage_gate, blueprint_triage_line_width, blueprint_triage_sub_feature). So the code is exercised and presumed correct in isolation — it is simply not invoked by the product.

Calling it “Lane A/D” etc.: the source carries internal lane labels (e.g. application.py:42 references “Lane D”; planning.py:459 references “D.3”). These are development-phase tags, not user-facing concepts.

How it would work (the intended flow)
SolvedMaterialPlan + ExposureContext
        │
        ▼
AnalysisContext.from_state(...)          fields.py:130
        │
        ▼
analyze_triage(plan, context)            api.py:18
        │   runs 7 detectors → classifies → builds verdict
        ▼
PrintabilityReport (verdict + hazards + summary + fingerprints)   report.py:179
        │
        ├── plan_fixes(report)           planning.py:25   → ranked FixCandidate list
        │       (counterfactual_cost per candidate)        costing.py:15
        ▼
apply_fixes(plan, candidates, state=...) application.py:19   → mutated plan + cache invalidation

AnalysisContext — the precomputed input bundle
AnalysisContext (fields.py:109) is the immutable bundle every detector reads. The classmethod AnalysisContext.from_state(state, *, exposure) (fields.py:130) builds it from a solved pipeline state; it requires state.solved_plan and raises ValueError otherwise (fields.py:137). What it precomputes:


















































FieldBuilt byMeaningcolour_ceiling_mapcolour_ceiling_from_plan (cap_quality.py:58), called at fields.py:146per-pixel top of coloured material (white base + colour stack)top_surface_maptop_surface_from_fields (cap_quality.py:70), called at fields.py:147colour ceiling + white-cap heightinterval_schedule_build_interval_schedule (fields.py:222)per-pixel ordered MaterialInterval column: white base → colours (palette order) → white capper_filament_masks_build_per_filament_masks (fields.py:283)boolean occupancy per filament id; white base omitted (everywhere by construction), __white_cap__ added where cap > 0salience_build_salience_fields (fields.py:314)Sobel luminance/chroma gradients on the solve-grid OKLab targetfidelity_prior_build_fidelity_prior (fields.py:361)residual proxy = __de__ raster scaled by normalized salienceconfigTriageConfig (config.py:21)triage-owned thresholds + ranking weightscolour_profiles / wb_profile / wc_profile_resolve_profiles (fields.py:204)forward-model spline profiles, needed only for counterfactual prediction
The interval schedule is the spine of the structural detectors. Each pixel column is a list of MaterialInterval(z_start_mm, z_end_mm, material_id) (fields.py:20), starting with MaterialInterval(0.0, d_wb, "__white_base__") (fields.py:254) and ending with a "__white_cap__" interval from the colour ceiling to ceiling+cap (fields.py:264).
ExposureContext (fields.py:46) carries edge-exemption data: an exempt_outer_perimeter flag and an optional exempt_edge_mask of shape (H, W, 4) in direction order (up, down, left, right) (fields.py:54). ExposureContext.from_export_bundle (fields.py:93) derives the inset border-exemption mask from a print’s border width — this is the one piece a test exercises directly (tests/generator/blueprint_triage_gate/test_orchestration_gate.py:20).
The seven detectors
analyze_triage (api.py:18) runs seven detectors and assembles a PrintabilityReport. Detectors split across detect/general.py (structural column invariants), detect/features.py (xy footprint geometry), and detect/cliffs.py (colour-step exposure). All return lists of Hazard dataclasses (report.py:33).





























































#DetectorSourceWhat it flagsDefault severity1Voiddetect_voids (detect/general.py:15)a pixel column with no schedule (MissingColumnHazard, general.py:22) or a positive-z gap between stacked intervals (general.py:33)always DISQUALIFYING2Floatingdetect_floating (detect/general.py:48)column starts above z=0 unsupported (general.py:56), or an interval doesn’t abut material below it (general.py:69)always DISQUALIFYING3Overlapdetect_overlaps (detect/general.py:86)non-finite / negative-thickness interval (general.py:92), or adjacent intervals overlapping in z (general.py:109)always DISQUALIFYING4Sub-featuredetect_sub_features (detect/features.py:29)xy connected component below min printable area/width, per material per z-layer, deduped by (material_id, bbox)graded — see below5Narrow stranddetect_narrow_strands (detect/features.py:107)skeletonized footprint segments thinner than the soft line-width thresholdgraded — see below6Cliffdetect_cliffs (detect/cliffs.py:20)a colour step where one pixel’s colour ceiling is exposed to air above a shorter 4-neighbour (cliffs.py:188)graded by exposure depth in analyze_triage7Skyscraperidentify_skyscrapers (detect/cliffs.py:38)isolated tall thin plateau among cliff high-sides (prominence + isolation gated)structural metadata only
The structural trio (void/floating/overlap) walk context.interval_schedule.intervals directly and treat any breach as a hard invariant violation — they always emit Verdict.DISQUALIFYING. The column epsilon is max(1e-6, layer_height_mm * 0.01) (general.py:127).
Graded severities (sub-feature, narrow strand, cliff)
The footprint detectors classify against hard/soft thresholds in TriageConfig:

Sub-feature (_sub_feature_severity, detect/features.py:196): DISQUALIFYING below hard_min_feature_area_mm2 or hard_min_feature_width_mm; WARNINGS below the soft_* equivalents; otherwise None (no hazard).
Narrow strand (_strand_severity, detect/features.py:214): DISQUALIFYING below hard_min_line_width_mm; WARNINGS below soft_min_line_width_mm. Uses skimage.morphology.skeletonize (features.py:124) and an EDT-derived local width.
Cliff: detectors emit raw CliffRegions; severity is decided in analyze_triage itself by comparing region.max_exposure_depth_mm against cliff_block_depth_mm / cliff_warn_depth_mm (api.py:42, api.py:50), wrapping each into a CliffHazard (report.py:130).

Skyscrapers and salience
identify_skyscrapers (detect/cliffs.py:38) clusters cliff high-side pixels into cap-floor-coherent components (_cluster_high_side_pixels, cliffs.py:372), then gates each on footprint area, width, prominence (skyscraper_prominence_mm) and isolation score (skyscraper_isolation_threshold) — cliffs.py:90–cliffs.py:98. Survivors get a blended feature_salience_score mixing the cliff salience, local feature support (score_noise_vs_feature, cliffs.py:136), prominence, and target-vs-ring contrast, with an isolation penalty (cliffs.py:108–cliffs.py:115). Crucially, skyscrapers are not a verdict input — analyze_triage never adds them to blocking_hazards or warnings; they only inform fix planning.
Salience itself is image-driven: _build_salience_fields (fields.py:314) takes Sobel derivatives of the solve-grid OKLab target (fields.py:334), with chroma being the gradient norm over the (a,b) channels (fields.py:344) and combined = hypot(luminance, chroma) (fields.py:351).
The verdict
analyze_triage aggregates into a PrintabilityReport (report.py:179). The verdict logic (api.py:67–api.py:71):
blocking_hazards = voids + floating + overlaps
                 + DISQUALIFYING sub-features + DISQUALIFYING narrow-strands + blocking cliffs
warnings         = WARNINGS sub-features + WARNINGS narrow-strands + warning cliffs

verdict = DISQUALIFYING if blocking_hazards
          else WARNINGS if warnings
          else CLEAN

Verdict is the three-value enum CLEAN / WARNINGS / DISQUALIFYING (report.py:12). The report also carries a ReportSummary of per-category counts (report.py:166), plus a plan_fingerprint and context_fingerprint (api.py:94, api.py:95) so a verdict can be checked for staleness against a (plan, exposure) pair. That check is the job of ValidatedBlueprintToken (report.py:199): from_report snapshots the fingerprints + verdict + summary, and is_valid_for(plan, context_fingerprint) re-hashes the plan and compares (report.py:214). No live code constructs or consumes such a token today.
Fix planning, costing, and application
If the verdict is not clean, the engine can propose and cost repairs. None of this runs in production; it is the most elaborate dormant part.
Fix types
FixType (report.py:18) enumerates ACCEPT, SHORTEN, WALL, SMOOTH, HYBRID, TRANSLUCENT_SMOOTH, TRANSLUCENT_HYBRID, BULLDOZE. Of these, only a subset is actually implemented end-to-end:





















































FixTypeGenerated in plan_fixes?Applied in apply_fixes?Simulated in costing?ACCEPTyes (every hazard)no-op (application.py:27)n/aSHORTENyes_apply_shorten (application.py:84)yes (costing.py:86)WALLcliff only_apply_wall (application.py:103)yes (costing.py:95)SMOOTHcliff only_apply_smooth (application.py:111)yes (costing.py:99)HYBRIDcliff only_apply_hybrid (application.py:146)yes (costing.py:107)BULLDOZEskyscraper onlyrouted through _apply_shorten (application.py:29)yes (costing.py:86)TRANSLUCENT_*never generatedNotImplementedError (“see Lane D”, application.py:41)NotImplementedError (costing.py:137)
plan_fixes — candidate generation and ranking
plan_fixes(report, policy=None) (planning.py:25) iterates cliff / skyscraper / sub-feature / narrow-strand hazards (planning.py:33–planning.py:36), generates candidates per hazard via _generate_candidates (planning.py:77), and scores them in two passes:

Heuristic pass — _heuristic_scores (planning.py:343) fills a FixScoreBreakdown (report.py:146) from cheap proxies: material cost (pixel area), a per-FixType workflow_cost table (planning.py:376), a shape_cost table keyed on feature salience (planning.py:383), and a printability_gain (planning.py:425).
Counterfactual pass — for the top-N viable candidates per hazard (counterfactual_top_n_per_hazard, default 3, planning.py:40), it replaces the heuristic image_cost with the true counterfactual_cost (planning.py:57) and re-finalizes the composite (planning.py:64).

The composite score (_composite, planning.py:414) is a weighted sum:
image·w_image + material·w_material + shape·w_shape + workflow·w_workflow − printability_gain·w_gain, with weights from TriageConfig. Candidates are then ranked (planning.py:66), and a phase-2 refinement (_apply_phase2_refinement, planning.py:600) folds the cheapest realized fix cost back into each region’s feature_salience_score.
counterfactual_cost — the dE penalty of a fix
counterfactual_cost (costing.py:15) answers “how much does this fix hurt the image match on the pixels it touches?” It:

simulates the fix on a copy of the plan (_simulate_fix, costing.py:67),
runs the forward model on just the affected pixels (_predict_oklab_for_pixels, costing.py:196, via predict_transmission + to_oklab from generator.model),
compares the modified per-pixel dE against the baseline dE (__de__ raster or recomputed baseline, costing.py:47),
returns the mean positive increase in dE — an improvement scores 0 (costing.py:40).

This is the only part of the engine that needs the forward-model profiles on the context; if they are missing it raises ValueError (costing.py:205).
apply_fixes — mutation and cache invalidation
apply_fixes(plan, candidates, *, state=None) (application.py:19) first asserts the batch’s target masks don’t overlap (_assert_non_overlapping, application.py:69), then dispatches each candidate to its _apply_* mutator. When a state is passed it invalidates derived caches (invalidate_triage_cache, application.py:12 — sets state.blueprint_triage = None and state.plan_derived_cache = None) and rebuilds state.thickness_maps via compatibility_thickness_maps (application.py:48), preserving any __de__ / __gamut_mask__ diagnostics (application.py:60). The shared SMOOTH/HYBRID geometry builder is build_smooth_target_cap_height_map (application.py:182), a linear distance-falloff cap raise reused by both planning.py and costing.py.
TriageConfig — the knobs
TriageConfig (config.py:21) holds only triage-owned thresholds and ranking weights; physical printer constraints stay on PipelineConfig. TriageConfig.from_pipeline_config (config.py:53) derives them: the hard floors come from the printer’s minimum extrusion width (config.py:55), while the soft (warning) band uses the nozzle-derived feature scale _FEATURE_WIDTHS_PER_NOZZLE * nozzle_diameter from generator.preprocessing.feature_scale (config.py:68). Cliff depths key off layer height: cliff_warn_depth_mm = layer_height, cliff_block_depth_mm = max(2·layer_height, layer_height) (config.py:73).
Two PrintabilityError, two PrintabilityReport (trap)
There are two unrelated PrintabilityError and PrintabilityReport symbols in the generator — do not conflate them:




















SymbolThis page’s moduleThe other, unrelated onePrintabilityReportblueprint_triage/report.py:180 (verdict + hazards)mesh/printability.py mesh-export classification (build_printability_report, mesh/printability.py:1071)PrintabilityErrorblueprint_triage/report.py:29reused by the mesh-exposure gate
The single live raise of blueprint_triage’s PrintabilityError is not in the triage engine at all: server.py:94 imports it, and _assert_material_exposure_safe_for_product (server.py:2445) raises it when a non-fixed white-cap solve exposes coloured filament. Even that gate is flagged suspected-inert / test-only by an in-code note (server.py:2438) — during a live solve only the non-raising audit runs. Likewise, mesh/printability.py:1061 carries an explicit warning that its export classification is suspected inert and that its PrintabilityError/PrintabilityReport must not be confused with this module’s. See Printability three layers for how these distinct printability mechanisms relate.
