printability/printability-three-layers.title: Printability three layers
printability/printability-three-layers.content:
Printability three layers

In one sentence: the generator has three separate “printability” subsystems at three abstraction levels — a per-pixel-column triage (blueprint_triage, test-only/dormant), a per-layer staged diagnostic + Stage 4 gate (staged_printability, the one that actually runs on every web solve), and a mesh-level measurement roll-up (mesh/printability.py, suspected inert) — and only the middle one is on the live path.

This is the orientation page for everything named “printability” in the generator. The name is overloaded: three unrelated modules share it, two of them define their own PrintabilityReport class, and most module docstrings are stale. Before trusting any liveness claim, read the master liveness map in What Actually Runs — this page links there rather than re-deriving each verdict, and adds the per-module physical detail the map omits.
The three subsystems differ in what they look at and whether they run:

































LevelModuleLooks atOutputStatusPer-pixel columngenerator.pipeline.blueprint_triage.apiMaterial intervals in each pixel column (voids, floats, overlaps, cliffs)A triage PrintabilityReport + fix candidatesDORMANT — test-only, never written on the live pathPer-layer stagedgenerator.pipeline.staged_printabilityConnected components inside each color/cap/detail layerA BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic report and an in-place Stage 4 repair gateLIVE — runs on every web solveMesh measurementgenerator.mesh.printabilityBuilt trimesh.Trimesh geometry (footprint, seals, thin islands)A different PrintabilityReport + export verdict ladderSUSPECTED INERT — only tests/scripts call the roll-up
Level 1 — per-pixel column triage (blueprint_triage) — dormant
pipeline/blueprint_triage/ walks the solved plan one pixel column at a time. Each column is a stack of MaterialIntervals, and the detectors flag structural hazards by inspecting those intervals: an empty column raises a MissingColumnHazard (“Pixel column has no material schedule.”, pipeline/blueprint_triage/detect/general.py:24), a positive-z gap inside a column is a VoidHazard (detect/general.py:37), and adjacent intervals that overlap become an OverlapHazard (detect/general.py:114). analyze_triage (pipeline/blueprint_triage/api.py:18) runs all detectors — voids, floating, overlaps, sub-features, narrow strands, cliffs, skyscrapers — and assembles them into a Verdict of CLEAN / WARNINGS / DISQUALIFYING (api.py:67-71) inside the triage PrintabilityReport (pipeline/blueprint_triage/report.py:180). A separate plan_fixes (pipeline/blueprint_triage/planning.py:25) proposes FixCandidates and apply_fixes (pipeline/blueprint_triage/application.py:19) mutates the plan.
It looks like a full repair pipeline, but nothing on the live solve invokes it. analyze_triage, plan_fixes, and apply_fixes have only test callers (tests/generator/blueprint_triage*); the sole non-test references to those three functions inside Prisma/generator are their own package re-exports (pipeline/blueprint_triage/__init__.py:1, :2, :17) — no production code calls them. (Other symbols from the module are imported on the live path — server.py:94, facade.py:36, and state.py:14 pull in PrintabilityError/PrintabilityReport — but only as a type or exception class, never the analyzer/fixer functions.) The runner clears the carrier field: _finalize_staged_backend_state sets state.blueprint_triage = None (runner.py:555 per What Actually Runs) and the staged path never writes a real report there. So the field threads through the facade and is read by the server, but always reads None. See What Actually Runs > blueprint_triage (printability triage) — dormant, and not the mesh report.

Its PrintabilityError is a different gate. blueprint_triage/report.py:29 defines PrintabilityError and the server imports it (server.py:94). The one place that raises it on a solve-shaped path is _assert_material_exposure_safe_for_product (server.py:2445), and even that is flagged suspected inert in a code comment at server.py:2438-2444 — during a real solve only the non-raising _run_material_exposure_audit runs. Do not assume PrintabilityError ⇒ blueprint triage ran.

Level 2 — per-layer staged diagnostic + Stage 4 gate (staged_printability) — LIVE
This is the printability layer that actually executes. It works on the staged blueprint’s per-layer occupancy, not pixel columns. build_layered_blueprint_view (pipeline/staged_printability.py:170) derives a read-only LayeredBlueprintView (staged_printability.py:31) — one boolean/label map per color layer, cap layer, and detail layer — from the staged artifacts (VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlan, CapSynthesisPlan). resolve_blueprint_printability_settings (staged_printability.py:72) resolves the physical thresholds (minimum extrusion width, minimum/preferred line length, pitch, layer height) from the solve config.
It has two distinct jobs:
(a) The diagnostic report. run_blueprint_printability_diagnostic (staged_printability.py:410) labels the connected components inside each layer, grades each via grade_blueprint_component (staged_printability.py:271, which flags tiny_component / narrow_width / short_length against the physical minima), additionally runs a morphological-opening neck test (_opening_width_loss / _opening_width_loss_is_structural, staged_printability.py:312, :326) and a vertical-support check, and returns a frozen BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic (pipeline/staged_artifacts.py:501) carrying per-surface hard-fail pixel maps and a list of BlueprintPrintabilityComponentFacts (staged_artifacts.py:477). On the live path this is gated by emit_blueprint_printability and runs at staged_runner.py:10715-10733, attaching the result to cap_plan.blueprint_printability_diagnostic.
(b) The Stage 4 enforcement gate. The same grading helpers are re-exported publicly (opening_width_structure / opening_width_loss / opening_width_loss_is_structural, staged_printability.py:358, :362, :370) precisely so Stage 4 can apply the identical neck criterion as an in-place repair. _apply_stage4_boundary_cap_printability_gate (staged_runner.py:5230) grows or suppresses boundary-cap coverage and _apply_stage4_detail_printability_gate (staged_runner.py:5941) suppresses hard-failing detail material. These run inside Stage 4 guarded by a local enforce_printability = _printability_enforcement_enabled(cfg) flag (staged_runner.py:9630, applied at :9925 and :9993). _printability_enforcement_enabled (staged_runner.py:3346) returns config.enforce_printability when that attribute is present, falling back to config.stage4_printability_gate_detail otherwise.
Why it is LIVE, with defaults pinned. On the web app the relevant config flags are all forced on, not user-toggleable:






























FlagLive defaultAnchor_enforce (drives both enforce_printability and stage4_printability_gate_detail)True unconditionallyserver.py:1008 (“Product printability is mandatory”)enforce_printabilityTrueserver.py:1044, resolved-config default server.py:379 / server.py:854stage4_printability_gate_detail_enforce (→ True)server.py:1079, default server.py:394emit_blueprint_printabilityTrueserver.py:1040, default server.py:375
So the gate repairs the blueprint and the diagnostic reports on it on every normal solve. The diagnostic results surface to the UI as performance counters (server.py:2401-2409) and overlay maps (server.py:5034-5040). See How a Solve Works for where Stage 4 sits and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve for the staged backend internals.

VisibleRecipe vs StackDefinition. The view builder consumes VisibleRecipe (staged_artifacts.py:73) thickness-by-filament records. This is a near-duplicate of StackDefinition — same shape, different role. When citing one, name it explicitly; do not assume they are interchangeable in a given call.

Level 3 — mesh-level measurement (mesh/printability.py) — suspected inert
mesh/printability.py is a measurement-only toolkit over already-built trimesh.Trimesh objects — it never mutates meshes or alters export behaviour. It answers geometry questions the other two levels cannot: do the per-filament STLs share an XY origin (compare_xy_footprints, mesh/printability.py:78); does the top of one layer meet the bottom of the next or is there a measurable gap/overlap (inter_mesh_gap_overlap, :359, bucketed by classify_seal_severity, :458); are there connected XY components below a printable footprint area (thin_island_risks, :601).
The export-facing roll-up is what is flagged inert. build_printability_report (mesh/printability.py:1071) aggregates the measurements and classify_printability_report (:1041) maps them onto a pass / warn / fallback / block ladder with a next_action such as do_not_export (_classify_printability_summary, :916), wrapping it in this module’s own PrintabilityReport dataclass (:680). A code comment at mesh/printability.py:1061-1070 records that no live solve/export path appears to consume this classification — the only known callers are tests/generator/test_mesh_printability.py and scripts/characterize_mesh_printability.py.

Treat “inert” as a hint, not a fact. That same comment (:1066-1069) warns that an earlier audit declared this “dead” after missing real references, so the reference graph is subtle. Re-verify exhaustively across tests, scripts, the config chain, and the separate blueprint_triage module before removing or disabling anything. See What Actually Runs > mesh printability + canonical mesh — suspected inert.

The two PrintabilityReport traps
These two classes share a name and nothing else — keep them straight:























ClassDefined atWhat it isLives whereTriage PrintabilityReportpipeline/blueprint_triage/report.py:180Per-column hazard report with Verdict + PrintabilityError (report.py:29)Level 1, dormantMesh PrintabilityReportmesh/printability.py:680Export-facing mesh summary with status/severity/next_actionLevel 3, suspected inert
The middle (live) level uses neither — its report type is BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic (staged_artifacts.py:501), a third, separately-named dataclass.

printability/the-live-staged-printabilit.title: The live staged printability diagnostic
printability/the-live-staged-printabilit.content:
In one sentence: after the staged solve builds the white cap, the generator re-derives the layered plan, grades every connected component on every layer against the printer’s physical min-feature thresholds, and records a read-only diagnostic (per-pixel fail maps + worst-component facts) that the UI overlays — while a separate, always-on audit counts any colour filament left exposed to air.

The live staged printability diagnostic
This is the plan-level printability check that runs as part of a production solve. It does not repair geometry — it measures it. Two distinct things live here, both wired into the live solve path:

The blueprint printability diagnostic — a layer-by-layer grade of every connected component against resolved physical thresholds (min extrusion width, min/preferred line length, plus a neck, clearance, and vertical-support audit). Built in generator.pipeline.staged_printability.
The material exposure audit — a 3D face-count of colour filament left touching air, plus the mandatory white boundary-shield floor implied by colour-height cliffs. Built in generator.pipeline.material_exposure.

The diagnostic is read-only. The enforcement passes inside generator.pipeline.staged_runner (Stage 4 boundary-cap and detail repair) reuse the same grading helpers so a component the diagnostic flags is the same component the gates repair — see Reuse by the enforcement passes. For the stage that owns those gates see The staged backend (Stage 0-5).
How to drive it
You do not call any of this directly. It runs automatically inside run_staged_backend_path (the live webapp solve engine, pipeline/staged_runner.py:10310; the only caller is the runner at pipeline/runner.py:843-846 — not the legacy solve.py CLI engine). The diagnostic stage is gated on one flag and bounded by a handful of physical settings you set per run:



































KnobDefaultWhere setEffectemit_blueprint_printabilityTruefacade.py:174, server.py:375, state.py:112, app.js:312Master on/off for the diagnostic stage (staged_runner.py:10715).printability_minimum_extrusion_width_mmNone → 0.40resolver staged_printability.py:80Min printable feature width; from the active nozzle’s min_line_width (app.js:6379).printability_minimum_line_length_mmNone → derivedresolver staged_printability.py:85-89Min printable feature length; defaults to max(0.40, width + 0.10).printability_preferred_line_length_mmNone → derivedresolver staged_printability.py:90-94Soft-warn threshold; defaults to max(0.60, minimum_line).
When emit_blueprint_printability is off the diagnostic stage is skipped entirely; the exposure audit (below) still runs on every solve.
Step 1 — Resolving physical thresholds
resolve_blueprint_printability_settings (staged_printability.py:72) collapses the user/printer config into a frozen BlueprintPrintabilitySettings (staged_printability.py:20) carrying five numbers in millimetres: minimum_extrusion_width_mm, minimum_line_length_mm, preferred_line_length_mm, pitch_mm, layer_height_mm.
The resolver is forgiving — each field falls through a chain of candidates via _first_positive (staged_printability.py:59), which returns the first strictly-positive value:

Width: printability_minimum_extrusion_width_mm → printer_min_line_width_mm → hard floor 0.40 (staged_printability.py:79-84).
Min line: explicit value, else max(0.40, width + 0.10) (staged_printability.py:85-89).
Preferred line: explicit value, else max(0.60, minimum_line) (staged_printability.py:90-94).
Pitch: the pitch_mm argument → solver_fine_pitch_mm → image_sample_pitch_mm → 0.20 (staged_printability.py:95-100). The live call passes pitch_mm=solver_fine_pitch_mm (staged_runner.py:10720) so grading happens at the true fine solve resolution.
Layer height: layer_height → 0.08 (staged_printability.py:101).

Pitch is the linchpin: every pixel-count is converted to physical area/width/length by multiplying by pitch_mm, so the thresholds are compared in millimetres regardless of solve resolution.
Step 2 — The layered blueprint view
build_layered_blueprint_view (staged_printability.py:170) derives a read-only per-layer occupancy view (LayeredBlueprintView, staged_printability.py:31) from two staged artifacts: the VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlan (colour recipes per zone) and the CapSynthesisPlan (white cap + detail heights). It splits the plan into three surface families:

Colour layers — each visible recipe’s per-filament thickness is quantized into integer layer counts (_positive_layer_counts, staged_printability.py:132; note ≥ 1 layer for any positive thickness, staged_printability.py:138), expanded into an ordered label stack per recipe (_recipe_color_layer_table, staged_printability.py:142), then scattered across the image via the recipe label map (staged_printability.py:191-193). Material ordering follows the declared palette, with any stragglers appended (_ordered_material_ids, staged_printability.py:113).
Cap layers — the boundary cap, computed as cap_height_mm − detail_height_mm clamped at 0 (staged_printability.py:199-203), sitting on top of the colour ceiling (color_ceiling = cap_boundary_top_mm − boundary_cap_height, staged_printability.py:204-208).
Detail layers — the detail cap, stacked on color_ceiling + boundary_cap_height (staged_printability.py:248-255).

Each surface is materialized into a stack of boolean layer masks anchored to an absolute Z grid (absolute_layer_masks, staged_printability.py:211), so the support audit (Step 4) can look downward through the stack.
Step 3 — Grading a component
grade_blueprint_component (staged_printability.py:271) is the atomic check. Given a connected component’s pixel count and bounding-box height/width in pixels, it computes three physical measures and returns a grade:

























MeasureFormula (staged_printability.py)Compared againstarea_mm2pixel_count · pitch² :279min_extrusion_width · min_line_length :282-285width_mmmin(h, w) · pitch :280minimum_extrusion_width_mm :290length_mmmax(h, w) · pitch :281minimum_line_length_mm :292, then preferred_line_length_mm :296
Grades and their reason flags:

hard_fail if area below min_area (tiny_component), or width below min (narrow_width), or length below min (short_length) — any one trips it (:288-295).
soft_warn with short_length_preferred if it clears the hard length floor but falls short of the preferred length (:296-297).
pass otherwise (:298).

Bounding-box width/length alone cannot catch a fat blob joined by a one-pixel neck, so the diagnostic adds two more per-component checks on top of the bbox grade.
The opening-width neck criterion
grade_blueprint_component only sees the bounding box; a dumbbell shape (two wide lobes joined by a sub-width neck) passes its width test. The neck is caught by a morphological opening with a square structuring element sized to the minimum printable width:

_minimum_width_px (staged_printability.py:301) → ceil(min_extrusion_width / pitch) pixels; _opening_width_structure (:307) builds an N×N all-ones kernel.
_opening_width_loss (:312) opens the component and returns the pixels the opening removed — the kernel cannot fit there, i.e. sub-width features. A 1×1 kernel is a no-op (:320-321).
_opening_width_loss_is_structural (:326) decides whether the loss matters: opening also rounds harmless exterior corners. The loss is structural only if removing the lost pixels destroys the component or splits it into more than one piece (:342-349). Only structural loss escalates to hard_fail with narrow_width (:545-553); harmless corner rounding is ignored.

These three helpers are public re-exports (opening_width_structure :358, opening_width_loss :362, opening_width_loss_is_structural :370) precisely so the enforcement passes apply the identical criterion — the comment at :352-357 spells out why.
Step 4 — The full diagnostic run
run_blueprint_printability_diagnostic (staged_printability.py:410) walks every layer of every surface and accumulates per-pixel fail maps plus component-level facts. The inner consume_mask closure (:463) does the work for one (surface, layer, material) mask:

Connected-component labelling with 4-connectivity (ndi.label, structure from :460), iterating bounding boxes via find_objects (:504-509).
Bbox grade via grade_blueprint_component (:515).
Centre clearance — a distance transform in mm gives each pixel’s clearance to the nearest edge (_component_center_clearance_mm, :377; applied :529-536). Recorded as max_center_clearance_mm, not itself a fail.
Opening-width neck — structural loss escalates to hard_fail and marks width_loss_map (:538-553).
Vertical support — see below. Any unsupported pixel escalates to hard_fail with low_vertical_support (:566-575).

Every non-pass component becomes a BlueprintPrintabilityComponentFacts (:579, dataclass at staged_artifacts.py:476) carrying its bbox, physical measures, grade, reason flags, clearance, width-loss pixels, and support fraction. The full set is sorted hard-fail-first then by pixel count (:708-720) and the worst max_worst_components (default 128) are kept (:808).
Support-fraction checks
A colour pixel printed with nothing under it overhangs. _support_fraction_for_layer (staged_printability.py:392) measures, for layer k, the mean occupancy of the window of layers below it (window_layers=3, :397; layer 0 is treated as fully supported on the base, :400-401). Inside consume_mask, the per-pixel support map is sampled over the component; the mean is its support_fraction (:555-561), and any pixel with support < 1.0 is unsupported (:566).
Support sources differ per surface (:654-697):

























SurfaceSupport mapSource (staged_printability.py)colourrolling 3-layer occupancy below_support_fraction_for_layer(color_occupancy, …) :658-662cap (boundary)full support (sits on the colour ceiling)full_support :682detailthe union of all boundary-cap layerscap_any_support :685-696
Projected clustering
Beyond per-component facts, the run projects all hard-fail pixels down to a 2D map and clusters them (projected_cluster_summary, :721) at two radii: tight (:739-744) and dilated by a cluster_radius_px derived from min_line_length / pitch (:745-756). This surfaces “many small fails packed into one region” as a single large-cluster fraction — the color_hard_fail_largest_cluster_fraction family on the result.
The result object
The run returns a BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic (staged_artifacts.py:500): the resolved thresholds, per-surface layer/mask/fail counts, the tiny/narrow/short/soft tallies, the projected-cluster summaries, the worst-component tuple, and a stack of float32 per-pixel maps (hard_fail_map, soft_warn_map, narrow_width_map, short_component_map, color_hard_fail_map, cap_hard_fail_map, detail_hard_fail_map, center_clearance_map, width_loss_map, low_support_map).
Where it goes
In the live solve the diagnostic is attached to the cap plan (cap_plan.blueprint_printability_diagnostic = blueprint_printability, staged_runner.py:10733) and its scalar counts are timed/recorded into the run’s performance profile (staged_runner.py:10734+). The bridge (Step 5 of the staged backend) copies the float maps into the solve’s debug-map dict under blueprint_printability_* keys (pipeline/staged_bridge.py:325-372), which is how they reach the generator’s overlay viewer. A subset of the scalar counts is also promoted into run_metadata["stats"] for display (server.py:2400-2412). This is purely diagnostic — it gates nothing and raises nothing.
Reuse by the enforcement passes
The diagnostic is the measurement; the Stage 4 boundary-cap and detail repair passes are the enforcement, and they reuse the diagnostic’s grading helpers so the two stay in lockstep:

grade_blueprint_component is imported by staged_runner.py:68 and called from the enforcement graders — e.g. _stage2_component_physical_grade (staged_runner.py:3386), _component_physical_grade_with_opening (:3416), a local growth grader (:3808), and the vectorized layer-failure scan _stage4_layer_failures_vectorized (:5879).
opening_width_structure / opening_width_loss / opening_width_loss_is_structural are imported (staged_runner.py:69-71) and applied in those same passes (:3427-3431, :5901-5905) so the neck criterion is identical. The header comment at staged_printability.py:352-357 is explicit that bbox/area/length-only gates would let a 1-pixel neck slip past.

The material exposure audit
This page owns material_exposure.py. It is a separate, always-on audit (independent of emit_blueprint_printability) that asks one question: does any colour filament touch air in the final print? It is geometry-agnostic — it audits the raster material occupancy the export path will use, and it never smooths or repairs (material_exposure.py:1-7 header; trust the line behaviour, not the prose).
The boundary-shield floor
lateral_boundary_shield_floor_layers (material_exposure.py:78) computes, per pixel, how many white cap layers are mandatory to shield internal colour-height cliffs. For each 4-neighbour pair it compares colour-layer counts: the lower side must carry enough white cap to cover its neighbour’s colour-height excess; the higher side needs none for that pair (:99-108). This floor is enforced in the live solve — staged_runner.py:7117 feeds the result into the implied cap heights as minimum_cap_height_mm (:7120-7132), but only when a non-fixed cap mode is active (_non_fixed_lateral_shield_required, staged_runner.py:1300, gating at :7111). In fixed cap mode the cap already covers everything, so no floor is computed.
The colour-air exposure count
audit_colored_filament_exposure_from_layer_counts (material_exposure.py:112) counts exposed colour faces in 3D without building a voxel stack, given colour and white-cap layer-count maps:

























Face typeWhat it countsCodelateral_internal_face_countcolour stack on one side taller than the total (colour + cap) stack of a 4-neighbour:131-136top_face_countpixels with colour but zero white cap on top:138exterior_face_countcolour layers on the four image borders (no neighbour to shield them):139-144
A MaterialExposureAudit (material_exposure.py:29) bundles these counts plus the exposed-colour pixel count and stack maxima. Its passes property (:54) is True only if the print is fixed_thickness_exempt or the total exposed face count is zero (:55-57). The height-based entry point audit_colored_filament_exposure_from_heights (:188) just quantizes mm → layer counts first; audit_colored_filament_exposure_from_thickness_maps (:204) sums every exposure-relevant material map (exposure_relevant_material_keys, :241 — everything not prefixed __, minus explicit exclusions, :267-270) and resolves the white cap from WHITE_CAP or WHITE_BOUNDARY_CAP + WHITE_DETAIL_CAP (:273-289).
How the audit is wired
In the live solve, server.py calls the non-raising _run_material_exposure_audit (server.py:2419, invoked :5123) once per solve. It excludes the white base/cap ids (_white_ids, server.py:798) and marks the solve exempt when the cap is in fixed thickness mode (server.py:2415-2435). The summary lands in run_metadata["material_exposure_audit"] and the boolean white_cap_exposure_safe (server.py:5127-5130) for display — it records, it does not block.
A second, assert-form gate _assert_material_exposure_safe_for_product (server.py:2445) does raise PrintabilityError on exposure, but per the in-code note at server.py:2438-2444 it is suspected inert on the live solve path (no confirmed live caller found; appears exercised only by tests/generator/test_material_exposure_product_gate.py). Treat that as unconfirmed — the note itself asks for a full reference re-check before relying on it.
Disambiguation (do not confuse)

The blueprint BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic here is unrelated to the mesh-side PrintabilityReport classes. There are two unrelated report types in the codebase (blueprint-triage vs mesh) — this page is strictly the blueprint/plan-level one.
VisibleRecipe (staged_artifacts.py:73) is the per-zone recipe the layered view consumes; it is a near-duplicate of StackDefinition but not the same type — the view reads recipe.to_mapping() (staged_artifacts.py:105) and recipe.thickness_by_filament (:76).

Related

generator.pipeline.material_exposure — module node for the exposure audit
generator.pipeline.staged_runner — the enforcement passes that reuse the graders
Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract — the artifacts the layered view reads
minimum feature width — the 0.2mm physical floor doctrine

printability/the-white-cap.title: The white cap
printability/the-white-cap.content:
The white cap

In one sentence: the white cap is the clear/white skin laid on top of the solved colour stack, and its per-pixel thickness is whatever height is left under the t_max total-height contract — optionally biased toward the source image’s dark regions by a default-off luminance prior.

The colour stack the solver picks decides each pixel’s colour ceiling (white base + committed colour layers). The white cap is everything above that ceiling, up to the total object height. This page covers how that cap thickness is determined: the colour ceiling, the budget contract, the optional luminance prior, the boundary-vs-detail split, the post-solve detail smoothing, and the (currently inert) luminance tie-break.
Related: The live staged printability diagnostic owns material_exposure and the live printability fields — it does not use the cap-ceiling helpers below. The dormant Blueprint triage the unwired engine is the only consumer of colour_ceiling_from_plan / top_surface_from_fields. generator.height_budget, generator.luminance_handler, generator.detail_cap_smoothing, generator.cap_quality are the modules described here.
The colour ceiling
Every pixel sits under a colour ceiling = white base thickness plus the total committed colour thickness of its solved stack. colour_ceiling_from_plan builds this from the solved plan: it maps each pixel to its committed stack via committed_stack_label_map(plan) and adds d_wb to that stack’s total_colour_thickness_mm (pipeline/cap_quality.py:58, summed at pipeline/cap_quality.py:61-67). Pixels with no colour stack get a ceiling of just d_wb (pipeline/cap_quality.py:66).
This function is computed-but-unwired: its only product caller is the dormant blueprint-triage engine at pipeline/blueprint_triage/fields.py:146, which also composes the top surface with top_surface_from_fields (pipeline/blueprint_triage/fields.py:147; the composer itself is colour ceiling + visible cap at pipeline/cap_quality.py:70-78). No live solve or export path constructs an AnalysisContext or calls analyze_triage, so neither helper actually runs in production today — see Blueprint triage the unwired engine. Do not confuse this with the genuinely-live printability diagnostic in pipeline/staged_printability.py, which builds its own layered view and never touches these two helpers.
The total-height budget contract
t_max is the total object height, white base included. The only headroom the white cap may occupy is whatever is left above the colour ceiling. generator.height_budget is the whole policy:

























HelperContractAnchormax_cap_height_for_colour_thicknessscalar headroom = t_max - d_wb - colour_thickness, optionally clamped by a max-cap ceiling, floored at 0pipeline/height_budget.py:12, computed :20-23max_cap_height_map_for_colour_ceilingper-pixel headroom = t_max - colour_ceiling, optional d_wc_max clamp, floored at 0pipeline/height_budget.py:26, :34-37clamp_cap_height_map_to_budgetclamp any cap map so total height never exceeds t_maxpipeline/height_budget.py:40, :48-54
The scalar form is live in the solve: Stage 2 cap precompute calls max_cap_height_for_colour_thickness per unique stack to find the printable cap range, then marks over-budget cap steps as inf so the optimizer can’t pick them (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:116, masked at pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:125). Note that call passes d_wc_max_mm=cfg.effective_boundary_d_wc_max() (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:120) — the boundary ceiling, not the full one.
What sets the cap maximum
Three config accessors define the ceilings (defaults in pipeline/state.py):

effective_d_wc_max() — explicit d_wc_max if set, else t_max - d_wb - d_wc_min (pipeline/state.py:190-193).
effective_boundary_d_wc_max() — the full max, then clamped down by (a) the runtime luminance boundary authority if one was computed and (b) an explicit boundary_cap_authority_mm, always floored at d_wc_min (pipeline/state.py:195-202).
effective_white_cap() — the cap filament; falls back to the white base when white_cap is unset (pipeline/state.py:180-181).

Relevant defaults: d_wb=0.20, d_wc_min=0.08, t_max=3.0, layer_height=0.08 (pipeline/state.py:66,67,70,64).
The default-off source-luminance prior
generator.luminance_handler gives the cap an optional bias toward darker source regions (a thicker cap dims the backlight, so dark image areas request more white). It is default-off: gated by luminance_handler_enabled reading cfg.luminance_handler_enabled (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:47-49), whose default is False (pipeline/state.py:82).
It is wired into the live solve when enabled. Two entry points:

Before LUT building, configure_luminance_handler_runtime computes a reference and stashes the boundary authority on the config so effective_boundary_d_wc_max can clamp to it (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:527, authority set at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:552). Returns None early if disabled or if state lacks profiles/target (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:535-541).
In Stage 4, the staged runner calls LuminanceHandler(cfg, state.profiles).build(...) to get boundary and detail cap references (pipeline/staged_runner.py:8834, gated by luminance_handler_enabled(cfg) at :8833). When disabled, Stage 4 falls back to quantizing the raw solver-implied cap directly (pipeline/staged_runner.py:8864-8876).

How the prior is built (LuminanceHandler.build_reference, pipeline/luminance_handler.py:160):

Source luminance is the OKLab L of the solve target (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:175).
It samples the white-base × white-cap appearance curve over the printable cap-step range (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:385; photo-stack provider path at :399, historical-spline fallback at :405-412).
Mode boundary_prior (the default, pipeline/state.py:83) maps source darkness into a cap-mm request: floor + darkness × (available range) (full-image at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:213-216, boundary at :217-220). Mode absolute_optical instead interpolates the appearance curve directly (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:187-208).
“Darkness” is a percentile-normalised, optionally toe/shoulder-shaped inverse of luminance (_darkness_map pipeline/luminance_handler.py:470; response curves linear/smoothstep/smootherstep/gamma/sqrt at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:506-522).
Every cap map is layer-quantized and clamped to [floor, d_wc_max] via _quantize_cap_map (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:107); the floor is the smallest layer-grid multiple ≥ d_wc_min (_quantized_cap_floor, pipeline/luminance_handler.py:99).

Boundary authority
The handler also derives a single boundary authority (mm) — a ceiling on how thick the boundary cap may go. It is the smaller of an optical authority (the cap thickness reaching a configured fraction, default 0.75, of the achievable OKLab swing — _optical_authority pipeline/luminance_handler.py:444; fraction default pipeline/state.py:85) and, in absolute_optical mode, a percentile of the boundary prior (_boundary_authority pipeline/luminance_handler.py:432). An explicit boundary_cap_authority_mm clamps it further (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:240-248). This authority is what feeds back into effective_boundary_d_wc_max (above).
Boundary cap vs detail cap
LuminanceHandler.build emits two references that Stage 4 consumes (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:289):




















TierMeaningBuilt atboundary_cap_request_mmthe smooth cap thickness at segment boundaries, ceilinged by the boundary authoritypipeline/luminance_handler.py:310-332detail_cap_reference_mmthe per-pixel detail cap, ≥ boundary request, ceilinged by the full d_wc_max and never exceeding remaining t_max headroompipeline/luminance_handler.py:334-354
Three blend modes set the boundary request: blend_solver (alpha-blend raw vs prior), boundary_ceiling (min of raw and a blended ceiling), and the default else-branch (floor + strength × (prior − floor)) at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:311-326. The detail reference defends the t_max contract directly: it subtracts the colour ceiling from t_max and clips against that remaining budget before quantizing (remaining at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:341-345, then np.minimum at :345). Stage 4 reads both back out at pipeline/staged_runner.py:8840-8841.
Detail-cap smoothing (post-solve)
generator.detail_cap_smoothing is a live post-solve cleanup that removes single-pixel topographic noise from the detail cap only — it never touches colour maps, boundary cap, or stack topology. It runs from server.py:

Entry: _apply_detail_cap_smoothing_to_result (server.py:1327), invoked on every solve result at server.py:4743.
Gated to luminance-detail mode and the two enable flags: luminance_mode == "luminance_detail" plus detail_cap_enabled and detail_cap_smoothing_enabled (server.py:1336-1341). The two enable flags default on (server.py:365,367), but luminance_mode defaults to "standard" (server.py:425) — so on a default run the gate short-circuits and the smoothing is a no-op; it only acts once the run is switched into luminance-detail mode.
It converts the detail map to integer layer counts, smooths, converts back, and rewrites only the detail contribution inside the aggregate __white_cap__ map (server.py:1363-1377).

The smoothing itself (smooth_detail_cap_layers, pipeline/detail_cap_smoothing.py:100) does two passes on the integer layer map: replace exact-height speckles (≤1 px by default) with the local ring mode (pipeline/detail_cap_smoothing.py:117, remove_exact_height_speckles at :139), then on cumulative material masks drop tiny components and fill tiny holes (pipeline/detail_cap_smoothing.py:122, cleanup_cumulative_detail_masks at :167). Defaults: max 8 layers, 1-px speckle, 2-px component, 2-px hole (DetailCapSmoothingSettings, pipeline/detail_cap_smoothing.py:12-20), overridable from config (server.py:1306-1324).
The luminance tie-break (computed but currently unconsumed)
resolve_luminance_tiebreak (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:71) resolves a (weight, window) pair intended to break near-ties in colour cost toward the luminance-preferred cap. It reads luminance_tiebreak_weight/luminance_tiebreak_de_window (defaults 0.0/0.0, pipeline/state.py:80-81) and, when the handler is enabled, falls back to handler-specific overrides or a fraction of de_threshold (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:80-94).
It is called on the live staged path — staged_runner.py:6259 computes luminance_tiebreak_weight, luminance_tiebreak_de_window = resolve_luminance_tiebreak(cfg). However, those two local variables are never read again anywhere later in staged_runner.py (verified: no occurrence after line 6259). So as the code stands the tie-break resolution runs but its result does not currently influence Stage 2 zone scoring — treat the tie-break as resolved-but-inert pending a consumer. The config fields and resolver are not dead (the resolver is invoked), but the downstream wiring is absent.
Legacy: the cap quality scorecard
generator.cap_quality also contains analyze_cap_quality (pipeline/cap_quality.py:576), which computes a full cap scorecard — exposed-colour cliffs, island/pinhole risks, boundary/neighbour deltas, dE stats. This is test-only. Grepping the product tree, analyze_cap_quality, compare_assignment_stability (pipeline/cap_quality.py:724), and metric_subset (pipeline/cap_quality.py:761) are referenced only by tests/generator/test_cap_quality.py outside their own module. The sub-analyses they drive — find_cap_island_risks (:306), find_cap_pinhole_risks (:318), exposed_colour_cliff_analysis (:330), default_line_profile (:536) — are reachable in product code only through analyze_cap_quality, so they are dormant too.
The two helpers colour_ceiling_from_plan and top_surface_from_fields are no exception — they are not live either. The module’s only non-test product import is pipeline/blueprint_triage/fields.py:11, which pulls in exactly those two functions; but that consumer (the blueprint-triage engine) is itself computed-but-unwired (see Blueprint triage the unwired engine), so the whole of cap_quality.py is dormant in production. The genuinely-live printability path is the separate pipeline/staged_printability.py diagnostic, which does not import this module at all.
Driving it (for users)

Leave luminance_handler_enabled off for the standard colour-faithful solve; the cap then just fills remaining t_max headroom.
Turn it on to bias the cap toward darker image regions; tune luminance_handler_strength (pipeline/state.py:84) and the response curve (pipeline/state.py:88-89).
Detail-cap smoothing only acts when the run is in luminance-detail mode (server.py:1336); in standard mode it is a no-op regardless of the enable flags.
To cap total height, set t_max; to cap just the white cap, set d_wc_max or boundary_cap_authority_mm.

readme.title: README
readme.content:
Prisma Documentation (pilot)
This folder is an Obsidian vault. To open it:

Install Obsidian (already done).
Open folder as vault → choose this Documentation/ folder.
Start at Home.

Everything here uses built-in Obsidian features only (wikilinks, tags, graph
view, backlinks, search) — no community plugins — so the same vault can later be
published as a static website with Quartz without rework.
What this pilot is
A small, deliberately incomplete first slice covering one subsystem of the
generator app — the solve pipeline, end to end. It exists so we can judge
whether this format (an interlinked wiki + graph) is the right home for
Prisma’s documentation before committing to a full pass.
It is not comprehensive yet. It covers: how a solve runs, the colour
(transmission) model, the joint LUT and staged solve, and how print files are
exported. Calibration is intentionally out of scope for now.
The one rule these docs follow
Every claim is traced to the actual code, not to prior notes or memory.
Where a page states how something works, it cites the source file and line
(e.g. Prisma/generator/pipeline/runner.py:587) so any reader can verify it
directly. If a page and the code ever disagree, the code wins — open an issue,
fix the page.
Folder layout

Home — start here; map of the whole slice.
Generator/ — the hand-written concept + walkthrough pages.
Concepts/ — short definitions of recurring terms (the wiki “glossary” nodes).
Architecture/ — one stub note per code module, linked to its real
dependencies, so the graph view reflects the actual import structure.

Open the graph view (the icon in the left ribbon) to see how these connect.

solver/solveconfig-and-solveresult-refer.title: SolveConfig and SolveResult reference
solver/solveconfig-and-solveresult-refer.content:
SolveConfig and SolveResult reference

In one sentence: SolveConfig is the ~80-field dataclass that fully specifies one solve, and SolveResult is the container the facade returns — thickness maps, diagnostics, stats, and the predict_image reconstruction methods.

Both live in generator.facade (Prisma/generator/facade.py). The module header still calls itself lith_facade.py (facade.py:2) — that name is stale; cite line anchors, not the header. This page covers the two dataclasses a caller hands in (SolveConfig) and gets back (SolveResult), the effective_* helpers that derive runtime values, and the two forward-prediction methods (predict_image, predict_image_color_only).
For the functions that consume a SolveConfig — solve_preview, solve_full, solve_compare — see The solve facade. For the pipeline they delegate into, see The staged backend and generator.pipeline.runner.

SolveConfig
@dataclass SolveConfig (facade.py:160) — “All parameters needed for a single solve invocation.” One required field, the rest defaulted. The web server builds one at server.py:1015 (return SolveConfig(...)); the CLI builds its own.
How it is driven
A caller constructs a SolveConfig, then passes it to a facade entry point. The same object flows through _to_pipeline_config (facade.py:612), which copies its fields one-for-one into a PipelineConfig for the runner. Almost every field below is forwarded verbatim there — SolveConfig is the public shape, PipelineConfig the internal one. SolveConfig does not hold an image: the image is a separate argument to solve_full(img, config, ...).
__post_init__ — the resolution backstop
__post_init__ (facade.py:283) calls _apply_resolution_backstop(self) from config/resolution_schema.py:153. This enforces the solve-coupled pitch pair invariant: if both image_sample_pitch_mm and solver_fine_pitch_mm are None, both default to the family default; if exactly one is set, it raises ResolutionSchemaConflictError (resolution_schema.py:170-177); if both are set they must agree (resolution_schema.py:178). So you cannot construct a SolveConfig with a half-specified pitch family — the dataclass refuses it at construction time. See Resolution schema.
Field groups
The dataclass declares its fields across facade.py:163-281. Grouped by what they do (defaults shown are the dataclass defaults, not server defaults):
Materials & palette













































FieldDefaultMeaningpalette(required)Ordered list of colour-filament IDswhite_base(required)White-base filament ID (the substrate)white_capNoneWhite-cap filament ID; None ⇒ reuse white_base (see effective_white_cap)profiles_dirNoneOverrides the default spline-profile directoryappearance_model_provider"historical_spline"Forward-model backend selector (see Appearance model providers)photo_stack_bundle_pathNoneBundle path when the provider is the photo-stack modeluse_corrections / correctionsFalse / NonePair-correction toggle and payload
Geometry budget


















































FieldDefaultMeaninglayer_height0.08mm per layert_max3.0Target total height (mm)d_wb0.20White-base thickness (mm)d_wc_min0.08Minimum white-cap thickness (mm)d_wc_maxNoneMax cap; auto-derived if None (see effective_d_wc_max)max_layersNoneColour-layer cap; auto-derived from t_max if Nonek_max3Max simultaneous colour filaments per pixelboundary_cap_authority_mmNoneOptional ceiling on boundary cap thickness
Resolution (canonical pitch fields)
image_sample_pitch_mm (0.20), solver_fine_pitch_mm (0.20), stage1_coarsening_factor (1), stage1_lattice_offset_y_px / _x_px (0). These are the only resolution channel — there are no legacy alias fields on the runtime dataclass (resolution_schema.py:157). See Resolution schema.
Cap shaping
cap_mode ("smooth_variable" | "fixed"), cap_fixed_thickness_mm (0.0, 0 ⇒ use d_wc_min in fixed mode), cap_continuity_cleanup (True, fills single-pixel cap pinholes), plus the detail-cap family detail_cap_pitch_mm / detail_cap_enabled / detail_cap_max_layers.
Solver behaviour
de_threshold (0.01), gamut_mode ("hull" convex hull, or "chroma" legacy), gamut_white_rescale, chroma_weight (1.0, >1 prioritises colour over lightness in the KD-tree), the luminance_tiebreak_* pair, and the full luminance_handler_* family (~14 fields, facade.py:220-233) governing the optional Luminance handler.
Model-domain ingress — model_domain_ingress (True) and model_domain_ingress_lut_path ("Prisma/data/camera_transform") thread the Camera Transform inverse LUT into image ingress. See Model domain ingress.
Staging / printability — a large stage2_* family (continuity weight, fine override, boundary mutation, printability gates/repair), stage4_* detail-surface flags, and the printability_* / enforce_printability / color_region_* group. These feed the staged backend and blueprint printability. emit_blueprint_printability defaults True; allow_print_despite_hazards defaults False.
Smoothing & cells — smooth_kernel (15.0), smooth_iters (3), cell_mode ("felzenszwalb"), smooth_boundaries (False), boundary_smooth_radius (1), and the v2_* cleanup family.
AMS slots — ams_slots (4), white_slots (1). Colour slots are derived (see colour_slots).
Grouping (beam search) — grouping_max_iterations, grouping_beam_width, grouping_z_waste_weight, grouping_overflow_weight, grouping_swap_count_weight, grouping_slot_stability, grouping_de_scoring, grouping_de_cost_weight, grouping_in_group_sub. These instantiate the grouping module in _resolve_grouping_from_state (facade.py:513) — only consumed when module_state["group_budget"] is set; otherwise a plain GreedyGrouping runs. See Grouping and slot scheduling.
Preprocessing — preprocessing_params (per-operator kwargs keyed by module name; every registered operator’s params block materializes here at its default), plus protect_subject_* and protect_mask_* for subject protection. See Preprocessing pipeline.
Printer / resample — nozzle_diameter (0.20), printer_min_line_width_mm, source_resample_kernel ("lanczos" default, bit-exact with pre-B7 behaviour; "area" selects cv2.INTER_AREA).
effective_* and derived helpers
These methods resolve None/auto fields into concrete runtime values. They are the canonical place to read a derived value — callers and the runner use them rather than recomputing.


















































Methodfacade.pyReturnseffective_white_cap()288white_cap or white_baseeffective_max_layers()291max_layers, else int((t_max - d_wb - d_wc_min) / layer_height)effective_d_wc_max()296d_wc_max, else t_max - d_wb - d_wc_mineffective_boundary_d_wc_max()301effective_d_wc_max() clamped by boundary_cap_authority_mm and a runtime override attr, floored at d_wc_mineffective_detail_cap_pitch_mm()310detail_cap_pitch_mm, else first non-None of solver_fine_pitch_mm, image_sample_pitch_mm, else 0.20effective_detail_cap_max_layers()3210 when detail_cap_enabled is false, else max(0, detail_cap_max_layers)effective_white_slots()326max(white_slots, 2) when base ≠ cap (a distinct cap filament needs its own slot), else white_slotscolour_slots()331ams_slots - effective_white_slots()
effective_boundary_d_wc_max reads a private runtime attribute _runtime_luminance_boundary_cap_authority_mm via getattr (facade.py:303) — the luminance handler can stamp a tighter authority onto the config object mid-solve; absent that, only the static fields apply.
Cloning
_replace_solve_config(config, **changes) (facade.py:769) shallow-clones a SolveConfig from config.__dict__ with overrides. solve_compare uses it to swap in each palette (facade.py:1011). Because it rebuilds via the constructor, __post_init__ re-runs — the resolution invariant is re-checked on every clone.

SolveResult
@dataclass SolveResult (facade.py:359) — “Complete result of a solve operation.” Built by _state_to_solve_result (facade.py:864), which converts a PipelineState back into the public result shape after the runner finishes. Direct tests may construct partial SolveResult objects with many fields None.
__post_init__ — thickness-map normalisation
__post_init__ (facade.py:394) wraps a raw dict into the typed ThicknessMaps if it is not already one (facade.py:400-401). This is a no-op when the runner already handed over a wrapped container (the webapp path), so it preserves exact object aliasing there. ThicknessMaps (thickness_maps.py:77) is a compatibility-first MutableMapping whose keys normalise to plain strings, so every serializer and frontend payload sees the exact legacy strings. The reserved sentinel keys are the MapKey enum (thickness_maps.py:40): __white_cap__, __white_boundary_cap__, __white_detail_cap__, __de__, __gamut_mask__. Dynamic filament-IDs are plain strings, distinguished by not starting with __.
Fields





















































































FieldTypeNotesthickness_mapsThicknessMapsPer-filament + reserved-sentinel arrays; the solve outputcolour_profiles / wb_profile / wc_profiledictsLoaded spline profiles used for predictionstatsSolveStatsAggregate dE / coverage / per-filament usage (facade.py:344)configSolveConfigThe config that produced this resultappearance_providerobject | NoneThe forward-model provider (drives predict_image backend choice)reference_imagendarray | NoneThe ingress image (model-domain), copied from statepalette_fit_image / palette_fit_de / solver_loss_mapndarray | NoneBest-case-fit diagnostics (full-solve only; see below)palette_fit_rms_de / solver_loss_rms_defloat | NoneRMS scalars for the abovegroupingGroupingResult | NoneSlot-scheduling resultimage_domain_width_mm / _height_mmfloat | NonePhysical extentsolved_planSolvedMaterialPlan | NoneCanonical solve-owned plan (product paths populate it)staged_resultobject | NoneThe raw StagedBackendResultdiagnosticsDict[str, ndarray]Canonical diagnostic home (see accessor fallback below)debug_maps / preprocessing_metrics / cap_qualitydictsAuxiliary outputsblueprint_triagePrintabilityReport | NonePrintability hazard report (the blueprint_triage variant — see Blueprint triage; not the mesh PrintabilityReport)
Diagnostics-vs-thickness_maps accessor fallback
The de_map and gamut_mask properties (facade.py:405-415) each prefer the diagnostics dict and fall back to thickness_maps:
@property
def de_map(self):
    if MapKey.DE in self.diagnostics:
        return self.diagnostics[MapKey.DE]
    return self.thickness_maps[MapKey.DE]
This dual lookup exists for a reason spelled out at facade.py:382-387: the staged/webapp runner populates diagnostics (from PipelineState.diagnostics: __de__, __gamut_mask__, __target_gamut_*__), so production results take the first branch. The fallback to thickness_maps serves only diagnostics-less legacy results — the separate legacy CLI engine, and tests that build a SolveResult straight from thickness_maps without a diagnostics dict. The same prefer-then-fall-back pattern appears in _compute_palette_fit_diagnostics (facade.py:802-805).
The other map accessors read thickness_maps directly (no fallback needed — caps are always part of the thickness output): cap_map → WHITE_CAP (facade.py:417), boundary_cap → WHITE_BOUNDARY_CAP or None (facade.py:421), detail_cap → WHITE_DETAIL_CAP or None (facade.py:427), filament_ids → the dynamic keys (facade.py:431).
Best-case palette-fit diagnostics
palette_fit_image / palette_fit_de / solver_loss_map are computed by _compute_palette_fit_diagnostics (facade.py:784) and only for preset.name == "full" (returns {} otherwise, facade.py:787). It re-queries the LUTs for the per-pixel best achievable match (query_luts_batch, facade.py:824) and computes the solver’s loss as max(final_de - best_de, 0) (facade.py:853) — i.e. how far the actual solve fell short of the palette’s theoretical best. See Solve diagnostics and dE maps.

predict_image and predict_image_color_only
These are the forward reconstruction methods: given solved thickness maps, recompose the predicted backlit image. This page owns the cap-zeroing explanation.
predict_image
predict_image(max_layers=None, *, thickness_maps=None) (facade.py:437) returns an (H, W, 3) uint8 image. Two backends, selected by the appearance provider’s model_kind (facade.py:452-454):

historical_spline (the default provider) and any diagnostics-less result fall to predict_image_fast (solve.py:674), the vectorised spline composition: T = T_wb · Π T_colour(d) · T_cap(d) per pixel, then gamma-2.2 to sRGB uint8 (solve.py:714).
non-spline providers (e.g. photo_stack_bundle, appearance_model.py:224) route to provider.predict_thickness_maps_srgb(...) (facade.py:456).

The thickness_maps= keyword overrides the solved maps for the prediction. Default None uses the solved maps, byte-for-byte preserving historical behaviour (facade.py:451). This override is the hook predict_image_color_only rides on.
max_layers defaults to config.effective_max_layers() (facade.py:450).
Callers (confirmed live): server.py:4007 (preview/gamut-check reconstruction), :4117 (per-palette reconstruction inside the solve_compare loop), :4806 (the full-solve reconstruction), plus evaluation/preprocessing_render.py:64,68, scripts/validate_task3_real_images.py:199, and several tests. predict_image is the live image-reconstruction path for the generator UI.
predict_image_color_only — and white-cap zeroing as multiplicative identity
predict_image_color_only(max_layers=None) (facade.py:494) reconstructs the base + colour image with the white cap omitted, so the cap’s luminance shaping does not drown out the colour story. The base stays in — it is the substrate. Output is the same model-domain gamma-2.2 sRGB uint8 as predict_image, so it can be baked through the display transform F (facade.py:501).
It is a thin wrapper: it calls self.predict_image(max_layers, thickness_maps=self._cap_zeroed_thickness_maps()) (facade.py:503). All the interesting work is in _cap_zeroed_thickness_maps (facade.py:474):
maps = self.thickness_maps.copy()
for cap_key in (WHITE_CAP, WHITE_BOUNDARY_CAP, WHITE_DETAIL_CAP):
    existing = maps.get(cap_key)
    if existing is not None:
        maps[cap_key] = np.zeros_like(np.asarray(existing))
return maps
It shallow-copies the maps (ThicknessMaps.copy(), arrays shared) and replaces every white-cap term — total cap and its boundary/detail components — with an all-zero array.
Why zeroing the cap thickness cleanly drops the term: a zero cap thickness is the multiplicative identity in the transmission model. The composition multiplies a per-channel cap transmission T_cap(d_wc) into the stack (solve.py:710-712; spline provider appearance_model.py:205-206). The transmission of any profile at thickness 0 is [1, 1, 1] — confirmed at lib/transmission.py:107-108:
if d <= 0.0:
    return np.ones(3)
So T_cap(0) = [1,1,1], and multiplying the stack by [1,1,1] leaves base × colour untouched. This holds in both spline-composition backends (predict_image_fast and the spline appearance provider both call predict_transmission → predict), exactly as the method’s docstring asserts (facade.py:478-481). The cap term is dropped without touching the composition math — no special-casing, just feeding it the identity input.
Liveness: predict_image_color_only and _cap_zeroed_thickness_maps are defined at facade.py:494 / :474 and are live. The full-solve path invokes result.predict_image_color_only() at server.py:4855, saving the result as predicted_color_only.png and baking it through the forward Camera Transform F into predicted_color_only_appearance.png (server.py:4859) — this is the colour-only predicted render for the Recipe viewer’s “Color Regions” tab (the cap-omitted “colour story” view). The behaviour is exercised directly by tests/generator/test_predict_color_only.py (including test_photo_stack_backend_receives_cap_zeroed_maps, which checks the non-spline backend receives a zeroed cap). (Confirmed by grep against the call site, not inferred from headers.)

Related

The staged backend — run_staged_backend_path, the engine the webapp actually runs (runner.py:843)
Resolution schema — the pitch-pair invariant __post_init__ enforces

Solve diagnostics and dE maps — what lives in diagnostics

solver/stage-1-and-2-solver-kernels.title: Stage 1 and 2 solver kernels
solver/stage-1-and-2-solver-kernels.content:
Stage 1 and 2 solver kernels

In one sentence: staged_solver_helpers.py is a bag of stateless NumPy kernels that the staged solver uses to carve an image into colour zones (Stage 1) and to turn the per-pixel colour stacks into a scored grid of cap-thickness colour predictions (Stage 2).

What this page is
pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py holds the shared, side-effect-free math kernels for the two early stages of the live solve. They do not own any solver policy — no commitment logic, no zone graph traversal, no budgeting decisions. They take arrays in and hand arrays back. The orchestration that calls them lives in generator.pipeline.staged_runner; this module is the low-level toolbox.
These kernels run on every webapp solve. The webapp solve runs the staged backend (pipeline/runner.py:843 imports and calls run_staged_backend_path, defined at pipeline/staged_runner.py:10310), not the legacy “6-step” engine in solve.py. So everything below is on the hot path for a real generate.
Origin note (stale-docstring defuse)
The module docstring claims these functions “used to live in the retired dual-resolution solver wrapper” (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:1-8). That is a historical note about where the code moved from, not about its current status. The functions are live — every public name in __all__ (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:306-315) has at least one in-tree caller (see Liveness below). Do not read “retired … legacy … dead solver wrapper” in that header as a claim that this code is dead; the wrapper is gone, the kernels were lifted out and kept.
The kernels

































































FunctionAnchorStageRolegenerate_stage1_zone_labels:2541Carve the planning image into a dense zone-label map_smooth_label_map:2161Majority-vote boundary smoothing of a label map_relabel_contiguous_labels:2471Force label ids into dense 0..n-1_vectorized_stack_ids:212Encode per-pixel layer stacks into unique-stack ids_predict_transmission_batch:582Batch spline transmission for an array of thicknesses_precompute_cap_oklabs:872Spline-model cap-OKLab grid + over-budget inf sentinel_precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized:1312Photo-stack cap-OKLab grid (scoring + dense views)_score_candidates_batch:1902Score many candidate stacks against a zone’s pixels_score_stack_for_cell:1802Per-stack fallback scorer (memory-safe path)
Stage 1 — zone-label generation
generate_stage1_zone_labels (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:254) produces a 2-D integer label map the same height/width as the planning image, where each integer is a colour zone. It is “dense Stage 1 zone-label map without solver commitment logic” (:264) — it only segments; the runner decides what to do with the zones.
Cell size. If scale is not passed, it is derived as round(color_region_target_mm / solver_fine_pitch_mm), floored to ≥1 (:266-271). pixels_per_cell = scale * scale (:272). In the live path the runner passes an explicit scale override (coarse_scale_override, derived from the stage-1 coarsening factor) when staging is active (staged_runner.py:702-717), so the internal derivation is mostly a fallback.
Three cell modes (:274-298), selected by cfg.cell_mode:

























cell_modeMechanismNotes"grid"Plain scale × scale square tiling via np.repeatDeterministic axis-aligned cells; default-ish"felzenszwalb"skimage.segmentation.felzenszwalb, scale = max(1, pixels_per_cell*0.8), sigma=0.8, min_size=pixels_per_cellContent-aware blobsanything elseskimage.segmentation.slic, n_segments = (h*w)//(pixels_per_cell*4), compactness=10SLIC superpixels; the catch-all branch
After segmentation the labels are forced contiguous (:300), optionally boundary-smoothed if cfg.smooth_boundaries is set (:301-302, radius from cfg.boundary_smooth_radius), then relabelled contiguous again on the way out (:303).
_smooth_label_map (:216) iterates radius passes; each pass finds 4-neighbour boundary pixels and replaces each with the majority label in its 3×3 window (np.bincount(...).argmax(), :240-242). It short-circuits when a pass finds no boundary (:232-233) and finishes with a contiguous relabel (:244). _relabel_contiguous_labels (:247) is the trivial “unique + inverse-index reshape” that guarantees ids are 0..n-1 as int32.

The radius/boundary_smooth_radius plumbing here is the same smooth_boundaries feature noted as bug-fixed 2026-04-12 in project memory; this kernel is where the majority vote actually happens.

Stage 2 — from per-pixel stacks to a scored cap grid
Stage 2 (entry around staged_runner.py:6195) turns LUT-queried per-pixel thicknesses into a compact, scorable representation. The kernels do three jobs: encode, predict, score.
Encode — _vectorized_stack_ids
_vectorized_stack_ids (:21) collapses the per-pixel thickness dictionary into a small set of unique stacks. Mechanics:

Round each filament’s thickness to an integer layer count: rint(raw / layer_height) per palette entry (:31-34).
Pack the per-pixel layer-count vector into a single integer using a positional base of max_layers + 1 (:36-38) — a mixed-radix encoding where each filament occupies one “digit”. max_layers defaults to 50 but the live caller passes cfg.effective_max_layers() (staged_runner.py:6218).
np.unique(..., return_inverse=True) gives pixel_stack_ids (per-pixel index into the unique table) and the unique codes (:40-41).
Decode each unique code back into a {filament_id: thickness_mm} dict, dropping zero-layer entries (:43-53).

Returns (pixel_stack_ids, unique_codes, unique_stack_dicts). This is the key compression step: a megapixel image with a handful of distinct stacks becomes a few hundred unique-stack dicts the rest of Stage 2 reasons over.

Palette order matters for the photo-stack model. The caller chooses the palette ordering before encoding: for the photo-stack model it keeps cfg.palette order (staged_runner.py:6209-6212) because that model is an ordered physical stack; for the historical spline model it sorted()s the palette because spline composition is order-insensitive. The kernel itself just encodes whatever ordered palette it is handed.

Predict — _predict_transmission_batch
_predict_transmission_batch (:58) evaluates the spline transmission model for a whole array of thicknesses at once. It pulls the per-channel splines via lib.transmission._get_splines (:60-62) and:

thickness ≤ 0 → transmission 1.0 (:68, :72);
thickness within knot range → clipped [0,1] spline eval per R/G/B (:74-78);
thickness beyond the last knot → per-element lib.transmission._extrapolate (:80-82).

Returns an (N, 3) RGB transmission array. This is the spline-model batch evaluator; see lib.transmission for the underlying PchipInterpolator splines and the transmission contract T_total = T_wb · ∏ T_fi · T_wc.
Cap-OKLab precompute — the two grids
Stage 2 needs, for every unique stack, the OKLab colour it would show at each possible white-cap thickness. There are two implementations, picked by model kind at staged_runner.py:6241.
Spline model — _precompute_cap_oklabs
_precompute_cap_oklabs (:87) builds the cap grid for the historical spline model:

Cap steps 0 .. d_wc_max at layer_height spacing (:94-98); d_wc_max = cfg.effective_boundary_d_wc_max().
White-cap transmission for all cap steps via _predict_transmission_batch (:100-102).
For each unique stack: compose white-base + colour layers with compose_stack (:108-112, from generator.model), multiply by every cap transmission, convert to OKLab with to_oklab (:114-115).
Over-budget inf sentinel (:116-126): the cap headroom left by this stack’s colour thickness is computed with max_cap_height_for_colour_thickness from generator.pipeline.height_budget (remaining = t_max - d_wb - colour_thickness, clamped to d_wc_max). Any cap step beyond that headroom has its OKLab row set to np.inf (:124-125). Because the downstream scorer takes a Euclidean distance and then .min() over cap steps, an inf row can never be the chosen cap — so the optimizer is structurally forbidden from selecting an unprintable cap. This is the mechanism that keeps the solve inside the ~3 mm total-height budget.

Returns (cap_values, all_oklabs) where all_oklabs is (unique_stacks, n_steps, 3).
Photo-stack model — _precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized
_precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized (:131) does the same job for the photo-stack provider, but returns two views (:138-147):




















ViewBudget handlingUsed forscoring_oklabsover-budget cells masked with inf (:175-176)zone scoring — the optimizer can’t pick unprintable combosdense_oklabsfinite at every cellStage-4 cap lookup always gets a colour answer; budget enforcement is the cap planner’s job
Cap steps come from the LUT cap grid (deduped from each LUT’s cap_thicknesses, :153-162) — never scavenged from the pruned LUT, never routed through the row-shaped predictor (docstring :144-146, behaviour :163-177). The actual grid evaluation is delegated to predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid (photo_stack_lut.py:957), which returns (dense_oklabs, within_budget); the budget mask is applied here at :175-176 with budget_mm = t_max - d_wb (:173).
The caller binds the dense view to dense_cap_oklabs and the scoring view to all_oklabs (staged_runner.py:6242-6248); the spline branch sets dense_cap_oklabs = all_oklabs since it has no separate dense view (:6250-6251).
Score — _score_candidates_batch
_score_candidates_batch (:190) scores a set of candidate stacks against a zone’s pixels. For each candidate it computes, per pixel, the OKLab distance to the candidate’s best cap step, then averages over the zone’s pixels — “mean optimal-cap dE” (:180-187). It has two code paths:

Vectorized (:205-208): if the pixels × candidates × steps × 3 tensor is under 50 M elements, it broadcasts the whole thing, squares-sums-sqrts to dE, takes min over cap steps then mean over pixels.
Per-candidate fallback (:210-213): above that size it loops candidates and calls _score_stack_for_cell (:180) one at a time to cap peak memory.

Both return a (candidates,) array of scores; lower is better. This is the kernel the zone-candidate machinery calls in two places: enumerating each zone’s own candidates (staged_runner.py:794) and scoring borrowed neighbour candidates during augmentation (staged_runner.py:889). The candidate ids being scored are unique-stack ids, and the cap grid passed in is the scoring view (all_oklabs), so the inf sentinel rows propagate into these scores as “never selected”.
How the kernels wire together (Stage 2 sequence)
_query_stage2_pixel_stacks (LUT batch query)   staged_runner.py:6198
        ↓ thickness_result
_vectorized_stack_ids                           staged_runner.py:6214  → helpers:21
        ↓ pixel_stack_ids, unique_stack_dicts
_precompute_cap_oklabs[_vectorized]             staged_runner.py:6242/6250 → helpers:87/131
        ↓ all_oklabs (scoring view, inf-masked)
_enumerate_zone_candidates                      staged_runner.py:6262
   └─ _score_candidates_batch                   staged_runner.py:794   → helpers:190
_augment_zone_candidates_with_neighbor_...      staged_runner.py:6281
   └─ _score_candidates_batch                   staged_runner.py:889   → helpers:190

Timings for two of these steps are recorded into the run’s performance profile as stage2_vectorized_stack_ids_s (staged_runner.py:6224) and stage2_precompute_cap_oklabs_s (staged_runner.py:6255) — these show up in run.json files under the run cache.
Reuse by the luminance handler
_predict_transmission_batch is also imported and used outside Stage 2 by generator.pipeline.luminance_handler (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:19). In _sample_white_luminance_curve’s spline branch it computes white-cap transmission for an array of cap thicknesses (luminance_handler.py:407-410), then converts to OKLab. So this one kernel serves both the Stage 2 cap precompute and the white-cap luminance handling — a single source of truth for “spline transmission of many thicknesses at once.” (The photo-stack branch of that same method bypasses the kernel and asks the provider’s own sample_white_cap_oklab directly, luminance_handler.py:399-404.)
Liveness
Confirmed from grep over Prisma/ (not from docstrings). Every public name in __all__ has a live in-tree caller:

The staged backend itself is the live solve path: pipeline/runner.py:843-846 imports and calls run_staged_backend_path (defined staged_runner.py:10310). The legacy solve.py “6-step” engine is a separate, non-webapp path and does not use these kernels.
