tooling/filesystem-layout,-caching,-and-.filePath: Tooling/Filesystem layout, caching, and the recipe cookbook.md
tooling/filesystem-layout,-caching,-and-.title: Filesystem layout, caching, and the recipe cookbook
tooling/filesystem-layout,-caching,-and-.content:
In one sentence: data_paths.py is the single source of truth for where the generator writes things (a clearable cache/ vs. persistent siblings under data/generator/), cache_admin.py clears that cache without ever escaping it through a Windows junction, run_naming.py mints chronological collision-free ids for exports and saved runs, and recipe_cookbook.py rolls each solve’s per-recipe color breakdown into the family → combo → recipe tree the recipe viewer browses.

This page covers four small, pure-ish modules that together define the generator’s on-disk contract. They are deliberately tiny and side-effect-light so the rest of the app can trust them. See generator.server for the endpoints that wire them together, and The interactive recipe viewer for the UI the cookbook feeds.

Filesystem layout (data_paths.py)
Every generator path flows from one module so there is exactly one place that decides “is this clearable scratch or persistent data?”. The module computes its anchors relative to its own file location — _GEN_DIR is Prisma/generator and _PRISMA_DIR is its parent (data_paths.py:14-15) — so it does not depend on the working directory.
The cache vs. persistent split
The governing rule: output/ holds only user deliverables, and everything else the app generates lives under data/generator/, split into a clearable cache/ and persistent siblings.





















































ConstantResolves toLifetimeClear endpoints touch it?OUTPUT_DIR (data_paths.py:50)Prisma/output/lithophanesuser deliverablenoCACHE_DIR (data_paths.py:52)data/generator/cacheclearable scratch root— (it is the root)RUN_CACHE_DIR (data_paths.py:53)cache/runsper-solve working dirsyesLUT_CACHE_DIR (data_paths.py:54)cache/lutsbaked LUTsyes (clear-all only)AUTO_RUNS_DIR (data_paths.py:55)cache/auto_runsauto-saved run archivesyesSAVED_RUNS_DIR (data_paths.py:57)data/generator/saved_runsuser-curated archivesnoLOG_DIR (data_paths.py:58)data/generator/logslogsno
GENERATOR_DATA_DIR (data_paths.py:48) is DATA_DIR / "generator", the parent of both cache/ and the persistent siblings. The structural safety of “clear cache never deletes saved runs” rests on saved_runs/ being a sibling of cache/, not a child — see the caching section below.
Where DATA_DIR comes from (env / .data-root resolution)
DATA_DIR is computed once at import time by resolve_data_dir() (data_paths.py:47, defined at data_paths.py:21). This is the filament/calibration data root shared by both web apps. Resolution order (first hit wins):

Environment variables, checked in order PRISMA_GENERATOR_DATA_ROOT then PRISMA_CALIBRATION_DATA_ROOT (the env names are bound at data_paths.py:17-18, the loop is data_paths.py:29-32). A set value is expanduser().resolve()’d.
.data-root pointer files, checked in order generator/.data-root then calibration/.data-root (data_paths.py:33-36). The file’s text is read and stripped; a relative pointer is resolved against the pointer file’s own directory (data_paths.py:41-42), so a .data-root can redirect with a path relative to itself.
Fallback: Prisma/data (data_paths.py:44).


Trap: there is a second, independent data-root redirect in lib.camera_transform that reads Prisma/calibration/.data-root on its own. If you redirect the generator in SQLite/relocation work, both mechanisms must agree or the registry and the Camera Transform can resolve to different roots (noted in the SQLite changeover audit). data_paths.resolve_data_dir does not govern the camera-transform path.

Boot: ensure_dirs()
ensure_dirs() (data_paths.py:61) mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)s the managed set: OUTPUT_DIR, CACHE_DIR, RUN_CACHE_DIR, LUT_CACHE_DIR, AUTO_RUNS_DIR, SAVED_RUNS_DIR, LOG_DIR (data_paths.py:63). It is called exactly once, at server import (server.py:158) — confirmed by grep; the only two references to ensure_dirs() in the generator are the definition and that one call site. Note LOG_DIR is created on boot but is not swept by either clear endpoint.

Run, export, and save ids (run_naming.py)
Three different id schemes coexist; do not conflate them.
Run-cache id = the request’s card_id
A per-solve working directory is cache/runs/{card_id}. The card_id is client-supplied (the UI’s run/card identifier), not minted by run_naming.py. _current_out_dir() (server.py:1894) builds the path; with no card_id it falls back to the literal "current" (server.py:1903). Before use the id is passed through _validate_card_id() (server.py:1886), which rejects anything not matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ with HTTP 400 (server.py:1889-1890) — this is the traversal/slug guard for run-cache and export dirs alike (_export_out_dir reuses it, server.py:1915).
Export id and save id (minted by run_naming.py)
Both make_export_id (run_naming.py:34) and make_save_id (run_naming.py:54) produce a Windows-safe, chronologically-sortable name of the form {timestamp}-{image-stem} — the timestamp leads so listings sort by time, and the image stem follows for readability (run_naming.py:37-38, run_naming.py:57-58). Neither encodes the palette/label: the palette is recorded in the export manifest (run_naming.py:39-40), and the save’s display label is deliberately excluded so renaming never changes identity (run_naming.py:58-59).
Both run their parts through _slugify (run_naming.py:16), which: normalizes / and \ to spaces before the regex so palette dots aren’t eaten by Path.stem (run_naming.py:22-24); lowercases and collapses any non-[a-z0-9] run to a single - (run_naming.py:25); truncates to _MAX_LEN = 64 (run_naming.py:7, applied run_naming.py:26); falls back to "export" if empty (run_naming.py:8, run_naming.py:27-28); and appends -x to Windows reserved device names like con/nul/com1 (run_naming.py:9-13, run_naming.py:29-30).
Collision handling differs by what counts as “taken”:























MintsCollision checkCallermake_export_idexport folder nameoutput_root/{candidate} directory exists (run_naming.py:46)server.py:5460make_save_idsaved-run id{candidate}.zip or {candidate}.json exists (run_naming.py:66)server.py:6030, auto_run_store.py:74
Both append -2, -3, … as a same-second backstop, trimming the base so the suffix stays within _MAX_LEN (run_naming.py:47-50, run_naming.py:67-69).
Timestamp formats (set by the callers, not run_naming.py)
The timestamp is passed in by the caller, so the format lives in server.py:

Export: datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") (server.py:5459) → e.g. 20260621-143005-steve.
Manual save: same %Y%m%d-%H%M%S (server.py:6076), then make_save_id at server.py:6030.
Auto save: saved_at or datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") (server.py:6063).
Promotion (auto → saved) reuses the auto record’s original saved_at as the timestamp unless overridden (auto_run_store.py:73), re-minting a fresh save_id against the saved-runs root (auto_run_store.py:74).

Saved-run and auto-run archives are stored as a {save_id}.zip + {save_id}.json sidecar pair, validated on every access by run_store.resolve_save_paths against _SAVE_ID_RE = ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ (run_store.py:14, run_store.py:31-33) — the same character class as card_id, enforced independently. Listings sort newest-first by (saved_at, save_id) reversed (run_store.py:69). See generator.run_store / generator.auto_run_store.

Caching (cache_admin.py)
cache_admin.py exists to answer one question safely: “delete the contents of this cache directory, and under no circumstances follow a link out of the cache to delete something else.” On Windows that “link” includes directory junctions (reparse points), which pathlib/shutil.rmtree will happily traverse.
The clear endpoints
Two POST endpoints in server.py call into it (grep-confirmed; these are the only callers):























EndpointSweepsSparesCodePOST /api/cache/clear-runsRUN_CACHE_DIR, AUTO_RUNS_DIR + in-RAM solve cacheLUTs, output, saved_runsserver.py:5933, sweep server.py:5942-5945POST /api/cache/clear-allRUN_CACHE_DIR, LUT_CACHE_DIR, AUTO_RUNS_DIR + in-RAMoutput, saved_runsserver.py:5950, sweep server.py:5958-5961
Both first call _assert_no_active_job() (server.py:5926), which raises HTTP 409 if any solve/export/compare job is running (server.py:5928-5930), then clear the in-RAM solve_cache (server.py:5946, server.py:5962). Every directory is cleared with root=data_paths.CACHE_DIR, so the boundary is the cache root itself.

Why saved_runs/ is structurally safe: it lives under data/generator/, a sibling of cache/. safe_clear_dir refuses any target not under its root, and the clear endpoints always pass root=CACHE_DIR. There is no code path that would point a clear at saved_runs/; it is outside the permitted root by construction.

safe_clear_dir(target, *, root) — the containment contract
safe_clear_dir (cache_admin.py:47) deletes the contents of target (keeping target itself) and returns the count of top-level entries removed (cache_admin.py:89-90). It refuses anything questionable by raising OutsideRootError (cache_admin.py:9). The guard is layered, and all of it runs on lexical absolute paths — os.path.normpath(os.path.abspath(...)) resolves .. but does not resolve symlinks/junctions (cache_admin.py:57-59). This is the whole trick: lexical paths can’t be redirected by a junction, so the checks below see the intended tree, not a relocated one.

Containment — target must equal root or have root among its lexical parents, else OutsideRootError (cache_admin.py:60-61).
Root + every ancestor must be real dirs — it walks root and all its parents up to the filesystem anchor; if any is a link/junction it refuses (cache_admin.py:66-70). A junction anywhere above the cache would physically relocate the whole tree, so deletion can’t be allowed to start.
Every component root→target must be real — each path part between root and target is checked the same way (cache_admin.py:72-76).
Missing target is a no-op returning 0 (cache_admin.py:77-78).

Junction/symlink-aware deletion
Detection is _is_link_or_junction (cache_admin.py:13): it os.lstats the path (never following), treats S_ISLNK as a link, and additionally checks st_file_attributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT (0x400) to catch Windows junctions (cache_admin.py:19-23). When the walker hits a link/junction entry it unlinks the entry itself without recursing through it via _unlink_link (cache_admin.py:26), which tries os.rmdir (junction-to-dir / dir symlink) and falls back to os.unlink (file symlink) (cache_admin.py:29-31). Real subdirectories are recursed with _rm_tree (cache_admin.py:34), which uses os.scandir + is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) so it likewise never crosses a reparse point (cache_admin.py:36-44). Net effect: a junction sitting inside the cache is removed as a single entry; its target is left untouched.
This behaviour is exercised by tests/generator/test_cache_admin.py (junction-root refusal at lines 83-84, mid-path component refusal at 113-116) and tests/generator/test_cache_clear_endpoints.py.

The recipe cookbook (recipe_cookbook.py)
The recipe viewer needs to answer “which filament combinations make up this image, and in what proportions?” The cookbook is the aggregator that turns the flat per-recipe breakdown into a browsable tree. It is a pure module — no I/O, no numpy, no server deps (recipe_cookbook.py:14), unit-tested in isolation by tests/generator/test_recipe_cookbook.py.
Input, caller, and what’s already been stripped
build_recipe_cookbook (recipe_cookbook.py:35) is called once, from the artifact-saver in server.py:1649 (grep-confirmed sole caller). It consumes the same per-recipe entries that get written to the *_recipe_breakdown.json artifact (the entries list, server.py:1615), feeding it two scalars from that payload’s totals block:

all_plan_pixels= the breakdown’s all_plan_pixels (server.py:1651, sourced server.py:1613 from segment_id_map.size) — the denominator for every area fraction.
base_only_pixels= the breakdown’s excluded_empty_recipe_pixels (server.py:1652, server.py:1612) — pixels whose stack has no colored filament.

Crucially, each entry’s recipe is the ordered stack of colored filaments only — the white base and white cap are excluded upstream before the cookbook ever sees them (recipe_cookbook.py:4-6). The cookbook does no color/optics; it is pure counting. The result is written next to the breakdown as {base}_cookbook.json (server.py:1654-1658) and reported back as cookbook_filename (server.py:1663).
The output tree
The taxonomy is three nested levels plus a flat rollup:
N-color family   →   unordered filament combo   →   specific thickness recipe

Walking the build (recipe_cookbook.py:65-89): each entry is bucketed by n_colors = len(recipe) (recipe_cookbook.py:70) and by an order-insensitive combo = the sorted tuple of filament ids (recipe_cookbook.py:71). Entries with pixel_count <= 0 are skipped (recipe_cookbook.py:68-69). The recipe_key is taken from the entry if present, else recomputed by _recipe_key (recipe_cookbook.py:28), whose "{id}:{thickness:.6g}" join is kept byte-identical to the breakdown’s own key format (the matching format string is server.py:1566-1567; the cookbook’s own comment cites it as server.py:1565) (recipe_cookbook.py:29-32) — so cookbook keys match the breakdown’s.
The returned dict (recipe_cookbook.py:165-172) has:








































FieldMeaningAnchorschema"prisma-recipe-cookbook-v1"recipe_cookbook.py:21, :166total_image_pixelsthe all_plan_pixels denominatorrecipe_cookbook.py:167base_only_pixels0-color pixel countrecipe_cookbook.py:168color_pixelssum over families with n_colors > 0recipe_cookbook.py:161-163familiesthe family → combo → recipe treerecipe_cookbook.py:91-146filamentsper-filament rolluprecipe_cookbook.py:148-159
Every node carries pixel_count and area_fraction, the latter via _frac (recipe_cookbook.py:24), which is numerator/denominator or 0.0 when the denominator is 0 (recipe_cookbook.py:25) — so a zero-pixel image yields all-zero fractions instead of dividing by zero.
The 0-color “Base only” family
If base_only_pixels > 0, a synthetic family is prepended with n_colors: 0, label "Base only", and a single collapsed combo/recipe whose recipe_key is the literal "base-only" and whose filaments list is empty (recipe_cookbook.py:95-119). It “collapses” because there is nothing to slice — family  combo  recipe. When base_only_pixels == 0 the family is omitted entirely (the if at recipe_cookbook.py:95).
Sort order (stable, deterministic)
Ordering is fixed so the UI renders deterministically:

Families: 0-color first (prepended), then ascending n_colors (sorted(families), recipe_cookbook.py:121).
Combos within a family: by descending pixel count, ties broken by the combo tuple — key=lambda c: (-combos[c]["pixels"], c) (recipe_cookbook.py:124).
Recipes within a combo: descending pixel count, ties by recipe_key (recipe_cookbook.py:126-128).
Filament rollup: descending pixel count, ties by filament_id (recipe_cookbook.py:158). Each rollup row also reports recipe_count = the number of distinct recipe keys the filament appears in, tracked via a set (filament_recipe_keys, recipe_cookbook.py:63, :89, counted :154).

Relationship to the viewer
This cookbook JSON is what powers the recipe viewer’s “Recipe cookbook” and “Color Regions” surfaces — see The interactive recipe viewer. The viewer ships both the recipe tree and the filament rollup; which one a user leans on is decided by interaction, not by the backend picking for them. The cookbook is the aggregation; it does not render color — the color-only predicted render is a separate path in generator.server.

tooling/saving,-loading,-and-auto-captur.title: Saving, loading, and auto-capturing runs
tooling/saving,-loading,-and-auto-captur.content:
In one sentence: a completed solve can be packed into a portable, self-contained zip archive (plus an authoritative JSON sidecar) and either deliberately saved by the user or silently auto-captured into a 20-slot ring buffer, then later loaded back into a fresh card — with the loader treating every archive (including uploaded ones) as untrusted input.

This page covers how the generator persists a finished solve so you can come back to it later or hand it to someone else. There are two storage tiers, one archive format, and a careful loader. See also Run cache and per-card artifacts, The staged solve backend, and generator.run_archive / generator.run_store / generator.auto_run_store / generator.run_naming.
The two tiers at a glance








































Saved runs (user-curated)Auto runs (ring buffer)Directorydata/generator/saved_runs/ (data_paths.py:57)data/generator/cache/auto_runs/ (data_paths.py:55)Created byExplicit user Save actionAutomatically after every completed solveSidecar tier"saved" (server.py:6081)"auto", forced on write (auto_run_store.py:41)RetentionKept until the user deletes (run_store.delete_save)Newest 20 only; older ones evicted (auto_run_store.py:12, :43)Survives “Clear cached runs”?Yes — under GENERATOR_DATA_DIR, not sweptNo — auto_runs/ is cache; swept by clear_cache_runs (server.py:5944)Promote-to-saved?n/aYes, via Save on the row → /api/runs/auto/{id}/promote
Both tiers use the same on-disk pair ({save_id}.zip + {save_id}.json) and the same archive format. auto_run_store is a thin re-root of run_store: it just points run_store at AUTO_RUNS_DIR and adds eviction (auto_run_store.py:19-28). The list endpoint merges both tiers and re-sorts newest-first (server.py:6088-6092).
Disk layout: zip + authoritative JSON sidecar
For each run, run_store.write_save writes two sibling files under the store root, named by save_id (run_store.py:46-55):

{save_id}.zip — the portable, self-contained archive (see below). This is the only thing you’d hand to another machine.
{save_id}.json — the sidecar: a small dict that is the authoritative source for the run list and its display label. list_saves reads only the sidecars, never opening a zip (run_store.py:64-66), and rename_save edits only the sidecar label, leaving the zip untouched (run_store.py:104, :99).

Both files are written atomically — to .tmp siblings first, then os.replace swaps them into place (run_store.py:51-55) — so a crash mid-write never leaves a half-written run in the list.
The sidecar carries: save_id, label, saved_at, source_image_name, the palette, a trimmed stats block (mean_de / max_de only), schema_version, and tier (server.py:6043-6055). list_saves sorts entries newest-first by (saved_at, save_id) (run_store.py:69).
save_id identity is stable across renames
make_save_id mints the id as {timestamp}-{image-stem}, slugified and Windows-safe, capped at 64 chars, with same-second collisions getting a -2, -3, … suffix; a candidate collides if either {id}.zip or {id}.json already exists (run_naming.py:54, :66). The display label is deliberately not part of the id (run_naming.py:58-60) — renaming changes the sidecar label but never the identity, so existing zip/sidecar paths stay valid. The id is also a strict allow-list ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ (run_store.py:14); anything else raises SaveNotFoundError before any path is built (run_store.py:32-33).
What’s inside the archive
run_archive.pack_run_archive (run_archive.py:98) builds the zip from already-extracted pieces — it touches no disk and no server state. Members:



































MemberRequiredContentsrun.jsonyesheader + full config + palette + image-domain dims + stats + result (server.py:6013-6023)thickness_maps.npzyesnp.savez_compressed of tm__<key> thickness arrays and dbg__<key> debug arrays (server.py:6001-6004)image/<file>yesexactly one source-image member; required, non-empty (run_archive.py:110-111)solve_state.jsonoptional{ solve_owned_fingerprint } review-tier state (server.py:6024)run_cache/<relpath>optionalthe entire per-card run-cache subtree (png/bin/json/csv + export bundle), nesting allowed (server.py:6005-6012)
The run_cache/ subtree is copied verbatim so that instant review (contours, surface explorer, recipe viewer) works on a loaded run without re-solving (server.py:6005-6006). Because the per-card cache can be large, pack_run_archive enforces the same member-count (MAX_MEMBERS = 4096) and total-uncompressed-byte (MAX_TOTAL_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES = 512 MB) ceilings the loader checks, so Save can never produce an archive the loader would reject (run_archive.py:121-133, :37-38). JSON members are serialized to the exact bytes that get written so the byte total matches what the reader later sees (run_archive.py:115-118).
Driving it: the user-facing flows
All flows live behind /api/runs/* in server.py and thin wrappers in app/api.js.
Save a completed solve
The Save button calls saveRun(cardId, label) → POST /api/runs/save (api.js:254-255). Server side (server.py:6073): it requires a completed cached solve for that card or returns 409 (server.py:5985-5990); the source image must still exist on disk or it refuses to write a “hollow” archive (409, server.py:5996-5998); then it packs and writes the pair with tier="saved", returning {save_id, label}. An empty label defaults to the save_id (server.py:6031).
Browse, load, download, rename, delete
The Saved Runs browser lists both tiers via GET /api/runs/saved (api.js:258, server.py:6086). Each row is tagged "Saved" or "Auto" (app.js:6657-6664) and offers:

Load → loadSavedRun(saveId, tier) → POST /api/runs/load with {save_id, tier} (api.js:262-263, server.py:6242).
Download → a direct link to /api/runs/saved/{id}/download or /api/runs/auto/{id}/download (app.js:6674-6676, server.py:6095, :6106) streaming the raw zip.
Rename (saved only) → POST /api/runs/saved/{id}/rename (api.js:274, server.py:6127) — sidecar label only.
Delete (saved only) → DELETE /api/runs/saved/{id} (api.js:270, server.py:6135).
Save (auto only) → promote (next section).

You can also load an uploaded zip that didn’t come from this machine: uploadSavedRun(file) → POST /api/runs/load-upload (multipart) (api.js:278-284, server.py:6256).
Delete is idempotent but surfaces locked files
run_store.delete_save removes both files with missing_ok=True, so deleting an already-gone run is a benign no-op (run_store.py:91). But a file that exists yet can’t be removed — e.g. a zip locked open on Windows — raises the typed SaveDeletionError (run_store.py:92-95), which the endpoint converts into a clean 409 telling the user to close the program holding it (server.py:6139-6144), rather than crashing.
Auto-capture and promotion
Capture happens automatically on every solve
At the end of a successful solve, once the completed-solve cache entry is written, the staged backend calls _maybe_write_auto_run(card_id, solve, config) (server.py:5355-5357). This packs the identical archive Save would (same _pack_completed_run_archive), but with tier="auto" and an auto-generated label Auto <timestamp> (server.py:6063-6068). The whole thing is wrapped in a try/except that only logs on failure (server.py:6069-6070) — auto-capture is best-effort and must never break a solve. (This is the live The staged solve backend path, not the legacy CLI engine in solve.py.)
write_auto_run forces tier="auto" onto the sidecar regardless of what the caller passed (auto_run_store.py:40-42), then immediately evicts.
Ring-buffer eviction keeps the newest 20
After each write, evict_old_auto_runs lists the auto sidecars newest-first and deletes everything past index limit (default AUTO_RUN_RETENTION_LIMIT = 20) (auto_run_store.py:46-54, :12). A negative limit is clamped to 0 (:48-49). Because auto runs share run_store’s newest-first ordering, “past index 20” is reliably the oldest records.
Promote an auto run to a saved run
The auto row’s Save button calls promoteAutoRun(saveId) → POST /api/runs/auto/{id}/promote (api.js:266-267, server.py:6117). auto_run_store.promote_auto_run (auto_run_store.py:57):

resolves the auto pair via run_store.resolve_save_paths (no raw f-string paths from endpoint-controlled ids — auto_run_store.py:66-68);
mints a fresh saved-tier save_id under SAVED_RUNS_DIR, preserving the original timestamp (auto_run_store.py:73-74);
rewrites the sidecar with the new id, tier="saved", and a promoted_from_auto_id breadcrumb (auto_run_store.py:75-80);
moves the zip bytes unchanged into saved_runs/, then publishes the new sidecar — and if the sidecar publish fails after the zip moved, it rolls the zip back so there’s never an unlisted orphan in saved_runs/ and the auto record survives for a retry (auto_run_store.py:86-96).

Promotion is gated by _assert_no_active_job (server.py:6119) so it can’t race a running solve/export/compare. Once promoted, the run lives under saved_runs/ and survives a cache clear.
How loading works
Loading a run never restores into the original card; it builds a fresh “loaded-” card and replays the archive into it.
load_run (server.py:6242) and load_run_upload (server.py:6256) both gate on _assert_no_active_job (server.py:6248, :6259), then funnel into _load_from_bytes → read_run_archive → _rehydrate_loaded_archive:

Untrusted parse — run_archive.read_run_archive validates the zip (see safety section) and returns a ParsedArchive (run_archive.py:149). On any ArchiveError, the endpoint returns HTTP 400 (server.py:6231-6232).
Fresh card id — _fresh_loaded_card_id mints a collision-free loaded-<timestamp> card (server.py:6151-6159).
Image — written to a save-scoped unique path {card_id}-{name} under the images dir; config.image_path is rewritten to it (server.py:6182-6185).
Thickness maps — the npz is split back into thickness_maps (tm__ prefix) and debug_maps (dbg__ prefix) (server.py:6187-6192).
Run-cache subtree — the whole run_cache/ tree is restored under the fresh card’s dir, so /api/run-cache/files serves contours/explorer/recipe (server.py:6193-6200); relpaths were already validated safe during parse.
URL rebasing — every ?run=<old> in the result payload (top-level and nested url maps/lists) is rewritten to the new card id by _rebase_run_urls (server.py:6162-6173, :6202).
Cache entry — a synthetic status="complete" solve entry is written into session["solve_cache"], with grouping / solved_plan / profiles set to None (re-export and swap tolerate their absence — server.py:6204-6218).

The frontend then applies the loaded run and (best-effort) restores its palette to the deck (app.js:6819-6883).
Safety: the loader assumes archives are hostile
read_run_archive is built to be safe on untrusted zips — uploaded archives go through the exact same path as locally-saved ones. It never calls extractall; every byte is read by explicit member name. The guards (run_archive.py:149-194):

Member-count ceiling — > MAX_MEMBERS (4096) → reject (run_archive.py:158-159).
No duplicate member names (run_archive.py:161-162).
Total-uncompressed-byte ceiling — sum of file_size > 512 MB → reject before decompressing (zip-bomb guard) (run_archive.py:163-165).
Closed allow-list of member names — only run.json, thickness_maps.npz, solve_state.json, one image/<leaf>, and run_cache/<relpath> are permitted; everything else is rejected (_member_is_safe, run_archive.py:70-82).
Path-traversal refusal — empty / absolute / drive-letter (:) / backslash / . / .. / ../-escaping relpaths are all rejected, including each nested run_cache/ path (_is_safe_relpath, run_archive.py:56-67).
Symlink / non-regular refusal — any member whose external-attr type field is set and isn’t a regular file is rejected; Windows writestr members (no type field) correctly pass (_zipinfo_is_symlink, run_archive.py:85-95).
Required members present — run.json and thickness_maps.npz must exist (run_archive.py:172-174).
Schema gate — run.json.schema_version must be in ACCEPTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {1} or reject (run_archive.py:176-177, :29).
Exactly one image, non-empty (run_archive.py:180-188).

The upload route adds a compressed-upload cap on top: it reads the multipart body in 1 MB chunks and aborts with HTTP 413 once it passes MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (512 MB), before the full read and the uncompressed zip-bomb check, and never trusts a client Content-Length (server.py:6262-6269, run_archive.py:39).
Liveness notes
Every endpoint and helper below was confirmed wired front-to-back by grepping callers:

saveRun/loadSavedRun/promoteAutoRun/renameSavedRun/deleteSavedRun/uploadSavedRun are all defined in app/api.js:254-285 and the Save button calls saveRun at app.js:6601; load is invoked at app.js:6772; promote at app.js:6718.
_maybe_write_auto_run is called from the live staged-solve completion path at server.py:5357.
clear_cache_runs (server.py:5934) sweeps AUTO_RUNS_DIR but not SAVED_RUNS_DIR, confirming auto-runs are cache and saved runs are durable.

Related

Run cache and per-card artifacts — the per-card run_cache/ subtree that gets embedded and restored
The staged solve backend — produces the completed solve that auto-capture archives
The interactive recipe viewer — a consumer of the restored run-cache artifacts

tooling/the-preprocessing-evaluation-har.title: The preprocessing evaluation harness
tooling/the-preprocessing-evaluation-har.content:
In one sentence: an offline A/B bakeoff that solves two images through the production pipeline under one shared config and reports a fixed metric bundle (mean/p95 dE, out-of-gamut pixels, small-component count, cap total-variation), optionally dropping predicted-PNG + heatmap + report.json artifacts to disk.

This page documents the evaluation/ package under Prisma/generator/: how to drive it from the CLI or a Python caller, what each metric means, and the generator.evaluation internals. It exists to answer “did this preprocessing operator (or solver tweak) actually help?” with comparable numbers instead of eyeballing two renders.
What it is for
The harness compares two versions of an image — a baseline and a candidate — by running each through the full generator solve and diffing the results. It is corpus-agnostic: both images are passed in as explicit arrays, so the difference between baseline and candidate can be anything the caller wants (a preprocessing operator applied to one, a different denoise setting, etc.). It does not generate the candidate; you do that, then hand both to evaluate_pair.
Both arms run through the same SolveConfig, so any metric delta is attributable to the image difference, not config drift.
The contract: evaluate_pair
The single public entry point is evaluate_pair(request, *, modules_path=None, module_state=None) at Prisma/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_harness.py:105. It takes an EvaluationInput and returns an EvaluationResult.



































SymbolWhereRoleEvaluationInputpreprocessing_harness.py:73Frozen dataclass: case_id, baseline_image, candidate_image, solve_config, optional out_dir.EvaluationMetricspreprocessing_harness.py:82Frozen dataclass holding all 11 metric fields (see below).EvaluationResultpreprocessing_harness.py:97Carries both SolveResult objects, the metrics bundle, and artifact_paths.EvaluationRunErrorpreprocessing_harness.py:57Raised (not swallowed) when either arm’s solve fails; tags .arm ("baseline"/"candidate") and .original.evaluate_pairpreprocessing_harness.py:105Runs both arms, aggregates metrics, optionally renders artifacts.
Flow

Two solves. _run_arm (preprocessing_harness.py:157) calls solve_full (from generator.facade) once per image. solve_full runs run_pipeline under FULL_PRESET (facade.py:975), i.e. the staged production backend — not the legacy 6-step CLI engine in solve.py. If either solve raises, it is wrapped as EvaluationRunError(arm, exc) (preprocessing_harness.py:174) rather than crashing silently.
Metric aggregation. _compute_metrics (preprocessing_harness.py:177) reads the two SolveResult objects and builds the EvaluationMetrics bundle.
Optional artifacts. Only when request.out_dir is not None (preprocessing_harness.py:135) does it lazily import render_evaluation_artifacts and write files. The lazy import is deliberate — in-memory metric callers never pull in PIL (preprocessing_harness.py:136).

Metrics are always returned in memory; artifacts are opt-in.
Where the metrics come from
_compute_metrics reads these SolveResult accessors (defined in generator.facade):



































Source fieldAccessorAnchordE mapresult.de_mapfacade.py:406 (prefers diagnostics[MapKey.DE], falls back to thickness_maps)Gamut maskresult.gamut_maskfacade.py:412Per-filament thicknessresult.thickness_mapsfacade.py:362White-cap mapresult.cap_mapfacade.py:418 (MapKey.WHITE_CAP)Predicted renderresult.predict_image()facade.py:437
The solver pitch used for area scaling is config.solver_fine_pitch_mm (preprocessing_harness.py:188), read off the baseline’s SolveResult.config.
The metric bundle
EvaluationMetrics (preprocessing_harness.py:82) holds eleven fields — for the five base metrics, both arms plus one delta where relevant:



































MetricBaseline / candidate fieldsHow computedMean dEbaseline_mean_de, candidate_mean_de, delta_mean_dede_map.mean() per arm; delta = candidate - baseline (preprocessing_harness.py:184, :198). Empty map → 0.0.p95 dEbaseline_p95_de, candidate_p95_de95th percentile of the dE map via _p95 → np.percentile(arr, 95.0) (preprocessing_harness.py:225). Empty → 0.0.Out-of-gamut pixelsbaseline_oog_pixels, candidate_oog_pixels_oog_pixels counts True cells in the boolean gamut_mask: int(mask.sum()) (preprocessing_harness.py:230).Small-component countbaseline_small_component_count, candidate_small_component_countcount_small_components over the thickness maps (see below).Cap total-variationbaseline_cap_total_variation, candidate_cap_total_variationcap_total_variation over cap_map (see below).
Note dE is the only metric with a precomputed delta_* field; for the rest the caller diffs the two arms themselves (the bakeoff runner does exactly this).
Metric primitives — preprocessing_metrics.py
Two metrics are non-trivial and live in Prisma/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_metrics.py:
count_small_components (preprocessing_metrics.py:32) — counts speckle. For each per-filament thickness map (keys starting with __ are diagnostics and skipped, preprocessing_metrics.py:56):

Mark a pixel “occupied” if its thickness exceeds 5% of that map’s max (_SMALL_COMPONENT_REL_THRESHOLD = 0.05, preprocessing_metrics.py:29; applied at :64).
Run 8-connectivity connected-component labelling — the 3×3 structuring element of ones (preprocessing_metrics.py:52) via scipy.ndimage.label (:67).
Convert each component’s pixel count to physical area as pixel_count × pixel_pitch_mm² (preprocessing_metrics.py:51, :72).
Accumulate the count of components whose area is below min_area_mm2 (preprocessing_metrics.py:73).

The min_area_mm2 threshold is derived in the harness, not hard-coded: feature_scale_mm², where feature_scale_mm comes from resolve_feature_scale_mm (preprocessing_harness.py:192). That helper returns 2.0 × nozzle_diameter (the constant _FEATURE_WIDTHS_PER_NOZZLE = 2.0, feature_scale.py:37; applied at feature_scale.py:73), i.e. 0.40 mm at the default 0.20 mm nozzle, so min_area = 0.40² = 0.16 mm² (preprocessing_harness.py:193). This is the value the retired cleanup_min_area_mm2 carried (preprocessing_harness.py:191).
cap_total_variation (preprocessing_metrics.py:77) — measures how “busy” the white-cap surface is. Returns the anisotropic L1 total variation Σ(|Δx| + |Δy|) over the 2-D cap map: abs(diff(axis=1)).sum() + abs(diff(axis=0)).sum() (preprocessing_metrics.py:89). It is a grid-space sum, not a per-mm integral (preprocessing_metrics.py:82) — a non-2-D or empty map returns 0.0 (:85). Lower means a smoother cap.
Artifacts — preprocessing_render.py
When out_dir is set, render_evaluation_artifacts (Prisma/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_render.py:49) writes exactly four files:






























FileConstant / anchorContentbaseline_predicted.pngpreprocessing_render.py:44, written :64Baseline predict_image() as RGB PNG.candidate_predicted.pngpreprocessing_render.py:45, written :68Candidate predict_image().delta_de_heatmap.pngpreprocessing_render.py:46, written :72Signed candidate − baseline dE heatmap.report.jsonREPORT_FILENAME preprocessing_render.py:43, written :76{"case_id": ..., **asdict(metrics)} (:121).
The heatmap (_save_delta_de_heatmap, preprocessing_render.py:89) is signed: it normalises delta = candidate − baseline by its peak absolute value, then puts positive delta (candidate worse) in the red channel and negative delta (candidate better) in the green channel (preprocessing_render.py:94, :110-111). Mismatched shapes are defensively cropped to the smaller grid (:97-103), though they are expected to match.
report.json’s schema is locked to the EvaluationMetrics dataclass via asdict (preprocessing_render.py:121); the drift-regression test in tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_metrics.py guards it.
How to drive it
From the CLI
Prisma/generator/preprocessing_eval_cli.py is a thin wrapper that loads two images, builds a shared SolveConfig, calls evaluate_pair, and prints the report to stdout (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:97). Artifacts are opt-in via --out-dir (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:72).
python preprocessing_eval_cli.py \
    --case-id my_case \
    --baseline baseline.png \
    --candidate candidate.png \
    --profiles Prisma/data/filaments/profiles \
    --palette bambu-basic-cyan bambu-basic-yellow \
    --white-base panchroma-matte-cotton-white \
    --out-dir /tmp/eval_out

Required flags: --case-id, --baseline, --candidate, --profiles, --palette (one or more filament IDs), --white-base (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:61-71). Images are EXIF-transposed and forced to RGB uint8 on load (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:85). --solver-preset accepts full only (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:49, :75).
From Python
from evaluation import EvaluationInput, evaluate_pair  # evaluation/__init__.py:3
 
result = evaluate_pair(EvaluationInput(
    case_id="my_case",
    baseline_image=baseline_u8,   # np.ndarray HxWx3 uint8
    candidate_image=candidate_u8,
    solve_config=cfg,             # facade.SolveConfig
    out_dir=None,                 # set a Path to also write artifacts
))
print(result.metrics.delta_mean_de)
The package re-exports the full surface (Prisma/generator/evaluation/__init__.py:15): evaluate_pair, the three dataclasses, EvaluationRunError, and the two metric primitives.
The bakeoff runner script
scripts/evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py is the F4 MVT batch runner that sweeps the landed first-wave preprocessing operators across a small real-photo corpus. Its run_bakeoff (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:281) loops a 5-photo corpus (_CORPUS, :84) × the operator set A1/B1/B3/C1/C2 (_OPERATORS, :95). For each cell it:

Applies the operator offline to the source raster via _offline_apply (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:189) to produce the candidate — both arms then solve with an empty preprocessing slot (:144). This sidesteps the single-module_state constraint of the harness while still exercising each operator’s real kernel (:5-8).
Calls evaluate_pair with a per-case out_dir (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:315).
Assigns a coarse _verdict label — promising / neutral / harmful / needs_tuning (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:219) — by diffing the metrics itself (the bundle only ships the dE delta precomputed).

It writes runs/<image>__<op>/... per-case artifacts plus summary.json and summary.csv (_write_summary, evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:379). Key flags: --out-dir (required), --max-edge-px (default 256, :441), --palette, --white-base, --cleanup-enabled/--no-cleanup-enabled (:458-470), and --solver-backend (default dual_resolution; use joint_lut to expose raw per-pixel speckle for the small-component metric, :471-487).
Two sibling runner scripts reuse the harness internals (_compute_metrics + render_evaluation_artifacts, not the evaluate_pair entry point) for narrower studies: scripts/evaluate_b1_b3_preservation.py and scripts/evaluate_b1_parameter_sweep.py.
Liveness
All symbols below are wired and exercised as of 2026-06-21:

evaluate_pair / harness package — imported by preprocessing_eval_cli.py:42, the evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py runner (:59), the package re-export evaluation/__init__.py:3, and tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_harness.py. The two evaluate_b1_* sibling scripts do not call evaluate_pair; they import the harness internals _compute_metrics + render_evaluation_artifacts directly. Live.
render_evaluation_artifacts — called by evaluate_pair under the out_dir branch (preprocessing_harness.py:139-141); exercised end-to-end by tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_harness.py (the out_dir write-out test) and imported directly by both evaluate_b1_* sibling scripts. Live.
count_small_components / cap_total_variation — called from _compute_metrics (preprocessing_harness.py:203, :213), re-exported (evaluation/__init__.py:10), and tested in tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_metrics.py. Live.
Bakeoff runner scripts — evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py, evaluate_b1_b3_preservation.py, evaluate_b1_parameter_sweep.py are standalone scripts/ entry points (run by hand, not imported by the app). They are research tooling, not part of the webapp request path; their last edits date to 2026-04-22..06-13. Live as CLIs, unconfirmed whether re-run recently.

Caveats

Production solve path. Both arms go through solve_full → run_pipeline / FULL_PRESET (facade.py:975) — the staged backend, the same engine the webapp uses. The metrics reflect production solver behaviour, including grouping/cleanup, not the legacy solve.py CLI engine.
Shapes must match. Metrics assume baseline and candidate solved to the same grid (same config, same image dimensions). The heatmap renderer crops defensively (preprocessing_render.py:97) but the dE mean/p95 do not align grids — feed same-sized images.
Cap-TV is grid-space. cap_total_variation is a raw grid sum (preprocessing_metrics.py:82); it is only comparable between two solves at the same resolution. Do not compare TV across differing solver_fine_pitch_mm.

Related

generator.facade — SolveConfig, SolveResult, solve_full
The staged solve backend — what run_pipeline / FULL_PRESET actually does
Preprocessing operators — the A/B/C operator kernels the bakeoff sweeps
Delta E and the gamut mask — what de_map and gamut_mask mean
generator.thickness_maps — MapKey, ThicknessMaps, the __-prefixed diagnostic keys

using/command-line-entry-points-and-fila.content:
Command-line entry points and filament availability

In one sentence: the generator ships two command-line scripts — a legacy batch solver (pipeline_cli.py, not the web-app path) and a preprocessing A/B harness (preprocessing_eval_cli.py) — and one of pipeline_cli.py’s files quietly hosts the image-loader and palette-validator that the live server still imports, gated by an exclude_from_model generation-availability policy.

This page serves two readers: the user who wants to drive a CLI, and the developer who has forgotten which parts of pipeline_cli.py are dead and which are load-bearing. The short version: the CLI’s run() solve engine is legacy and unused by the product, but several helper functions defined in the same file are imported by the live server.
Related: How a Solve Works · The Joint LUT and Staged Solve · generator.facade · generator.filament_policy · generator.evaluation.preprocessing_harness

The two scripts at a glance























Scriptprog nameWhat it doesLive as a CLI?generator/pipeline_cli.pylith_pipelineLegacy batch solve → diagnostic PNGs (no mesh)Runs, but legacy — not the product solve pathgenerator/preprocessing_eval_cli.pypreprocessing_eval_cliSolve two images under one config, print A/B metricsYes — dev/evaluation harness
A third entry point lives in palette/suggest.py (main() at palette/suggest.py:1907, prog="lith_palette" at palette/suggest.py:1912) — the palette-suggestion dev CLI — but it is outside this page’s scope.

pipeline_cli.py — legacy batch solver
Driving it
python pipeline_cli.py photo.jpg bambu-basic-cyan bambu-basic-magenta bambu-basic-yellow --out Prisma/output/lithophanes
python pipeline_cli.py photo.jpg --palette-file palette.json --out my_print
python pipeline_cli.py --list-filaments
main() (pipeline_cli.py:916) parses args, resolves the palette (positional IDs or --palette-file JSON, pipeline_cli.py:934), auto-loads pair corrections from data/filaments/pair_corrections.json unless --no-corrections (pipeline_cli.py:944), calls run(...), then prints a per-filament usage table via print_summary() (pipeline_cli.py:991). --list-filaments (pipeline_cli.py:920) just lists every spline profile on disk with its registry display name and exits.

Header warning. The module docstring (pipeline_cli.py:1) calls the file lith_pipeline.py and shows from lith_pipeline import run — that filename no longer exists. Trust the line anchors below, not the header.

run() is legacy and unwired
run() (pipeline_cli.py:402) is a self-contained “6-step” solve engine: validate palette → load image → load spline profiles → build joint LUTs → solve (per-pixel or SLIC-superpixel) → save diagnostic PNGs (de_map.png, predicted.png, source.png, cap_height.png, etc.). It explicitly does not export a mesh — the final step prints “Mesh export is handled by the post-solve exporter” (pipeline_cli.py:787).
This engine is not the web app. The product solve runs the staged backend — run_staged_backend_path (pipeline/staged_runner.py:10310), invoked from pipeline/runner.py:846. Grep confirms no product module imports run: it is reachable only from pipeline_cli.main(). The in-repo legacy audit reaches the same verdict — “pipeline_cli.run(...) is not part of the live webapp solve path” (generator/docs/legacy_audit/03_LEGACY_PIPELINE_CLI_SOLVE_PATH.md:106), classing both run(...) and its segment_image(...) helper as dead_or_legacy_cli_only (lines 164-165). See generator.pipeline.staged_runner for the path that is live.
Silently-ignored legacy parameters
run()’s signature carries four deprecated parameters kept only for call-site compatibility (pipeline_cli.py:436):






























ParameterCLI flagBehaviourdark_filament--dark-filament (argparse.SUPPRESS)Ignored; prints a one-line deprecation note when verbose (pipeline_cli.py:492) — “joint LUT handles luminance”tone_map--no-tone-map (argparse.SUPPRESS)Accepted, never readtone_map_gamma--gamma (argparse.SUPPRESS)Accepted, never readpixel_size_mm—Aliased onto image_sample_pitch_mm when the pitch is still default (pipeline_cli.py:495); otherwise inert
The three suppressed flags are hidden from --help (pipeline_cli.py:877). Of the four, only dark_filament produces visible output, and only as a warning.
What in this file the live server actually uses
The same pipeline_cli.py file hosts a handful of helpers that the product imports — this is the trap. They live in a CLI file but are not legacy. server.py:65 imports exactly two of them:
from pipeline_cli import (
    load_image,
    apply_adjustments,
)



































HelperDefinedLive caller(s)Roleload_imagepipeline_cli.py:61server.py:825 (in _load_run_source_image), palette/suggest.py:403sRGB load + EXIF transpose + frame crop/rotate/flip + resize to print resolutionapply_adjustmentspipeline_cli.py:199server.py:832 (only call site)non-destructive exposure/contrast/saturation/tint/highlight/shadow/temperature on the loaded rastervalidate_palettepipeline_cli.py:338pipeline/runner.py:654, and run() itself (pipeline_cli.py:508)profile-present + not-excluded gate for a new solveload_filament_registrypipeline_cli.py:330grouping/beam_search.py:46, grouping/greedy_optimize.py:30read data/filaments/registry.json (→ {} if absent)
So in the product: server.py’s shared loader _load_run_source_image (server.py:822) calls load_image then apply_adjustments, and the live solve calls validate_palette from pipeline/runner.py:654 (the staged path’s “Fixed spine: Load” step). The legacy audit confirms all four as live (generator/docs/legacy_audit/03_LEGACY_PIPELINE_CLI_SOLVE_PATH.md:159-163); their eventual rehoming out of a CLI file is a noted cleanup, not done yet.

For developers: do not assume “it’s in pipeline_cli.py, so it’s dead.” run()/segment_image()/main() are legacy; load_image/apply_adjustments/validate_palette/load_filament_registry are live product surface. See Pipeline Map for where they sit.


preprocessing_eval_cli.py — the A/B harness
Driving it
python preprocessing_eval_cli.py \
    --case-id my_case \
    --baseline baseline.png \
    --candidate candidate.png \
    --profiles Prisma/data/filaments/profiles \
    --palette bambu-basic-cyan bambu-basic-yellow \
    --white-base panchroma-matte-cotton-white \
    --out-dir /tmp/eval_out
This is a thin wrapper (main(), preprocessing_eval_cli.py:97). It loads two images, builds one shared SolveConfig from --palette / --white-base / --profiles (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:89), calls evaluate_pair (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:114), and prints the metric bundle as JSON. Artifact writes (predicted PNGs, delta-dE heatmap, report.json) are opt-in via --out-dir (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:72). --solver-preset accepts only "full" (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:49).
How it works (and why it’s not the legacy engine)
The CLI delegates to evaluate_pair (evaluation/preprocessing_harness.py:105), part of generator.evaluation.preprocessing_harness. Because it builds a real SolveConfig, each arm solves through the live facade/staged path, not pipeline_cli.run() — so the two scripts share a name space (“CLI”) but exercise different engines. evaluate_pair is live and tested (tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_harness.py) and is also driven by scripts/evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:315. The CLI module itself is a leaf — nothing imports preprocessing_eval_cli (only the harness it wraps is imported elsewhere).

Note the metrics reported are A4 primitives — dE, out-of-gamut, small-component, cap total-variation — per the CLI’s own description (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:58). Its own header cites a planning doc (F4_PHASE.md) — verify behaviour against the line anchors, not the prose.


Filament generation-availability policy (exclude_from_model)
Both the CLIs and the web app share one gate on which filaments may enter new work, defined in generator.filament_policy (filament_policy.py).
The rule
A filament flagged exclude_from_model: true in data/filaments/registry.json is treated as unavailable for new generation (filament_policy.py:1). The flag is originally a calibration model-fit policy field, but the generator reuses it as a stop-gap until a dedicated generation_availability field exists. The contract: an excluded filament must not silently enter a new solve, palette validation, or palette suggestion just because a stale profile file still sits on disk — but existing saved palettes/runs are preserved; only NEW work is gated (filament_policy.py:9).
The three functions and who calls them





























FunctionDefinedReturnsLive callersis_generation_available(fid, registry)filament_policy.py:35False iff flaggedbase predicate for the other twounavailable_for_generation(ids, registry)filament_policy.py:48excluded subset, ordered + de-dupedpipeline_cli.validate_palette (pipeline_cli.py:360), server.py:3501 (palette pre-check endpoint), server.py:3767 (suggestion white-base/cap refusal)excluded_filament_ids(registry)filament_policy.py:40set of all excluded idsserver.py:3886 + palette/suggest.py:1939 (passed as exclude_filament_ids to the suggester so candidates are filtered up front)
Where the gate fires

Palette pre-check (UI): POST /api/palette/validate (server.py:3488) returns missing (no profile on disk) and unavailable (excluded) separately. This is advisory; the solve re-validates.
Solve / suggestion validation: validate_palette (pipeline_cli.py:338) raises plain ValueError for a missing profile, and raises FilamentUnavailableError (filament_policy.py:18) for an excluded one. That error subclasses ValueError so existing except ValueError handlers still catch it, while callers that care can distinguish a policy refusal from a missing-profile error (pipeline_cli.py:343, filament_policy.py:22).
Suggestion: an excluded white base/cap is a hard 400 up front (server.py:3768), because the suggester cannot drop a fixed white the way it drops colour candidates; excluded colour candidates are filtered via excluded_filament_ids before search.

See Model-domain ingress and generator.model for why a profile’s existence on disk is not sufficient to trust it.
Disambiguation — two different excluded_filament_ids
There are two unrelated functions with this name; do not confuse them:

























GeneratorCalibration / fittingModulegenerator/filament_policy.py:40calibration/fitting/filament_exclusions.py:19Inputa registry dicta store object (calls store.list_filaments())Purposegate new generation workdrop a filament from every production fit
Both read the same underlying exclude_from_model field, but they operate on different inputs and serve different halves of the product (generation vs. model fitting). When working in the generator, the registry-dict version is the relevant one.

Quick reference — file/line anchors





















































ClaimAnchorLegacy solve enginepipeline_cli.py:402 (run)run() does no mesh exportpipeline_cli.py:787Silently-ignored legacy paramspipeline_cli.py:436Suppressed legacy flagspipeline_cli.py:877Live solve path (not this CLI)pipeline/staged_runner.py:10310, pipeline/runner.py:846Server imports from this fileserver.py:65 (only load_image, apply_adjustments)Shared loader uses bothserver.py:822 (_load_run_source_image)validate_palette live callpipeline/runner.py:654A/B harness CLIpreprocessing_eval_cli.py:97 (main)Policy contractfilament_policy.py:1, :35, :48, :40Policy error typefilament_policy.py:18 (FilamentUnavailableError)

using/driving-the-generator.title: Driving the Generator
using/driving-the-generator.content:
Driving the Generator

In one sentence: the generator web app (port 8010) is a four-step wizard backed by a FastAPI server that runs every long job — solve, palette suggest, palette compare, export — in a background thread on a single module-level session dict, which the browser drives by start-then-poll and which makes the whole app strictly single-user, one-job-at-a-time.

This page serves two readers: the user who wants to drive the app end to end (pick an image, build a palette, solve, review, compare, export), and the developer who has forgotten the backend’s job model — how a click becomes a background thread, how progress reaches the screen, and why two browser tabs will fight each other. It stays at endpoint-contract altitude; for what happens inside a solve see How a Solve Works and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve.
Related: How a Solve Works · Pipeline Map · Exporting Print Files · Settings, resolution, and the config contract · Command-line entry points and filament availability · generator.facade · generator.filament_policy

Starting the app
cd Prisma/generator
uvicorn server:app --reload --port 8010
server.py builds one FastAPI instance (server.py:333) titled “Prisma — Lithophane Generator API”, wide-open CORS for development (server.py:340), and — as the last mount so it doesn’t shadow the API — serves the single-page app from generator/app/ with html=True so / resolves to index.html (server.py:6276). All JSON routes live under /api/...; everything else is the static frontend (app.js, style.css, data.js).

Header trap. The module docstring at the top of server.py cites the wrong directory and port. The real home is Prisma/generator and the real port is 8010 — trust the run command above and the line anchors below, not the header.


The wizard at a glance
The frontend is a four-step bar (index.html:64-77): 1 Image → 2 Palette → 3 Preview → 4 Export. The steps map to backend route families like this:






























Step (UI label)What you doPrimary endpoint(s)1 ImagePick / upload a source imageGET /api/images, POST /api/images/upload2 PaletteAuto-suggest, compare, or hand-build a palettePOST /api/palette/suggest, POST /api/palette/compare, POST /api/gamut-preview, POST /api/palette/validate3 PreviewKick off the full solve and review the resultPOST /api/solve/start, GET /api/solve/status4 ExportGenerate STL/3MF print files + AMS swap planPOST /api/export/files/start, GET /api/export/swap-instructions
A persistent Palette Deck and Active Library live in the left rail (index.html:24, :34) and are settings/state, not part of the linear flow.

The job model (read this if you are the developer)
One global session, one process
All mutable app state is a single module-level dict, session (server.py:474), created once at import. It holds the live config, the current solve slot, an in-RAM solve_cache keyed by card_id, and one slot each for compare, suggest, and export. Each long-running slot is a small state machine on a status string: idle | running | complete | error | cancelled (e.g. server.py:477).
Because this state is process-global and not keyed by user or browser session, the app is single-user by construction. Two tabs share the same session; a solve started in one tab is visible (and cancellable) from the other, and GET /api/session (server.py:2634) returns the same config and solve status to everyone.
Start, then poll
No endpoint blocks for the duration of a long job. The pattern is always: a POST .../start validates inputs, sets the slot’s status to "running" synchronously before returning (so an immediately-following request sees the job as active), spawns a daemon threading.Thread, and returns {"job_id": ..., "status": "running"}. The browser then polls a matching GET .../status on an interval until status leaves "running".








































JobStartStatus pollCancelBrowser poll cadenceSolvePOST /api/solve/start (server.py:4653)GET /api/solve/status (server.py:5383)POST /api/solve/cancel (server.py:5397)500 ms (app.js:10153)SuggestPOST /api/palette/suggest (server.py:3746)GET /api/palette/suggest/status (server.py:3942)POST /api/palette/suggest/cancel (server.py:3956)1000 ms (app.js:4031)ComparePOST /api/palette/compare (server.py:4044)GET /api/palette/compare/status (server.py:4382)(none — cooperative cancel flag only)500 ms (app.js:3601)ExportPOST /api/export/files/start (server.py:5666)GET /api/export/files/status (server.py:5745)POST /api/export/files/cancel (server.py:5764)500 ms (app.js:10493)
Each /status route reads the slot and returns status, a progress string (the current stage_label), a richer progress_detail dict, elapsed_s, and — once finished — the result payload (e.g. server.py:5383-5394). The status endpoint is a pure read; it never advances the job.
One job at a time
Each start endpoint refuses to run on top of itself with HTTP 409: solve guards on if session["solve"]["status"] == "running" (server.py:4656), and suggest/compare/export do the same on their own slots (server.py:3758, :4058, :5670). There is no global “only one of any kind” lock at start time, but the cache-management and run-load endpoints call _assert_no_active_job() (server.py:5926), which raises 409 if any of solve/export/compare is running — so you cannot, for example, clear the cache or load a saved run mid-solve.
Internally each background worker grabs a module-level lock (_solve_lock, _compare_lock, _suggest_lock, server.py:521-523) for the body of its run, so the heavy numeric work is serialised even if the 409 guard were bypassed.
Cancellation is cooperative
Cancel endpoints don’t kill the thread — they set a cancel_requested flag on the slot (server.py:5403). The worker’s progress callback checks that flag and raises a sentinel (SolveCancelled / ExportCancelled) on the next progress tick, which the worker catches and turns into status = "cancelled" (e.g. server.py:5364). So a cancel only lands at the next progress checkpoint, not instantly. Compare has a cancel_requested flag honoured in its progress callback (server.py:4086) but, as of this code, no dedicated cancel route.

Step 1 — Picking an image
GET /api/images (server.py:2554) lists files in the images dir filtered to a fixed extension allow-list — .png .jpg .jpeg .tif .tiff .bmp .webp (server.py:2551). POST /api/images/upload (server.py:2566) accepts a multipart upload, rejects unsupported suffixes with 400, sanitises the filename to its basename (path-traversal guard), auto-suffixes _1, _2, … to avoid overwriting, then re-opens the saved file with Pillow to confirm it is a real image (deleting it and returning 400 if not). GET /api/images/preview/{filename} (server.py:2610) streams an EXIF-transposed, max-800px JPEG thumbnail for the gallery.
Selecting an image writes image_path into the session config (via the config endpoints — see Settings, resolution, and the config contract); the solve later resolves it against the images dir and 404s if it has gone missing (server.py:4666-4668).

Step 2 — Building a palette
There are three ways to arrive at a palette, plus a cheap validity pre-check. All of them respect the exclude_from_model generation-availability gate documented in Command-line entry points and filament availability and generator.filament_policy.
Validate (instant, advisory)
POST /api/palette/validate (server.py:3487) is a synchronous pre-check: it returns missing (no spline profile on disk) and unavailable (flagged exclude_from_model) as separate lists, plus a combined valid boolean (server.py:3502). It is advisory only — the solve path re-validates regardless.
Gamut preview (synchronous, one palette)
POST /api/gamut-preview (server.py:3972) is the one palette operation that runs inline rather than as a background job. It accepts an optional palette override so the UI can probe a non-active deck palette without mutating the session (server.py:3972-3979), runs a preview-quality solve, and returns coverage %, out-of-gamut count, mean/max dE, and URLs to freshly-baked preview PNGs (dE map, gamut overlay, source, predicted) with a cache-busting ?t= suffix (server.py:4013-4027).
Auto-suggest (background job)
POST /api/palette/suggest (server.py:3746) launches the suggester in a thread. Suggestion is always thorough now — the old fast/quality switch was removed, and unknown legacy fields are rejected loudly with 422 (server.py:3511-3515). Two modes:

Plain top-K (max_swaps unset): returns the best top_k palettes of n_filaments colours.
Swap-aware tiers (max_swaps set): sweeps AMS swap tiers honouring ams_slots, n_ams_units, and reserved white_slots from config (server.py:3891-3908).

Before any model loads, the endpoint hard-rejects (400) if the configured white base/cap is itself excluded from generation, because the suggester can drop colour candidates but not the fixed whites (server.py:3766-3774). Excluded colour candidates are filtered up front via excluded_filament_ids (server.py:3886). Poll GET /api/palette/suggest/status (1000 ms) for progress and the final candidate/tier list.
Compare (background job, N palettes side by side)
POST /api/palette/compare (server.py:4044) takes a list of palettes and solves each at preview quality via solve_compare (server.py:4094, defined facade.py:992), then writes per-palette diagnostic PNGs (compare_<idx>_predicted.png, cap maps, surface maps) into the shared run-cache dir. A palette that errors comes back as an {"error": ...} entry rather than failing the whole batch (facade.py:1031). Poll GET /api/palette/compare/status (500 ms). This is how you A/B several candidate palettes before committing one to the full solve.

Preview ≠ full. Suggest and compare use the COMPARE_PRESET / preview path; the Step-3 solve uses the FULL_PRESET path. Numbers from compare are directional, not the final solve’s metrics.


Step 3 — Solving
Kicking it off
POST /api/solve/start (server.py:4653) validates that an image and a palette exist (the palette can be overridden in the body, else it comes from config; server.py:4662), snapshots the config so mid-solve setting changes can’t perturb the running thread (server.py:4671), mints an 8-char job_id, sets solve.status = "running" synchronously, and spawns the worker. The body may carry a card_id (for per-run caching), a profile_ref / recipe_snapshot (provenance recorded into the run metadata), and a palette override (SolveStartPayload, server.py:4398).
What the worker actually runs
The worker (_run_solve, server.py:4688) resets the solve slot, loads the source image through the shared loader, then calls solve_full(...) (server.py:4740, defined facade.py:967).

The product solve is the staged backend, not the CLI engine. solve_full → run_pipeline (facade.py:988) → run_staged_backend_path (pipeline/runner.py:846, defined pipeline/staged_runner.py:10310). It does not use pipeline_cli.run()’s legacy “6-step” engine — that engine is unwired from the product (see Command-line entry points and filament availability and Pipeline Map).

Progress detail
Inside the worker, a _progress(msg) closure (server.py:4732) both checks the cancel flag and writes the latest stage into solve["progress"] — accepting either a bare string or a dict carrying stage_label/stage_pct. That dict is exactly what GET /api/solve/status surfaces as progress_detail, so the UI’s progress bar is driven by whatever the staged backend reports. On completion the worker logs a one-line SOLVE_PHASE_TIMINGS JSON of coarse phase durations (server.py:5352).
What lands when it finishes
On success the worker writes a large pile of diagnostic artifacts into the run-cache dir (predicted/source/reference PNGs, dE maps, per-filament thickness maps, white-cap and colour-ceiling/total-surface maps, contour blobs, recipe-breakdown artifacts), then assembles a JSON-safe solve["result"] dict of metrics plus /api/run-cache/files/... URLs (built from server.py:5148). The headline metrics include mean_de, source_rms_de, max_de, coverage_pct, out-of-gamut count, image dimensions, and max_height. Every URL carries a cache-bust query (?run=<card>&t=<epoch>, server.py:5007) so the browser fetches fresh images for each run. The worker also records a solve_owned_fingerprint (server.py:5344) — a hash of the solve-coupled settings — which export later checks for staleness.
Reviewing the result
The frontend reads solve["result"] from the status poll and renders the predicted render, the dE heatmaps, the per-filament thickness maps, the colour-ceiling / total-surface views, and the recipe breakdown (which colours compose which regions — the Color Ceiling / Recipe Viewer sub-tab). The blocky look of the predicted render is intentional: it honours the true solve resolution and never fakes smoothness the print won’t have. Binary .bin blobs of the thickness/surface fields are served alongside the PNGs for the interactive viewers.
Auto-archiving
If the solve carried a card_id, on completion the worker writes a completed-solve cache entry and then _maybe_write_auto_run(...) (server.py:5357, defined :6059) silently packs the run into the auto-runs archive tier (labelled Auto <timestamp>). This is best-effort — failures are logged and swallowed, never failing the solve.

Step 4 — Exporting print files
The full mesh + serialization details live in Exporting Print Files; this is the driver’s view.
Two export entry points
POST /api/export/files (server.py:5651) runs the export synchronously and is retained for direct API callers and tests. The UI uses the background variant POST /api/export/files/start (server.py:5666), which threads the same _perform_export_files worker with a progress callback, then polled via GET /api/export/files/status (500 ms) and cancellable via POST /api/export/files/cancel.
What export needs from the solve
_perform_export_files (server.py:5432) refuses with 400 if there is no complete solve to export, and — when exporting the current solve (no explicit card_id) — refuses with 409 if the solve is stale: it recomputes _solve_owned_fingerprint(cfg) and rejects if it differs from the fingerprint captured at solve time, telling you to re-solve first (server.py:5443-5450). Export options come from ExportFilesPayload (server.py:742): geometry_source (default field_derived), field_scale (one of 2/4/8/16, default 4), and output_format (stls or 3mf, default 3mf).
Swap instructions and downloading
GET /api/export/swap-instructions (server.py:5774) returns the AMS swap plan — grouped filament bands with z-ranges and slot assignments, human-readable instructions, and OrcaSlicer pause G-code (server.py:5848). It reads the currently selected AMS capacity (ams_slots/white_slots) rather than whatever was active at solve time, since AMS capacity is export-time printer state (server.py:5797-5802). Generated files are downloaded as a zip via GET /api/export/files-zip (server.py:5855), or served individually under GET /api/export/files/{path} (server.py:5897). Run-cache diagnostics are served by GET /api/run-cache/files/{path} (server.py:5912); both use _safe_path to reject traversal.

Saving, loading, and comparing runs
Beyond the per-job state there is a small archive layer (Stage 9b) for keeping runs around:













































ActionEndpointNotesSave current runPOST /api/runs/save (server.py:6073)packs the cached solve into the user-curated saved tierList runsGET /api/runs/saved (server.py:6086)merges saved + auto tiers, newest first, each tagged tierDownloadGET /api/runs/saved/{id}/download, .../auto/{id}/download (server.py:6095, :6106)streams the run zipPromote auto → savedPOST /api/runs/auto/{id}/promote (server.py:6117)guarded by _assert_no_active_job()Rename / deletePOST .../rename, DELETE .../{id} (server.py:6127, :6135)delete returns 409 if the file is lockedLoad by idPOST /api/runs/load (server.py:6242)tier is "saved" or "auto"; both rehydrate via the same pathLoad from uploadPOST /api/runs/load-upload (server.py:6256)multipart zip, size-capped before the full read
Loading rehydrates the archive into a fresh card_id, restores the whole run-cache subtree to disk, rewrites every ?run= URL to the new card, and installs a complete entry into session["solve_cache"] (_rehydrate_loaded_archive, server.py:6176) — so a loaded run behaves like a just-finished solve for review and re-export. Both load routes are gated by _assert_no_active_job() so you cannot load over a running job.
Caches you can clear
POST /api/cache/clear-runs (server.py:5933) sweeps the run-cache and auto-run archives plus the in-RAM solve_cache, keeping LUTs, output, and user-curated saved runs. POST /api/cache/clear-all (server.py:5950) additionally drops the LUT cache. Both first call _assert_no_active_job().

Single-user caveats (what will bite you)

Two browser tabs share one backend. The session dict is process-global (server.py:474); there is no per-client isolation. A second tab sees and can cancel the first tab’s solve.
One job per kind at a time. Starting solve/suggest/compare/export over a running one of the same kind returns 409 (server.py:4656, :3758, :4058, :5670). Cache-clear and run-load return 409 if any of solve/export/compare is running (server.py:5926).
Cancellation is deferred, landing only at the next progress checkpoint (server.py:4733-4734).
Mid-solve setting changes are ignored for the running solve — config is snapshotted at start (server.py:4671) — but they will make the result stale, and export/swap-instructions will 409 until you re-solve (server.py:5443).
Not a production server. Single process, daemon threads, in-RAM state lost on restart, CORS wide open (server.py:340). Restarting uvicorn drops all session state (saved-run archives on disk survive).


Quick reference — file/line anchors

























































































ClaimAnchorFastAPI app + wide CORSserver.py:333, :340SPA served last from app/server.py:6276Global session dict + status enumserver.py:474, :477Per-kind background locksserver.py:521-523Solve start (snapshot, 409, thread)server.py:4653, :4656, :4671Solve worker → solve_full → staged backendserver.py:4740, facade.py:988, pipeline/runner.py:846Solve result payload assemblyserver.py:5148Solve status / cancelserver.py:5383, :5397Suggest (always thorough)server.py:3746, :3758Compare (preview, per-palette PNGs)server.py:4044, :4094Gamut preview (synchronous)server.py:3972Palette validate (advisory)server.py:3487Export start / status / cancelserver.py:5666, :5745, :5764Export staleness 409server.py:5443Swap instructionsserver.py:5774_assert_no_active_jobserver.py:5926Auto-run archive on completionserver.py:5357, :6059Run load rehydrationserver.py:6242, :6176Browser poll cadencesapp.js:10153, :4031, :3601, :10493Wizard step barindex.html:64-77
